STUDYQURAN:2:228/r10.anchor: for others, it means that women have a right to sexual relations similar to that of men (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r11.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās said he beautified himself for his wife as she beautified herself for him.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r11.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās said, “I beautify myself for my wife, just

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r12.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r12.claim: Another reading frames mutual rights as protection from harm: husbands should not trap wives in repeated divorce and reconciliation, and wives should not hide a pregnancy.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r12.anchor: For others, it is a question of mutual protection from harm, where the man does not harm the wife through an endless cycle of divorce and reconciliation

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r13.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r13.claim: Others see marriage as shared closeness, love, and peace; al-Rāzī adds that a woman's share may be greater.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r13.anchor: Others mention that the point of marriage is closeness, love, and peace, which should be shared between husband and wife

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r14.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r14.claim: Al-Rāzī says one could argue that the woman's share in marriage is more abundant.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r14.anchor: al-Rāzī says, “One might even say that [in this] the share

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r15.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r15.claim: Many commentators understand men's degree as noblesse oblige, a responsibility to exercise their advantage for women's benefit.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r15.anchor: many commentators understand a kindof noblesse oblige

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r16.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the degree as men's promoting good relations and generosity in wealth and virtuous conduct; greater power requires self-restraint.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r16.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said, “This degree is a

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r17.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r17.claim: Others connect men's degree with economic advantage, obligations, and the ability to fight in God's way, while noting some female Companions fought too.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r17.anchor: Others state that this degree over them consists of men’s economic advantages and also obligations and their ability to fight in the way of God (although some female Companions of the Prophet did participate in fighting)

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r18.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r18.claim: Others attribute men's degree to traits such as strength and intelligence.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r18.anchor: or refers to qualities such as strength and intelligence (Q)

STUDYQURAN:2:228/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r19.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r19.claim: Spiritually, the soul has rights owed to it and rights it owes; the spirit governs the soul, yet spiritual progress occurs through it, so it should be treated gently and allowed rest.
STUDYQURAN:2:228/r19.anchor: Interpreted spiritually, this verse can mean that the soul

TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r1.claim: The verse addresses women divorced after their husbands have consummated the marriage, if they menstruate, and requires them to wait three qurūʾ before marrying again.
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r1.anchor: والمطلقات اللواتي طلقن بعد ابتناء أزواجهن بهن، وإفضائهم إليهن إذا كن ذوات حيض، وطهر، يتربصن بأنفسهن عن نكاح الأزواج ثلاثة قروء

TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets the three qurūʾ as three menstrual periods.
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} [البقرة: 228] قال: حيض "

TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ explains the count as three menstrual periods, which the woman completes as her waiting period.
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r3.anchor: عن الربيع: " {ثلاثة قروء} [البقرة: 228] أي ثلاث حيض. يقول: تعتد ثلاث حيض

TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r4.claim: Qatada says qurūʾ are menstruations and states that the rule is excluded for a woman divorced before intercourse, a postmenopausal woman, one who has not menstruated, and a pregnant woman.
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r4.anchor: سمعت قتادة، في قوله: " {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} [البقرة: 228] يقول: جعل عدة المطلقات ثلاث حيض

TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak also interprets qurūʾ as menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r5.anchor: عن جويبر، عن الضحاك، قال: " القروء: الحيض "

TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the waiting period consists of three menstruations.
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} [البقرة: 228] قال: ثلاث حيض

TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r7.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r7.claim: Amr ibn Dinar says the Prophet's Companions understood qurūʾ to mean menstruations.
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r7.anchor: قال: ثنا ابن جريج، قال: قال عمرو بن دينار: «الأقراء الحيض عن أصحاب النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم»

TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r8.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r8.claim: Ikrima says qurūʾ means menstruations, not purity, and argues that the command is to divorce women for their prescribed waiting period, not for their qurūʾ.
TAB-FULL:v4p87#2/r8.anchor: سمع عكرمة، قال: " الأقراء: الحيض، وليس بالطهر

TAB-FULL:v4p90/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r1.claim: Al-Suddi interprets three qurūʾ as three menstrual periods.
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r1.anchor: عن السدي: " {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} [البقرة: 228] أما ثلاثة قروء: فثلاث حيض "

TAB-FULL:v4p90/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود وعمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud says a husband retains the right to take his wife back until she washes after the third menstruation; Umar agrees and applies that view.
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي، أنه رفع إلى عمر، فقال لعبد الله بن مسعود: لتقولن فيها

TAB-FULL:v4p90/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r3.claim: Umar accepts Ibn Masʿud's opinion that the husband retains his right until the wife washes after the third menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r3.anchor: قال: ذاك رأيي وافقت ما في نفسي فقضى بذلك عمر

TAB-FULL:v4p90/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r4.speaker: الحسن وأبو موسى الأشعري
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r4.claim: In al-Hasan's report, a husband claimed to have returned his wife as she prepared to wash after her third period; Abu Musa had her swear she had not yet washed and restored her to him.

TAB-FULL:v4p90/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r5.claim: Umar and Ibn Masʿud also say the husband may return her until she has washed, or until prayer becomes permissible to her.
TAB-FULL:v4p90/r5.anchor: عن النخعي، عن قتادة، أن عمر بن الخطاب، قال لابن مسعود، فذكر نحوه

TAB-FULL:v4p92/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r1.speaker: يونس بن جبير وعمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r1.claim: A report says Umar reclaimed his wife as she was about to wash after her third menstruation; ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi said the report's transmitter, Abu Hilal, was unreliable.
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، عن يونس بن جبير: أن عمر بن الخطاب " طلق امرأته، فأرادت أن تغتسل من الحيضة الثالثة

TAB-FULL:v4p92/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن مهدي
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r2.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi rejects the report's reliability, saying Abu Hilal is not a reliable transmitter for it.
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r2.anchor: فذكرت هذا الحديث لعبد الرحمن بن مهدي، فقال: سمعت هذا الحديث من أبي هلال، عن قتادة، وأبو هلال، لا يحتمل هذا

TAB-FULL:v4p92/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وعمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r3.claim: Asked about a woman who had prepared to wash after her third period, Ibn Masʿud said she remained the man's wife until prayer became permissible; Umar agreed.
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r3.anchor: قال عمر، لعبد الله: ما ترى؟ قال: أراها امرأته ما دون أن تحل لها الصلاة. قال عمر: وأنا أرى ذلك

TAB-FULL:v4p92/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r4.claim: Umar and Ibn Masʿud allow return after a reversible divorce until she washes after the third period.
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم، عن الأسود، " أنه قال في رجل طلق امرأته ثم تركها حتى دخلت في الحيضة الثالثة

TAB-FULL:v4p92/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r5.claim: Umar says the husband retains return rights and inheritance between the spouses until she washes after her third menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم، أن عمر بن الخطاب، كان يقول: «إذا طلق الرجل امرأته تطليقة، أو تطليقتين، فهو أحق برجعتها، وبينهما الميراث

TAB-FULL:v4p92/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r6.speaker: الحسن وأبو موسى الأشعري
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r6.claim: Al-Hasan reports that Abu Musa returned a wife to her husband after she declined to swear that she had already washed and become permitted to pray.
TAB-FULL:v4p92/r6.anchor: عن الحسن: " أن رجلا طلق امرأته تطليقة، أو تطليقتين ثم وكل بها بعض أهله، فغفل الإنسان

TAB-FULL:v4p93/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وعمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the husband may return his wife until she washes after the third period, and Umar says this matches his own view and restores her to him.
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: أراه أحق بها ما لم تغتسل، فقال عمر: وافقت الذي في نفسي

TAB-FULL:v4p93/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r2.claim: Ali says the husband retains the right to return until his wife washes after the third menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب: أن عليا، كان يقول: «هو أحق بها ما لم تغتسل من الحيضة الثالثة»

TAB-FULL:v4p93/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says there is no right of return once the menstrual blood stops.
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار، قال: سمعت سعيد بن جبير، يقول: «إذا انقطع الدم فلا رجعة»

TAB-FULL:v4p93/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وأبو موسى الأشعري
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r4.claim: Umar approved Abu Musa's ruling that the husband may return her until she washes, saying he would have rebuked him had he ruled otherwise.
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r4.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب، أن عمر، سأل أبا موسى، عنها، وكان بلغه قضاؤه فيها

TAB-FULL:v4p93/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب وعثمان بن عفان
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r5.claim: Ubay ibn Kaʿb says the husband may return her until she washes after the third period and prayer is permitted; Uthman sought his opinion and followed it.
TAB-FULL:v4p93/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن رفيع، عن أبي عبيدة بن عبد الله، قال: " أرسل عثمان، إلى أبي يسأله عنها

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r1.speaker: أبو قلابة وقتادة وأبو موسى الأشعري
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r1.claim: A report says the husband announced his return as his wife was preparing to wash; after she washed, he disputed with her before Abu Musa, who restored her to him.
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r1.anchor: عن أيوب، عن أبي قلابة، قال: وأخبرنا معمر، عن قتادة، قالا: " راجع رجل امرأته حين وضعت ثيابها تريد الاغتسال

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r2.speaker: معبد الجهني
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r2.claim: Maʿbad al-Juhani says the divorce is final and she may marry another once she has washed her private parts after the third menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن رفيع، عن معبد الجهني، قال: «إذا غسلت المطلقة فرجها من الحيضة الثالثة بانت منه وحلت للأزواج»

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r3.claim: Umar says the husband may return her until she washes after the third period; once she washes, she is permitted to fast.
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، عن حماد، عن إبراهيم: أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: «يحل لزوجها الرجعة عليها حتى تغتسل من الحيضة الثالثة، ويحل لها الصوم»

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r4.claim: Ali says the husband has the right to return his wife until she washes after the third menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r4.anchor: عن سعيد، عن قتادة، عن سعيد بن المسيب، قال: قال علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه: «هو أحق بها ما لم تغتسل من الحيضة الثالثة»

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r5.claim: Other authorities hold that qurūʾ in this verse means periods of purity rather than menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل القرء الذي أمر الله تعالى ذكره المطلقات أن يعتددن به: الطهر

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r6.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r6.claim: Several reports attribute to Aisha the view that qurūʾ means periods of purity, not menstruation.

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r7.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r7.claim: Aisha says a divorced woman is separated from her husband and may marry again upon entering her third menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r7.anchor: عن الزهري، عن عمرة، وعروة، عن عائشة، قالت: «إذا دخلت المطلقة في الحيضة الثالثة فقد بانت من زوجها وحلت للأزواج»

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r8.speaker: عمرة وعائشة
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r8.claim: Al-Zuhri reports Amra's statement that Aisha understood qurʾ as purity, not menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r8.anchor: قال الزهري: قالت عمرة: " كانت عائشة، تقول: " القرء: الطهر، وليس بالحيضة "

TAB-FULL:v4p95/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r9.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن وابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r9.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman and Ibn Umar are reported to share the positions attributed here to Zayd and Aisha.
TAB-FULL:v4p95/r9.anchor: عن الزهري، عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام، مثل قول زيد، وعائشة

TAB-FULL:v4p97/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r1.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says that entering the third menstruation ends the marriage bond and permits her to marry again; al-Zuhri issued fatwas according to this view.
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r1.anchor: عن الزهري، عن سعيد بن المسيب، وسليمان بن يسار، أن زيد بن ثابت قال: «إذا دخلت المطلقة في الحيضة الثالثة فقد بانت من زوجها وحلت للأزواج»

TAB-FULL:v4p97/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r2.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Saʿid reports Aisha's view that qurūʾ means periods of purity.
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r2.anchor: يحيى بن سعيد يقول: بلغني أن عائشة قالت: " إنما الأقراء: الأطهار "

TAB-FULL:v4p97/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وعلي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r3.claim: Zayd says no return is allowed once the third menstruation begins, whereas Ali allows return until she washes after it.
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r3.anchor: عن ابن المسيب: " في رجل طلق امرأته واحدة أو ثنتين، قال: قال زيد بن ثابت: «إذا دخلت في الحيضة الثالثة فلا رجعة له عليها»

TAB-FULL:v4p97/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r4.claim: Zayd says the spouses no longer inherit from one another once she enters her third menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r4.anchor: عن أبي الزناد، عن سليمان بن يسار، عن زيد بن ثابت، قال: «إذا دخلت في الحيضة الثالثة فلا ميراث لها»

TAB-FULL:v4p97/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r5.speaker: زيد بن ثابت ومعاوية بن أبي سفيان وابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r5.claim: In the case of al-Ahwas, Muawiya asked Zayd whether a husband who died while his divorced wife was in her third period left her an inheritance; Zayd said no, and Ibn Umar held the same rule.
TAB-FULL:v4p97/r5.anchor: عن سليمان بن يسار: " أن الأحوص رجل من أشراف أهل الشام طلق امرأته تطليقة، أو ثنتين، فمات وهي في الحيضة الثالثة

TAB-FULL:v4p100/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r1.claim: Ibn Umar says the husband has no right to return her once she enters the third menstruation; she is then separated from him.
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r1.anchor: عن نافع، قال: قال ابن عمر: «إذا دخلت في الحيضة الثالثة فلا رجعة له عليها»

TAB-FULL:v4p100/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r2.speaker: ابن عمر وزيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r2.claim: Ibn Umar and Zayd say that when the third menstrual bleeding begins, neither spouse inherits from the other and the divorce is final.
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر، وزيد بن ثابت، أنهما كانا يقولان: «إذا دخلت المرأة في الدم من الحيضة الثالثة، فإنها لا ترثه، ولا يرثها، وقد برئت منه، وبرئ منها»

TAB-FULL:v4p100/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r3.claim: Zayd says that a woman who begins her third menstruation has no right of return and no inheritance tie with her former husband; Salim and others are also reported to hold this.
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت، قال: «إذا طلقت المرأة، فدخلت في الحيضة الثالثة أنه ليس بينهما ميراث، ولا رجعة»

TAB-FULL:v4p100/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r4.claim: Zayd says the waiting period ends when the divorced woman sees blood in her third menstruation.
TAB-FULL:v4p100/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت، قال: «إذا طلق الرجل امرأته، فرأت الدم في الحيضة الثالثة، فقد انقضت عدتها»

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r1.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r1.claim: Zayd says that if the third menstruation begins before the husband has returned to her, he no longer has the right to do so.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r1.anchor: كان زيد بن ثابت يقول: «إذا حاضت المطلقة الثالثة قبل أن يراجعها زوجها فلا يملك رجعتها»

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r2.speaker: عائشة وزيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r2.claim: Aisha and Zayd say that once a divorced woman enters the third menstruation, her husband no longer has a right of return.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r2.anchor: عن الزهري، عن سعيد بن المسيب، أن عائشة، وزيد بن ثابت، قالا: «إذا دخلت في الحيضة الثالثة فلا رجعة له عليها»

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r3.claim: The Arabic plural of qurʾ is qurūʾ, also aqrāʾ; the verb aqraʾat describes a woman entering the alternating condition of menstruation and purity.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r3.anchor: والقرء في كلام العرب: جمعه قروء، وقد تجمعه العرب أقراء، يقال في أفعل منه: أقرأت المرأة

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r4.claim: Al-Tabari explains the root sense of qurʾ as a fixed time when a regularly recurring thing arrives or departs.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r4.anchor: وأصل القرء في كلام العرب: الوقت لمجيء الشيء المعتاد مجيئه لوقت معلوم، ولإدبار الشيء المعتاد

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r5.claim: Arab usage applies aqraʾ to the approaching due time of a need and to the appointed setting or rising of a star.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r5.anchor: أقرأت حاجة فلان عندي، بمعنى دنا قضاؤها، وجاء وقت قضائها؛ وأقرأ النجم: إذا جاء وقت أفوله

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r6.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r6.claim: The cited line about the Pleiades and the two fish stars illustrates aqraʾ as the star's appointed time of setting.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r6.anchor: إذا ما الثريا وقد أقرأت … أحس السماكان منها أفولا

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r7.speaker: الهذلي
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r7.claim: The Hudhali poet's line uses qāriʾ for the appointed time when the winds blow.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r7.anchor: شنئت العقر عقر بني شليل … إذا هبت لقارئها الرياح

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r8.claim: Some Arabs called the onset of menstruation a qurʾ because menstrual blood appears at its regular time and recedes at another.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r8.anchor: سمى بعض العرب وقت مجيء الحيض قرءا، إذا كان دما يعتاد ظهوره من فرج المرأة في وقت

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r9.claim: The Prophet told Fatima bint Abi Hubays to stop praying during her aqraʾ, understood here as the days when menstruation comes.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r9.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لفاطمة بنت أبي حبيش: «دعي الصلاة أيام أقرائك»

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r10.claim: Other Arabs called the time of purity a qurʾ because menstrual blood recedes then and the expected period of purity begins.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r10.anchor: وسمى آخرون من العرب وقت مجيء الطهر قرءا، إذ كان وقت مجيئه وقتا لإدبار الدم دم الحيض

TAB-FULL:v4p101/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r11.speaker: الأعشى ميمون بن قيس
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r11.claim: Al-Aʿsha's poem provides poetic evidence for calling the recurring periods of women's purity qurūʾ.
TAB-FULL:v4p101/r11.anchor: فقال في ذلك الأعشى ميمون بن قيس: [البحر الطويل] وفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة … تشد لأقصاها عزيم عزائكا مورثة مالا وفي الذكر رفعة … لما ضاع فيها من قروء نسائكا

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes qurʾ to mean a period of purity, while recognizing that menstruation periods are also called qurʾ.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r1.anchor: فجعل القرء: وقت الطهر. ولما وصفنا من معنى القرء أشكل تأويل

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r2.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r2.claim: One reported view counts qurūʾ as menstruations, so a divorced woman waits through three menstrual periods and refrains from suitors.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r2.anchor: فرأى بعضهم أن الذي أمرت به المرأة المطلقة ذات الأقراء من الأقراء أقراء الحيض

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r3.claim: Another reported view counts qurūʾ as periods of purity, requiring three such periods of waiting.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r3.anchor: ورأى آخرون أن الذي أمرت به من ذلك إنما هو أقراء الطهر

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r4.claim: He requires three periods of purity; the third is completed and the following menstruation begins before her waiting period ends, since the intervening menstruations are not counted among those three.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r4.anchor: وأن بانقضائه ومجيء قرء الحيض الذي يتلوه انقضاء عدتها

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r5.claim: He rejects treating the waiting period as ending after the second purity: Qurʾanic wording remains general unless revelation specifies an exception, and the intervening opposite phases do not count as the three required qurūʾ.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r5.anchor: الحكم عندنا في كل ما أنزله الله في كتابه على ما احتمله ظاهر التنزيل ما لم يبين الله تعالى ذكره

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r6.claim: The verse shows that a woman whose husband swore ilaʾ does not become free to marry merely after four months and three menstruations; her waiting period starts only after he resolves to divorce her, since ilaʾ itself is not divorce.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r6.anchor: إن الله تعالى ذكره إنما أوجب عليها العدة بعد عزم المؤلي على طلاقها، وإيقاع الطلاق بها

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r7.claim: Al-muṭallaqāt are women whose way has been made free: they are no longer held by husbands or engaged suitors.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r7.anchor: والمخليات السبيل غير ممنوعات بأزواج ولا مخطوبات

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r8.claim: Muṭallaqa is the form used when a man has divorced his wife; ṭāliq is used of the woman who has become divorced.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r8.anchor: فلانة مطلقة، إنما هو مفعلة من قول القائل: طلق الرجل زوجته فهي مطلقة

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r9.claim: Some Arab groups say ṭaliqat al-marʾa for giving birth; this is from ṭalq, distinct from divorce, which is ṭalāq.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r9.anchor: وأما قولهم: طلقت المرأة، فمعنى غير هذا إنما يقال في هذا إذا نفست

TAB-FULL:v4p103/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r10.claim: Tarabbus means abstaining from marriage and restraining oneself from it.
TAB-FULL:v4p103/r10.anchor: وقد بينا أن التربص إنما هو التوقف عن النكاح، وحبس النفس عنه

TAB-FULL:v4p105/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r1.claim: One view says divorced women must not hide their menstruation from a husband who can still revoke the divorce, thereby frustrating his right of return.
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r1.anchor: يكتمن أزواجهن الذين طلقوهن في الطلاق الذي عليهم لهن فيه رجعة

TAB-FULL:v4p105/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r2.claim: Another view takes the concealed matter as menstruation and forbids falsely claiming to have had the third period before it occurred, which would block the husband's return.
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: هو الحيض غير أن الذي حرم الله تعالى ذكره عليها كتمانه فيما خلق في رحمها

TAB-FULL:v4p105/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r3.speaker: ابن شهاب
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r3.claim: Ibn Shihāb says they had been told that what is in the womb may be pregnancy or menstruation, which must not be concealed to run out the waiting period and defeat the husband's return right.
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r3.anchor: عن ابن شهاب، قال: قال الله تعالى ذكره

TAB-FULL:v4p105/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī repeatedly explains the concealed matter as menstruation; one transmission says menstruation is what is chiefly meant.
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r4.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] قال: الحيض

TAB-FULL:v4p105/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r5.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r5.claim: In another report, Ibrāhīm says menstruation is the principal referent of what they must not conceal.
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r5.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] قال: أكثر ذلك الحيض

TAB-FULL:v4p105/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r6.speaker: عكرمة وخالد
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r6.claim: ʿIkrima explains the concealed matter as menstruation, and Khalid glosses it as blood.
TAB-FULL:v4p105/r6.anchor: ثنا خالد الحذاء، عن عكرمة، في قوله

TAB-FULL:v4p107/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r1.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r1.claim: Another reported view includes both menstruation and pregnancy among the matters women must not conceal.
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r1.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل المعنى الذي نهيت عن كتمانه زوجها المطلق الحبل، والحيض جميعا

TAB-FULL:v4p107/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm says menstruation is what is chiefly intended by the prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r2.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] قال: أكثر ما عني به الحيض

TAB-FULL:v4p107/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says women must disclose both menstruation and pregnancy, neither concealing a period nor a pregnancy.
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] من الحيض، والحمل، لا يحل لها إن كانت حائضا

TAB-FULL:v4p107/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r4.claim: Mujāhid includes pregnancy and menstruation in the womb's contents women must not hide.
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] قال: الحمل، والحيض

TAB-FULL:v4p107/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r5.claim: Mujāhid specifies that a divorcee must not falsely claim to be menstruating or pregnant, or falsely deny that she is pregnant.
TAB-FULL:v4p107/r5.anchor: عن عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

TAB-FULL:v4p109/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r1.claim: Mujāhid says both menstruation and pregnancy are included, and a woman must not make false claims about either; the same explanation is transmitted through more than one route.
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r1.anchor: عن الحجاج، عن مجاهد، قال: " الحيض والحبل، قال: تفسيره أن لا تقول إني حائض وليست بحائض

TAB-FULL:v4p109/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r2.claim: A report from Mujāhid adds that such concealment or falsehood may arise from a woman's hatred of her husband or her love for him.
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r2.anchor: عن ليث، عن مجاهد، مثله، وزاد فيه: قال: وذلك كله في بغض المرأة زوجها، وحبه

TAB-FULL:v4p109/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says a woman must not hide either menstruation or pregnancy, nor claim a period or pregnancy contrary to fact.
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، في قوله

TAB-FULL:v4p109/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says women must disclose menstruation and offspring; concealment of pregnancy can prevent the husband from knowing when he may return her and wrong him.
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] الآية، قال: لا يكتمن الحيض، ولا الولد

TAB-FULL:v4p109/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the child and menstruation as matters women are entrusted with, especially the child.
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] يعني الولد، قال: الحيض، والولد هو الذي أؤتمن عليه النساء

TAB-FULL:v4p109/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r6.claim: Another view takes the concealed matter to be pregnancy alone; some say concealment is forbidden to prevent a woman from nullifying her husband's right to return before childbirth.
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r6.anchor: فقال بعضهم: نهيت عن ذلك لئلا تبطل حق الزوج من الرجعة إذا أراد رجعتها قبل وضعها

TAB-FULL:v4p109/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r7.claim: ʿUmar cites a woman divorced while pregnant who concealed the pregnancy until she gave birth as an example of concealing what God created in the womb.
TAB-FULL:v4p109/r7.anchor: عن علي بن رباح، أنه حدثه، أن عمر بن الخطاب قال لرجل

TAB-FULL:v4p111/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a man who divorces his pregnant wife once or twice may return her until she gives birth.
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " إذا طلق الرجل امرأته تطليقة، أو تطليقتين وهي حامل

TAB-FULL:v4p111/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says the verse concerns women divorced once or twice who hide pregnancy to escape their husbands; after three divorces there is no return until they marry another man.
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r2.anchor: عن يحيى بن بشر، أنه سمع عكرمة، يقول: " الطلاق مرتان بينهما رجعة، فإن بدا له أن يطلقها بعد هاتين فهي ثالثة

TAB-FULL:v4p111/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r3.claim: Qatāda says women in pre-Islamic practice hid pregnancy after divorce and took the child to another man, prompting the prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v4p111/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] قال: كانت المرأة إذا طلقت كتمت ما في بطنها

TAB-FULL:v4p112/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r1.claim: Qatāda reports that a woman could conceal her pregnancy until assigning the child to another man.
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] قال: كانت المرأة تكتم حملها حتى تجعله لرجل آخر منها

TAB-FULL:v4p112/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r2.claim: Another explanation says husbands asked about pregnancy before divorcing to avoid harming themselves and the child through separation, so women were ordered to tell the truth rather than lie.
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل السبب الذي من أجله نهين عن كتمان ذلك، هو أن الرجل كان إذا أراد طلاق امرأته سألها هل بها حمل

TAB-FULL:v4p112/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r3.claim: Al-Suddī describes a husband asking whether his wife is pregnant before divorce; she hides it to leave him, and if discovered is returned to him in disgrace as punishment.
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r3.anchor: عن السدي: " {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} [البقرة: 228] فالرجل يريد أن يطلق امرأته فيسألها

TAB-FULL:v4p112/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the prohibition covers both menstruation and pregnancy for women divorced once or twice: each determines the end of the waiting period and the husband's right of return, and both are created in the womb.
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r4.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال بتأويل الآية قول من قال: الذي نهيت المرأة المطلقة عن كتمانه زوجها المطلقها تطليقة أو تطليقتين مما خلق الله في رحمها الحيض، والحبل

TAB-FULL:v4p112/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r5.claim: He rejects al-Suddī's account that the prohibition concerns hiding pregnancy before a husband intends divorce: the wording follows the description of women already divorced and serving their waiting period.
TAB-FULL:v4p112/r5.anchor: وأما الذي قاله السدي من أنه معني به نهي النساء كتمان أزواجهن الحبل عند إرادتهم طلاقهن، فقول لما يدل عليه ظاهر التنزيل مخالف

TAB-FULL:v4p114/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p114/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p114/r1.claim: The phrase is an admonition: concealing menstruation or pregnancy to harm an ex-husband is not believers' conduct, so Muslim women should not imitate unbelieving women; it does not exempt unbelievers from the prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v4p114/r1.anchor: معنى ذلك على غير ما ذهبت إليه، وإنما معناه: أن كتمان المرأة المطلقة زوجها المطلقها ما خلق الله تعالى في رحمها من حيض، وولد في أيام عدتها

TAB-FULL:v4p114/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p114/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p114/r2.claim: The duty applies to all women subject to God's obligations who have menstrual cycles and are divorced after consummation: they must disclose menstruation and pregnancy.
TAB-FULL:v4p114/r2.anchor: بل الواجب على كل من لزمته فرائض الله من النساء اللواتي لهن أقراء إذا طلقت بعد الدخول بها

TAB-FULL:v4p115/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r1.claim: Baʿūla is a plural of baʿl, meaning a woman's husband; Jarīr's verse uses baʿl in that sense.
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r1.anchor: والبعولة جمع بعل: وهو الزوج للمرأة، ومنه قول جرير

TAB-FULL:v4p115/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r2.claim: Baʿl has the plurals baʿūla and baʿūl; Arabic often adds feminine tāʾ to faʿūl plurals, while it is uncommon with faʿāl, as examples including ʿiẓāma show.
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r2.anchor: ما كان على مثال «فعول» من الجمع، فإن العرب كثيرا ما تدخل فيه الهاء، فأما ما كان منها على مثال «فعال» فقليل

TAB-FULL:v4p115/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r3.claim: Husbands of women in the prescribed waiting period have the prior right to restore them to the marriage during the three qurūʾ or pregnancy, rather than the women withholding themselves from them.
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r3.anchor: أزواج المطلقات اللاتي فرضنا عليهن أن يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء، وحرمنا عليهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن

TAB-FULL:v4p115/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that after one or two divorces, a husband may return his pregnant wife until she gives birth.
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، قوله

TAB-FULL:v4p115/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r5.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm explains the husband's right to return her as applying during the waiting period.
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم: " {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن} [البقرة: 228] قال: في العدة

TAB-FULL:v4p115/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r6.speaker: عكرمة والحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r6.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī report that husbands once retained a right to return wives even after three divorces, then 2:229 abrogated that rule.
TAB-FULL:v4p115/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة، والحسن البصري، قالا: قال الله تعالى ذكره: " {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء

TAB-FULL:v4p117/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r1.claim: Mujāhid twice explains “in that” as meaning during the waiting period.
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} [البقرة: 228] في عدتهن

TAB-FULL:v4p117/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r2.claim: Qatāda says the return right lasts during the waiting period: three menstruations, three months, or pregnancy, after a first or second divorce.
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله: " {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} [البقرة: 228] أي في القروء في الثلاث حيض

TAB-FULL:v4p117/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r3.claim: Qatāda connects this return right to the warning against hiding pregnancy so that a child might be assigned to another man.
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: " {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} [البقرة: 228]

TAB-FULL:v4p117/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the husband may return her during the waiting period unless he has divorced her three times.
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: " {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} [البقرة: 228] يقول: في العدة ما لم يطلقها ثلاثا

TAB-FULL:v4p117/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says a husband may return her during the waiting period as punishment for concealing her pregnancy, making her return in disgrace.
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r5.anchor: عن السدي: " {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} [البقرة: 228] يقول: أحق برجعتها صاغرة عقوبة لما كتمت زوجها من الحمل

TAB-FULL:v4p117/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the husband is entitled to return her until the waiting period has ended.
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن} [البقرة: 228] أحق برجعتهن ما لم تنقض العدة

TAB-FULL:v4p117/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the husband may return her while she is in her waiting period if he intends to do so.
TAB-FULL:v4p117/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك: " {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} [البقرة: 228] قال: ما كانت في العدة إذا أراد المراجعة

TAB-FULL:v4p118/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r1.claim: A husband who revokes a divorce to harm his wife sins before God, since lawful revocation requires seeking reform.
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r1.anchor: أما فيما بينه وبين الله تعالى فغير جائز إذا أراد ضرارها بالرجعة لا إصلاح أمرها وأمره مراجعتها.

TAB-FULL:v4p118/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r2.claim: In court his revocation during the waiting period remains effective despite harmful intent; others may not block it, and she may claim her marital rights against later harm.
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r2.anchor: وإن أراد ضرار المراجعة برجعته فمحكوم له بالرجعة وإن كان آثما

TAB-FULL:v4p118/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r3.claim: The verse supports the view that a husband who resolves to divorce after ila pronounces a revocable divorce; it rejects treating the mere four-month lapse as an irrevocable divorce.
TAB-FULL:v4p118/r3.anchor: وفي قوله: {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} [البقرة: 228] أبين الدلالة على صحة قول من قال

TAB-FULL:v4p119/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r1.claim: Wives obey God and their husbands; husbands owe them good companionship, protection from harm, and maintenance according to their means.
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: " {ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف} [البقرة: 228] قال: إذا أطعن الله

TAB-FULL:v4p119/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r2.claim: Husbands should fear God concerning their wives just as wives should fear God concerning their husbands.
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: " {ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف} [البقرة: 228] قال: يتقون الله فيهن

TAB-FULL:v4p119/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r3.claim: Wives and husbands should reciprocally adorn themselves for one another; Ibn Abbas likes to adorn himself for his wife as he likes her to adorn herself for him.
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: " إني أحب أن أتزين للمرأة كما أحب أن تتزين لي؛ لأن الله تعالى ذكره يقول:

TAB-FULL:v4p119/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r4.claim: In context, each spouse owes the other freedom from harm: husbands should not revoke to injure, and wives should not conceal pregnancy or menstrual blood to injure them.
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r4.anchor: فحرم الله على كل واحد منهما مضارة صاحبه، وعرف كل واحد منهما ما له وما عليه من ذلك

TAB-FULL:v4p119/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r5.claim: The wording may also cover every reciprocal right, so the reported duties of good treatment and mutual adornment fall within its general sense.
TAB-FULL:v4p119/r5.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون كل ما على كل واحد منهما لصاحبه داخلا في ذلك، وإن كانت الآية نزلت فيما وصفنا

TAB-FULL:v4p121/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r1.claim: The degree is men's divinely granted advantage over women in jihad, inheritance, and everything else in which God favored them.
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {وللرجال عليهن درجة} [البقرة: 228] قال: فضل ما فضله الله به عليها من الجهاد، وفضل ميراثه

TAB-FULL:v4p121/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r2.claim: The degree means men's superior merit over women.
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " {وللرجال عليهن درجة} [البقرة: 228] قال: للرجال درجة في الفضل على النساء،

TAB-FULL:v4p121/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r3.claim: The degree means men's authority over women.
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r3.anchor: عن سفيان، عن زيد بن أسلم، في قوله: " {وللرجال عليهن درجة} [البقرة: 228] قال: إمارة

TAB-FULL:v4p121/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r4.claim: The degree is obedience: wives obey their husbands, while husbands do not obey their wives.
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وللرجال عليهن درجة} [البقرة: 228] قال: طاعة، قال: يطعن الأزواج الرجال

TAB-FULL:v4p121/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r5.speaker: محمد
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r5.claim: Muhammad says women have the like of what is due from them if they recognize this degree.
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r5.anchor: عن ابن عون، عن محمد، في قوله: " {وللرجال عليهن درجة} [البقرة: 228] قال: لا أعلم إلا أن لهن مثل الذي عليهن إذا عرفن تلك الدرجة

TAB-FULL:v4p121/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r6.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r6.claim: The degree comes from the dowry he paid: if he accuses her, he invokes liʿān, while if she accuses him she is flogged.
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r6.anchor: عن عبيدة، عن الشعبي، في قوله: " {وللرجال عليهن درجة} [البقرة: 228] قال: بما أعطاها من صداقها

TAB-FULL:v4p121/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r7.claim: A husband's degree is to be generous, overlook some of his wife's duties, and not demand every right from her.
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: " ما أحب أن أستنظف جميع حقي عليها، لأن الله تعالى ذكره يقول

TAB-FULL:v4p121/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r8.claim: Some say the degree is that men have beards and women do not.
TAB-FULL:v4p121/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل تلك الدرجة التي له عليها أن جعل له لحية، وحرمها ذلك

TAB-FULL:v4p123/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r1.speaker: حميد
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r1.claim: Humayd gives “a beard” as the meaning of the degree.
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r1.anchor: حدثني موسى بن عبد الرحمن المسروقي، قال: ثنا عبيد بن الصباح، قال: ثنا حميد، قال: " {وللرجال عليهن درجة} [البقرة: 228] قال: لحية "

TAB-FULL:v4p123/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r2.claim: Tabari prefers Ibn Abbas: the degree is a husband's generosity in overlooking some duties owed by his wife while fully giving her what he owes her.
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r2.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال بتأويل الآية ما قاله ابن عباس، وهو أن الدرجة التي ذكر الله تعالى ذكره في هذا الموضع الصفح من الرجل

TAB-FULL:v4p123/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r3.claim: Because the degree follows the reciprocal-rights clause, men are urged to forgo some rights when wives fall short; this is the favor Ibn Abbas describes.
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r3.anchor: ثم ندب الرجال إلى الأخذ عليهن بالفضل إذا تركن أداء بعض ما أوجب الله لهم عليهن

TAB-FULL:v4p123/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r4.claim: The word daraja means rank or station; although phrased as a statement, the verse urges men to show favor to women.
TAB-FULL:v4p123/r4.anchor: ومعنى الدرجة: الرتبة، والمنزلة، وهذا القول من الله تعالى ذكره، وإن كان ظاهره ظاهر الخبر، فمعناه معنى ندب الرجال

TAB-FULL:v4p124/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r1.claim: God is mighty in requiting those who disobey and transgress, and wise in ordering creation and judging people; the warning covers the preceding marital prohibitions and duties.
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r1.anchor: ولمن كتم من النساء ما خلق الله في أرحامهن أزواجهن، ونكحن في عددهن، وتركن التربص بأنفسهن إلى الوقت الذي حده الله لهن

TAB-FULL:v4p124/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ glosses “mighty” as mighty in vengeance and “wise” as wise in His command.
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r2.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: " {والله عزيز حكيم} [البقرة: 228] يقول: عزيز في نقمته، حكيم في أمره

TAB-FULL:v4p124/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r3.claim: The threat follows the prohibitions and commands from 2:221 through this verse to deter thoughtful people and prompt them to fear God's punishment.
TAB-FULL:v4p124/r3.anchor: من ابتداء قوله: {ولا تنكحوا المشركات حتى يؤمن} [البقرة: 221] إلى قوله: {وللرجال عليهن درجة} [البقرة: 228] ثم أتبع ذلك بالوعيد

TAB-FULL:v4p409/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r1.claim: God is mighty in punishing men and women who oppose His commands and limits, including violations of the previously prescribed rights and duties mentioned here.
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r1.anchor: الحول وترك المحافظة على الصلوات وأوقاتها، ومنع من كان من النساء

TAB-FULL:v4p409/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r2.claim: The violations include men withholding women’s prescribed rights and women neglecting the required waiting period after a husband’s death; both are also admonished about prayer times.
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r2.anchor: ومنع من كان من النساء ما ألزمهن الله من التربص عند وفاة أزواجهن عن الأزواج وخالف أمره في المحافظة على أوقات الصلوات

TAB-FULL:v4p409/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r3.claim: God is wise in the rulings He has already decreed among His servants and in His other judgments.
TAB-FULL:v4p409/r3.anchor: حكيم} [البقرة: 209] فيما قضى بين عباده من قضاياه التي قد تقدمت في الآيات قبل قوله. {والله عزيز حكيم} [البقرة: 228] وفي غير ذلك من أحكامه وأقضيته

TABATABAI:2:228/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r1.claim: The surrounding passage concerns divorce rulings, waiting periods, and a divorced woman nursing her child, with some rulings on prayer interposed.
TABATABAI:2:228/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات في احكام الطلاق والعدة وإرضاع المطلقة ولدها، وفي خلالها شيء من أحكام الصلاة

TABATABAI:2:228/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r2.claim: Ṭalāq originally means releasing a restraint; it was transferred metaphorically to release from marriage and became the established literal term through frequent use.
TABATABAI:2:228/r2.anchor: أصل الطلاق التخلية عن وثاق وتقييد، ثم استعير لتخلية المرأة

TABATABAI:2:228/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r3.claim: Tarabbus means waiting or detention; ‘with themselves’ indicates withholding from men, the divorce waiting period that prevents mixing of reproductive fluids and confused lineages.
TABATABAI:2:228/r3.anchor: والتربص هو الانتظار والحبس، وقد قيد بقوله تعالى بأنفسهن، ليدل على معنى التمكين من الرجال

TABATABAI:2:228/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r4.claim: The waiting-period rationale is preserving lineage, but a legal rationale need not apply in every case because rulings follow predominant interests rather than universal ones.
TABATABAI:2:228/r4.anchor: ويزيد على معنى العدة الإشارة إلى حكمة التشريع، وهو التحفظ عن اختلاط المياه

TABATABAI:2:228/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r5.claim: The declarative wording is intended as a command and emphasizes the obligation to observe the waiting period.
TABATABAI:2:228/r5.anchor: والجملة خبر أريد به الإنشاء تأكيدا

TABATABAI:2:228/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r6.claim: Qurʾ can mean either purity or menstruation and is called a contronym; because its root sense is gathering blood, followed by its discharge, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers purity.
TABATABAI:2:228/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا فالأظهر أن يكون معناه الطهر لكونه حالة جمع الدم ثم استعمل في الحيض لكونه حالة قذفه بعد الجمع

TABATABAI:2:228/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r7.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:2:228/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib says qurʾ technically names entry into menstruation after purity and collectively denotes purity with the following menstruation, then can name either separately; neither uninterrupted purity without blood nor continuous bleeding is called dhāt qurʾ.
TABATABAI:2:228/r7.anchor: قال الراغب في مفرداته والقرء في الحقيقة اسم للدخول في الحيض عن طهر ولما كان اسما جامعا للأمرين

TABATABAI:2:228/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r8.claim: Qurʾ’s root sense of gathering is supported by the Qurʾān’s use of qurʾān and qurʾānah for collection and recitation in 75:16–18 and 17:106.
TABATABAI:2:228/r8.anchor: ويشعر بأن الأصل في مادة قرء الجمع، قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:2:228/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r9.claim: The prohibition covers concealing menstruation or a child in the womb to shorten the waiting period or harm the husband by obstructing his return.
TABATABAI:2:228/r9.anchor: المراد به تحريم كتمان المطلقة الدم أو الولد استعجالا في خروج العدة أو إضرارا بالزوج

TABATABAI:2:228/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228/r10.claim: The faith condition does not make faith a prerequisite for the law; it exhorts believers to comply by framing the ruling as inherent to faith.
TABATABAI:2:228/r10.anchor: مع عدم اشتراط أصل الحكم بالإيمان نوع ترغيب وحث لمطاوعة الحكم والتثبت عليه

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r1.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, a male spouse while the couple remains married; its associations of height, strength, and steadiness underlie uses for a rider, elevated land, an idol, and a mature palm.
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r1.anchor: البعولة جمع البعل وهو الذكر من الزوجين ما داما زوجين وقد استشعر منه معنى الاستعلاء والقوة والثبات

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to the divorced women, but the return right applies only to revocably divorced women, during the waiting period, not irrevocably divorced women.
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r2.anchor: إلا أن الحكم خاص بالرجعيات دون مطلق المطلقات الأعم منها ومن البائنات

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r3.claim: The condition requires the husband to intend reconciliation and reform, barring return intended to injure the woman, as the following verse also forbids.
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r3.anchor: والتقييد بقوله إن أرادوا إصلاحا، للدلالة على وجوب أن يكون الرجوع

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r4.claim: The comparative ‘more entitled’ implies a comparison with other suitors, but only the first husband can actually resume the marriage; its implied sense is ‘more entitled to them than others.’
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r4.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن في الآية تقديرا لطيفا بحسب المعنى، والمعنى وبعولتهن أحق بهن من غيرهم

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r5.claim: The comparative entitlement itself confirms that the rule concerns revocable divorces, since irrevocable divorce permits no return.
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r5.anchor: وهذه الأحقية إنما تتحقق في الرجعيات دون البائنات التي لا رجوع فيها

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r6.claim: This verse addresses consummated marriages of menstruating women who are not pregnant; other verses govern unconsummated marriages, minors, menopausal women, and pregnant women.
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r6.anchor: والآية خاصة بحكم المدخول بهن من ذوات الحيض غير الحوامل، وأما غير المدخول بها والصغيرة واليائسة والحامل فلحكمها آيات أخر

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r7.claim: Maʿrūf is what people recognize through the acquired taste of their social life; under Islam’s natural order it also embraces reason, religious law, good character, and proper etiquette.
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r7.anchor: المعروف هو الذي يعرفه الناس بالذوق المكتسب من نوع الحياة الاجتماعية المتداولة بينهم

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r8.claim: The passage repeats maʿrūf twelve times to ensure divorce and related conduct follow sound, natural standards.
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r8.anchor: وقد كرر سبحانه المعروف في هذه الآيات فذكره في اثني عشر موضعا اهتماما بأن يجري هذا العمل

TABATABAI:2:228#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r9.claim: Natural social order requires equal rights and duties, while recognizing each person’s distinct contribution and status; Islam gives women what it places upon them while preserving their social weight in marriage and procreation.
TABATABAI:2:228#2/r9.anchor: فجعل لها مثل ما جعل عليها مع حفظ ما لها من الوزن في الحياة الاجتماعية في اجتماعها مع الرجل للتناكح والتناسل

TABATABAI:2:228-231/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-231/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-231/r1.claim: The degree is a rank that qualifies the preceding equality: women receive like obligations and rights while men retain their degree over them; he promises fuller treatment later.
TABATABAI:2:228-231/r1.anchor: والدرجة المنزلة. ومن هنا يظهر أن قوله تعالى { وللرجال عليهن درجة } ، قيد متمم للجملة السابقة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#2/r5.claim: These two rulings uniquely invoke belief in God and the Last Day because monotheism calls people to unity and connection rather than separation.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#2/r5.anchor: دين التوحيد يدعو إلى الاتحاد دون الافتراق

TABATABAI:2:228-242#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#2/r6.claim: The discourse shifts between singular and plural: rulings address the whole community, while non-ruling clauses sometimes address the Prophet directly, preserving the speech's structure and his central role.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#2/r6.anchor: والأصل في هذا الكلام خطاب المجموع أعني خطاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأمته جميعا

TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r5.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن الأنصارية
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r5.claim: Asma says she was divorced during the Prophet’s time when divorced women had no waiting period; the verse established the first divorce waiting period.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r5.anchor: عن أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن الأنصارية، قالت طلقت على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ولم يكن للمطلقة عدة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r6.speaker: ربيعة الرأي
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r6.claim: Rabiʿa holds that the Qur’anic qurūʾ are the periods of purity between menstruations, not menstruation itself.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r6.anchor: سمعت ربيعة الرأي وهو يقول إن من رأيي أن الأقراء التي سمى الله في القرآن إنما هي الطهر فيما بين الحيضتين وليس بالحيض

TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r7.claim: Imam al-Baqir says Rabiʿa’s purity interpretation came from Ali; the Imams reject the popular attribution that Ali counted menstruations as qurūʾ.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r7.anchor: إنما بلغه عن علي عليه السلام فقلت أصلحك الله أكان علي عليه السلام يقول ذلك؟ قال نعم، كان يقول إنما القرء الطهر

TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r8.claim: For a divorce pronounced during purity without intercourse and witnessed by two just men, al-Baqir says the waiting period ends when the third menstruation begins.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#11/r8.anchor: إذا دخلت في الحيضة الثالثة فقد انقضت عدتها وحلت للأزواج

TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says several chains report from Ali that qurūʾ means periods of purity, as the preceding narration states.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r1.anchor: هذا المعنى مروي بعدة طرق عنه عليه السلام

TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r2.claim: A report cited from al-Shafiʿi and other Sunni authorities attributes to Ali the view that the wife may be taken back until she bathes after the third menstruation.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام قال تحل لزوجها الرجعة عليها حتى تغتسل من الحيضة الثالثة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت، عبد الله بن عمر، عائشة
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r3.claim: The purity interpretation is also attributed to Zayd ibn Thabit, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, and ʿAʾisha.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r3.anchor: نسبوا هذا القول إلى عدة أخرى من الصحابة غيره عليه السلام كزيد بن ثابت وعبد الله بن عمر وعائشة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r4.speaker: جعفر الصادق
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r4.claim: Al-Ṣadiq interprets what God created in women’s wombs as pregnancy and menstruation.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r4.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام في قوله تعالى ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن الآية الحبل والحيض

TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r5.claim: Tafsīr al-Qummī says God entrusted women with three matters: purity, menstruation, and pregnancy.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r5.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي وقد فوض الله إلى النساء ثلاثة أشياء الطهر والحيض والحبل

TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r6.speaker: جعفر الصادق
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r6.claim: Al-Qummī transmits al-Ṣadiq’s statement that men’s rights over women are greater than women’s rights over men.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r6.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي أيضا في قوله تعالى وللرجال عليهن درجة، قال قال عليه السلام حق الرجال على النساء أفضل من حق النساء على الرجال

TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r7.claim: This report does not conflict with equality in the way reciprocal rights are established, as the commentary explained earlier.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#12/r7.anchor: وهذا لا ينافي التساوي من حيث وضع الحقوق كما مر

TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r1.claim: The author compares human use of domestic animals: people treat their lives as subordinate to human needs and recognize claims against them only as property claims belonging to the owner.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r1.anchor: لأن الإنسان يرى وجودها تبعا لوجود نفسه وحياتها فرعا لحياته ومكانتها مكانة الطفيلي

TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r2.claim: He says women in many societies likewise lived dependently, treated as made for men, without independent lives or rights, under the absolute guardianship of fathers and then husbands.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r2.anchor: كذلك كانت حياة النساء عند الرجال في هذه الأمم والقبائل حياة تبعية

TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r3.claim: The author describes men as controlling women’s bodies, marriage, labor, and property, while women were required to obey and perform domestic and arduous work without independence.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r3.anchor: كان للرجل أن يبيع المرأة ممن شاء وكان له أن يهبها لغيره، وكان له أن يقرضها لمن استقرضها للفراش أو الاستيلاد

TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r4.claim: He notes that customs varied by people and environment, including a reported tribe where a woman resumed household work immediately after childbirth while her husband rested in her bed.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#19/r4.anchor: وقد بلغ عجيب الأمر إلى حيث إن المرأة الحامل في بعض القبائل إذا وضعت حملها قامت من فورها إلى حوائج البيت

TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r1.claim: In pre-Islamic societies governed mainly by inherited custom, including China, India, ancient Egypt, and Iran, women's status followed local practice rather than scripture or codified law.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r1.anchor: من غير استناد إلى كتاب أو قانون كالصين والهند ومصر القديم وإيران ونحوها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r2.claim: Women lacked independent will and action, had no public role in government or adjudication, and were expected both to work alongside men and to manage the home and obey them.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r2.anchor: لا كان لها حق المداخلة في الشؤون الاجتماعية من حكومة أو قضاء أو غيرهما

TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r3.claim: Compared with women in less settled societies, they were generally spared killing and eating, but men could take unlimited wives, divorce them, and remarry after a wife's death.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r3.anchor: وكان للرجل أن يتخذ زوجات متعددة من غير تحديد وكان لها تطليق من شاء منهن

TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r4.claim: A woman could sometimes acquire property by inheritance, marriage, or other means, yet could not dispose of it independently.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r4.anchor: كانت تتملك في الجملة من إرث أو ازدواج أو غير ذلك وإن لم تكن لها أن تتصرف فيها بالاستقلال

TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r5.claim: Customs differed by region and class: some elite Iranian women could participate in property, rule, or sovereignty, and marriages among close relatives occurred.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r5.anchor: تميزا لنساء الطبقات العالية من المداخلة في الملك والحكومة أو نيل السلطنة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r6.claim: In China, marriage resembled purchasing the woman into subjection; women lacked inheritance and even shared meals with men, while multiple men could share one wife and children were assigned chiefly to the strongest husband.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r6.anchor: كان بالصين الازدواج بالمرأة نوعا من اشتراء نفسها ومملوكيتها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r7.claim: In India, widows could not remarry and were either burned with their husbands or left humiliated; menstruating women and what touched them were treated as impure.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r7.anchor: لا يحل لهن الازدواج بعد توفي أزواجهن أبدا

TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r8.claim: Al-Tabataba'i summarizes these societies as treating women like an inferior being between animal and human, useful as a weak dependent who must remain under guardianship.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#20/r8.anchor: كالبرزخ بين الحيوان والإنسان يستفاد منها استفادة الإنسان المتوسط الضعيف

TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r1.claim: Some societies, including the Chaldeans, Romans, and Greeks, lived under written law or scripture, unlike the customs-based societies discussed earlier.

TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r2.claim: Under Hammurabi's law, a wife was subordinate; disobedience could lead to expulsion or treatment as a concubine, and proven wasteful household management could lead to drowning.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r2.anchor: لو لم تطع زوجها في شيء من أمور المعاشرة أو استقل بشيء فيها كان له أن يخرجها من بيته

TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r3.claim: Rome began codifying civil law around 400 BCE and gradually expanded it; household heads exercised authority over domestic affairs.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r3.anchor: وضع القانون فيها أول ما وضع في حدود سنة أربعمائة قبل الميلاد ثم أخذوا في تكميله تدريجا

TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r4.claim: The Roman paterfamilias was treated as a household deity and had unrestricted command over wife and children, even authority to kill them without challenge.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r4.anchor: وكان له الاختيار التام والمشية النافذة في جميع ما يريده ويأمر به على أهل البيت

TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r5.claim: Roman women had less standing than dependent male children: they could not complain, transact, or participate in public life, while men, including adopted sons, could be authorized to act independently.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r5.anchor: فإنهن لم يكن أجراء للاجتماع المدني فلا تسمع لهن شكاية

TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r6.claim: In Greek and Roman-style households, formal kinship and inheritance linked men; women lacked official kinship even with mothers, daughters, sisters, husbands, and sons, although natural kinship still existed and could shape marriage and household authority.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#21/r6.anchor: فكانت القرابة الاجتماعية الرسمية المؤثرة في التوارث ونحوها مختصه بما بين الرجال

TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r1.claim: A woman's life was controlled by her father or husband: he could sell, give, lend, punish, control her property, arrange her marriage, and divorce her.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r1.anchor: زمام حياتها وإرادتها بيد رب البيت من أبيها إن كانت في بيت الأب أو زوجها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r2.claim: Greek household organization and the subordination of women were broadly similar to the Roman pattern.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r2.anchor: فالأمر عندهم في تكون البيوت وربوبية أربابها فيها كان قريب الوضع من وضع الروم

TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r3.claim: These legal systems contradicted themselves: women were punished independently for wrongdoing but recognized or rewarded only through male guardianship, reflecting a view of them as dangerous yet necessary for reproduction and useful to men.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r3.anchor: كانت المرأة عندهم تعاقب بجميع جرائمها بالاستقلال

TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r4.claim: Because society was understood to depend on men, male descendants alone counted as true continuers of a household; adoption and having a male relative impregnate a barren man's wife were used to prevent extinction.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي سمعته أن الاجتماع كان متقوما عندهم بالرجال هو الذي ألزمهم أن يعتقدوا أن الأولاد بالحقيقة هم الذكور

TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r5.claim: Greek men could have multiple wives, but only one was an official wife; the others lacked that formal status.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#22/r5.anchor: وكان من الجائز عندهم تعدد الزوجات

TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r1.claim: The Arabs lived on a hot, arid peninsula, mostly as nomadic raiding tribes connected to Persia, Rome, Abyssinia, and Sudan; their customs were mainly uncivilized but borrowed regional practices.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r1.anchor: والمعظم من أمتهم قبائل بدوية بعيدة عن الحضارة والمدنية

TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r2.claim: Arab women generally lacked independent standing, inheritance, and social honor beyond family reputation; men could have unlimited wives and divorce freely.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r2.anchor: كانت العرب لا ترى للمرأة استقلالا في الحياة ولا حرمة ولا شرافة إلا حرمة البيت وشرافته

TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r3.claim: Female infanticide began among Banū Tamīm after the capture of their daughters in a conflict with al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir, then spread to other Arabs.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r3.anchor: ابتدأ بذلك بنو تميم لوقعة كانت لهم مع النعمان بن المنذر

TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r4.claim: Arabs regarded a daughter as a disgrace and hid her birth, while celebrating sons even when obtained by adoption or affiliation; rival chiefs sometimes claimed the same child.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r4.anchor: يتوارى من القوم من سوء ما بشر به

TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r5.claim: Some elite households allowed women, especially daughters, a say in choosing marriage, resembling Iranian aristocratic custom.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r5.anchor: وربما لاح في بعض البيوت استقلال لنسائهم وخاصة للبنات في أمر الازدواج

TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r6.claim: Arab treatment combined urban restrictions on women's rights and public roles with the coercion of barbarian societies; it arose from power over the weak, not household-head worship.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r6.anchor: فلم يكن حرمانهن مستندا إلى تقديس رؤساء البيوت وعبادتهم

TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r7.claim: Arab men and women worshipped idols tied to tribal preferences, including stars, angels imagined as God's daughters, and objects such as stones and wood.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#23/r7.anchor: فيعبدون الكواكب والملائكة وهم بنات الله سبحانه بزعمهم ويتخذونها على صور صورتها لهم أوهامهم

TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r1.claim: A satirical verse mocked Banū Ḥanīfa for worshipping an idol made from date paste and then eating it during famine.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r1.anchor: أكلت حنيفة ربها زمن التقحم والمجاعة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r2.claim: Arabs might replace a stone idol with a better stone, or make an idol by pouring milk over a handful of soil and worship it.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r2.anchor: وإذا لم يجدوا شيئا جمعوا حفنة من تراب ثم جاؤا بغنم فحلبوه عليها ثم طافوا بها يعبدونها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says deprivation and suffering weakened women's thought and made them susceptible to strange superstitions about events, recorded in historical works.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r3.anchor: وقد أودعت هذا الحرمان والشقاء في نفوس النساء ضعفا في الفكرة يصور لها أوهاما وخرافات عجيبة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r4.claim: His first conclusion is that societies viewed women as animal-like or as deficient, unsafe human beings if freed from dependence; he associates the harsher view with uncivilized peoples.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r4.anchor: يرونها إنسانا في أفق الحيوان العجم

TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r5.claim: Second, women were excluded from society's structure, viewed instead as a necessary condition of it or as captive dependents exploited by dominant society.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r5.anchor: أنها خارجة من هيكل المجتمع المركب غير داخلة فيه

TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r6.claim: Third, women were denied nearly all rights except to the extent that men responsible for them could benefit.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r6.anchor: يرون حرمانها في عامة الحقوق التي أمكن انتفاعها منها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r7.claim: Fourth, relations with women rested on the strong exploiting the weak; settled societies additionally claimed that women's nature made them incapable of independence and dangerous if trusted.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#24/r7.anchor: هو غلبة القوي على الضعيف وبعبارة أخرى قريحة الاستخدام

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r1.claim: Across languages, idioms and figures of speech used womanhood to taunt cowards and condemn the weak or humiliated; al-Tabataba'i treats this vocabulary as evidence of women's social standing.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r1.anchor: الخصائل الروحية والجهات الوجودية في كل أمة تتجلى في لغتها وآدابها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r2.claim: An unnamed poet asks whether the people of al-Ḥiṣn are men or women, an example of using womanhood as an insult.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r2.anchor: وما أدري وليت إخال أدري أقوم آل حصن أم نساء

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r3.claim: Before Islam, only parts of the Torah and Jesus' counsel to ease and treat women gently showed concern for their condition.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r3.anchor: إلا بعض ما في التوراة وما وصى به عيسى بن مريم عليهما السلام من لزوم التسهيل عليها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r4.claim: Islam brought an unprecedented change: it restored a natural foundation for women's status and rejected earlier beliefs about her identity and practices toward her.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r4.anchor: فإنه أبدع في حقها أمرا ما كانت تعرفه الدنيا منذ قطن بها قاطنوها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r5.claim: Women and men are equally human, composed from male and female, with no superiority except through piety; Qur'an 49:13 makes that criterion explicit.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r5.anchor: أن المرأة كالرجل إنسان وأن كل إنسان ذكرا أو أنثى فإنه إنسان يشترك في مادته وعنصره

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r6.speaker: القائل
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r6.claim: A cited poet calls mothers mere vessels; al-Tabataba'i rejects that reduction and says each person is formed from both sexes.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r6.anchor: مثل ما قاله القائل وإنما أمهات الناس أوعية

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r7.speaker: الآخر
