TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r7.claim: Another poet claims sons of sons belong to us while daughters' sons belong to other men; al-Tabataba'i rejects this patrilineal account of descent.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r7.anchor: مثل ما قاله الآخر بنونا بنو أبنائنا وبناتنا بنوهن أبناء الرجال الأباعد

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r8.claim: Qur'an 3:195 says neither sex's effort is lost: each person is accountable for their own deeds, unlike the view that women bear sins while men take the benefits of their existence.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r8.anchor: فصرح أن السعي غير خائب والعمل غير مضيع عند الله

TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r9.claim: Virtue depends on piety, faith, knowledge, sound reason, good character, patience, and forbearance; a woman excelling in these can rank above a man who does not.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#25/r9.anchor: ومن التقوى الأخلاق الفاضلة كالإيمان بدرجاته

TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r1.claim: Qur'an 16:97, 40:40, and 4:124 affirm that believing women and men who do good receive good life, reward, and entry into Paradise without injustice.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r1.anchor: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى

TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r2.claim: Qur'an 16:59 condemns the shame Arab fathers felt at a daughter's birth; they hid her because they feared she would become another man's sexual plaything and bring dishonor to her family.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r2.anchor: ولم يكن تواريهم إلا لعدهم ولادتها عارا على المولود له

TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r3.claim: The Qur'an's condemnation of burying girls alive is emphatic: the buried girl will be asked for what sin she was killed.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r3.anchor: وقد بالغ الله سبحانه في التشديد عليه حيث قال وإذا الموؤدة سئلت بأي ذنب قتلت

TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r4.claim: Some Muslims retain an inherited double standard that treats adultery as lasting shame for a woman and her family but not for a persistent male adulterer; Islam assigns shame to the sin and guilt equally to both.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r4.anchor: تراهم يعدون الزنا عارا لازما على المرأة وبيتها وإن تابت دون الزاني وإن أصر

TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r5.claim: Women have independent will and action in managing life and may own what they earn; both sexes share social standing, with each accountable for their own gain, as 3:195 and 2:286 indicate.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r5.anchor: فلها أن تستقل بالإرادة ولها أن تستقل بالعمل وتمتلك نتاجهما كما للرجل ذلك من غير فرق

TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r6.claim: God-given differences shape some distinct rules: a woman is like a cultivated field in reproduction and preservation of the human kind, and her delicate constitution and feeling also affect social duties.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#26/r6.anchor: إحداهما أنها بمنزلة الحرث في تكون النوع ونمائه فعليها يعتمد النوع في بقائه

TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r1.claim: Qur'an 4:32 forbids coveting distinctions assigned to each sex: men's inheritance share and women's exemption from maintenance obligations correspond to different social contributions.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r1.anchor: كفضل الرجل على المرأة في سهم الإرث

TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r2.claim: Other forms of excellence depend on individual deeds, not sex: faith, knowledge, reason, piety, and other virtues; believers should ask God for bounty.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r2.anchor: ومنه ما لم يتعين إلا بعمل العامل كائنا من كان كفضل الإيمان والعلم والعقل والتقوى

TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the following phrase about men being maintainers will further explain the division of merits in 4:32.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r3.anchor: والدليل على هذا الذي ذكرنا قوله تعالى بعده الرجال قوامون

TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r4.claim: Women share men's worship and social rights and may act independently in inheritance, earning, transactions, education, learning, acquiring rights, and defending them, except where nature calls for different rules.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#27/r4.anchor: فلها أن تستقل فيما يستقل به الرجل من غير فرق في إرث ولا كسب ولا معاملة ولا تعليم وتعلم

TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i lists governance, judgeship, and armed combat as roles women do not hold; this excludes direct fighting, not attendance or assistance such as treating the wounded.

TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r2.claim: Women receive half a man's inheritance share and must cover themselves and adornments.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r2.anchor: ولها نصف سهم الرجل في الإرث

TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r3.claim: A wife must obey her husband regarding sexual access; in return, her father or husband must provide for her and protect her to the fullest ability.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r3.anchor: وعليها أن تطيع زوجها فيما يرجع إلى التمتع منها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r4.claim: Women have rights to raise and care for children; they are protected in person and reputation, excused from worship during menstruation and postpartum bleeding, and owed gentle treatment in all circumstances.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r4.anchor: وأن لها حق تربية الولد وحضانته

TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r5.claim: Women's required learning covers foundational beliefs and religious rulings, including worship and social laws; their required conduct also includes the husband's sexual rights.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r5.anchor: لا يجب عليها في جانب العلم إلا العلم بأصول المعارف والعلم بالفروع الدينية أحكام العبادات

TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r6.claim: Earning a livelihood, household work, education, useful professions, and public contribution are not obligatory for women; doing them is meritorious and a source of pride, which Islam encourages women to express.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r6.anchor: ولازمه أن يكون الورود في جميع هذه الموارد من علم أو كسب أو شغل

TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r7.claim: Prophetic conduct with Khadija, Fatima, his wives, and other women, along with the conduct of the Prophet's household and its women, supports this account; the author defers fuller examples to reports on women's verses.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r7.anchor: مع زوجته خديجة ومع بنته سيدة النساء فاطمة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r8.claim: The foundation of these rights and duties is human nature: social roles and normative obligations ultimately arise from natural human constitution, though social arrangements can become defective as bodies can be malformed or ill.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#28/r8.anchor: أن الوظائف الاجتماعية والتكاليف الاعتبارية المتفرعة عليها يجب انتهائها بالأخرة إلى الطبيعة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r1.claim: Social arrangements, whether sound or corrupt, ultimately answer to human nature; corruption alters their effects along the way.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r1.anchor: فالاجتماع بجميع شؤونه وجهاته سواء كان اجتماعا فاضلا أو اجتماعا فاسدا ينتهي بالاخرة إلى الطبيعة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r2.claim: Creation is equipped and guided toward its ends; a flourishing human life aligns conduct with created nature and fitra.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r2.anchor: فالأشياء ومن جملتها الإنسان إنما تهتدي في وجودها وحياتها إلى ما خلقت له وجهزت بما يكفيه

TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r3.claim: Social justice does not give every person every office regardless of capacity; indiscriminate sameness would harm both capable and incapable people.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r3.anchor: لكن ليس مقتضى هذه التسوية التي يحكم بها العدل الاجتماعي أن يبذل كل مقام اجتماعي لكل فرد

TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r4.claim: Equality means each person receives the particular right due to them and their proper station, without one right displacing or nullifying another.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r4.anchor: أن يعطى كل ذي حق حقه وينزل منزلته، فالتساوي بين الأفراد والطبقات إنما هو في نيل كل ذي حق خصوص حقه

TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r5.claim: The verse affirms equality of rights while also explicitly recognizing a difference between women and men.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r5.anchor: فإن الآية تصرح بالتساوي في عين تقرير الاختلاف بينهن وبين الرجال

TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r6.claim: Because women and men share thought and will, women share in freedom of thought and choice and may independently manage their personal and social lives absent a restriction.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r6.anchor: اشتراك القبيلين أعني الرجال والنساء في أصول المواهب الوجودية أعني، الفكر والإرادة المولدتين للاختيار

TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r7.claim: Islam grants women independence in action and will from male guardianship; the Qur’an permits their proper conduct in their own affairs.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#29/r7.anchor: فصارت بنعمة الله سبحانه مستقلة بنفسها منفكة الإرادة والعمل عن الرجال وولايتهم وقيمومتهم

TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r1.claim: He claims average women have less developed physical traits and greater sensitivity, while men are more governed by reason and women by feeling.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r1.anchor: فإن المتوسطة من النساء تتأخر عن المتوسط من الرجال في الخصوصيات الكمالية من بنيتها كالدماغ والقلب والشرايين

TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r2.claim: He assigns leadership, judging, and fighting to men on the ground that these roles require reason, and child care, upbringing, and household management to women.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r2.anchor: فخص مثل الولاية والقضاء والقتال بالرجال لاحتياجها المبرم إلى التعقل والحياة التعقلية إنما هي للرجل

TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r3.claim: Men bear women’s expenses and receive a two-to-one inheritance share; he describes this as compensating men for support while women chiefly benefit from assets.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r3.anchor: وجعل نفقتها على الرجل، وجبر ذلك له بالسهمين في الإرث وهو في الحقيقة بمنزلة أن يقتسما الميراث نصفين

TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r4.claim: An objection says that relieving women of necessary work and requiring male support will make them idle and socially unproductive, as experience allegedly shows.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r4.anchor: فإن ارتفاع الحاجة الضرورية إلى لوازم الحياة بتخديرها، وكفاية مؤنتها بإيجاب الانفاق على الرجل يوجب إهمالها وكسلها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r5.claim: He answers that sound laws and their successful implementation through good practice and education are separate matters.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r5.anchor: قلت وضع القوانين المصلحة لحال البشر أمر، وإجراء ذلك بالسيرة الصالحة والتربية الحسنة التي تنبت الإنسان

TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r6.claim: He attributes Islam’s historical failure to put its rules into practice to the loss of righteous guardians and administrators, which stalled education and reversed progress.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r6.anchor: والذي أصيب به الإسلام في مدة سيرها الماضي هو فقد الأولياء الصالحين والقوام المجاهدين فارتدت بذلك أنفاس الأحكام

TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r7.claim: Experience shows that ideas alone have no effect unless sound preaching and education establish them in people’s character.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r7.anchor: ومن أوضح ما أفاده التجارب القطعي أن مجرد النظر والاعتقاد لا يثمر أثره ما لم يثبت في النفس بالتبليغ

TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r8.speaker: معاوية
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī recalls Muʿāwiya saying after taking power in Iraq that he fought to rule people, not to make them pray or fast, and had achieved that aim.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#30/r8.anchor: فهذا معاوية، يقول على منبر العراق حين غلب على أمر الخلافة ما حاصله إني ما كنت أقاتلكم لتصلوا

TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r1.claim: God’s enduring light preserved Islam from being extinguished despite its opponents and historical failures.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r1.anchor: ولولا استضاءة هذا الدين بنور الله الذي لا يطفأ والله متم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r2.claim: Islam led in freeing women from bondage and granting independence of will and action; Western nations later imitated it, though imperfectly.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r2.anchor: الإسلام له التقدم الباهر في إطلاقها عن قيد الاسارة، وإعطائها الاستقلال في الإرادة والعمل

TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r3.speaker: الرأي العام عندهم
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r3.claim: The prevailing Western view he describes attributes women’s lesser virtue to centuries of poor upbringing, while assuming their innate nature equals men’s.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r3.anchor: والرأي العام عندهم تقريبا أن تأخر المرأة في الكمال والفضيلة مستند إلى سوء التربية التي دامت عليها

TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r4.claim: He rejects that account: social organization has long subordinated women, and equal innate natures should sometimes have produced the opposite and similar anatomy.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r4.anchor: ويتوجه عليه أن الاجتماع منذ أقدم عهود تكونه قضى على تأخرها عن الرجل في الجملة، ولو كان الطباعان متساويين

TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r5.claim: He argues that even highly attentive Western societies have not achieved equality in leadership, judging, or fighting, where statistics still favor men.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r5.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك أن المدنية الغربية مع غاية عنايتها في تقديم المرأة ما قدرت بعد على إيجاد التساوي بينهما

TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r6.claim: Marriage is a foundational social practice, and social practices ultimately need a natural basis.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r6.anchor: عمل النكاح من أصول الأعمال الاجتماعية، والبشر منذ أول تكونه وتكثره حتى اليوم لم يخل عن هذا العمل الاجتماعي

TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r7.claim: Islam bases marriage on complementary male and female sexual nature directed toward reproduction and preserving the human species; related rules govern sex, exclusivity, divorce, waiting periods, children, and inheritance.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#31/r7.anchor: ومن البين عند كل من أجاد التأمل أن طبيعة الإنسان الذكور في تجهيزها لا تريد إلا الإناث وكذا العكس

TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r1.claim: He says contemporary civil laws base marriage on the spouses sharing their work and life together.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r1.anchor: وأما القوانين الأخر الحاضرة فقد وضعت أساس النكاح على تشريك الزوجين مساعيهما في الحياة

TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r2.claim: He argues that general social cooperation arises from people’s varied needs and skills, but gives no natural reason specifically for pairing a man and a woman.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r2.anchor: فالجميع يقوم بالجميع، والأشواق الخاصة المتعلق كل واحد منها بشغل من الأشغال ونحو من أنحاء الأعمال متفرقة في الأفراد

TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r3.claim: He rejects marriage as merely a partnership in livelihood because it departs from the natural basis of reproduction and procreation.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r3.anchor: انحراف عن صراط الاقتضاء الطبيعي للتناسل والتوالد

TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r4.claim: If marriage rested only on partnership, it would need no special rules beyond general cooperation; he says that would abolish chastity, lineage, inheritance, and innate sexual instincts, as communism accepts.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r4.anchor: وفي ذلك إبطال فضيلة العفة رأسا وإبطال أحكام الأنساب والمواريث كما التزمته الشيوعية

TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r5.claim: He calls divorce permitted by Islamic law a merit grounded in nature, since nature gives no evidence for banning it; its particular conditions are treated in Sūrat al-Ṭalāq.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r5.anchor: وأما الطلاق فهو من مفاخر هذه الشريعة الإسلامية، وقد وضع جوازه على الفطرة إذ لا دليل من الفطرة يدل على المنع عنه

TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r6.claim: He says major modern nations were eventually compelled to include divorce in their civil laws.
TABATABAI:2:228-242#32/r6.anchor: وقد اضطرت الملل المعظمة اليوم إلى ادخاله في قوانينهم المدنية بعد ما لم يكن

TABRISI:2:228/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228/r1.claim: Qurūʾ has the few plural aqruʾ and the more commonly used aqraʾ or qurūʾ; the common plural form signals the many women governed by the rule although each waits three periods.
TABRISI:2:228/r1.anchor: القروء جمع قرء وجمعه القليل أقرء والكثير أقراء وقروء

TABRISI:2:228/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228/r2.claim: One root sense of qurʾ is gathering, as with the gathering of letters in recitation or a womb gathering around a pregnancy.

TABRISI:2:228/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228/r3.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
TABRISI:2:228/r3.claim: ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's line uses qaraʾ for a womb that has not gathered a fetus, illustrating the root sense of gathering.
TABRISI:2:228/r3.anchor:
قال عمرو بن كلثوم:
ذراعي عيطل أدماء بكر

TABRISI:2:228/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228/r4.claim: On the gathering sense, a woman is said to have aqraʾ when she menstruates as blood gathers in the womb; qurʾ can also mean purity as blood gathers in the body.
TABRISI:2:228/r4.anchor: فعلى هذا يقال أقرأت المرأة فهي مقرىء إذا حاضت

TABRISI:2:228/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228/r5.claim: A second root sense is a regularly recurring time, which can designate either menstruation or purity.
TABRISI:2:228/r5.anchor: والوجه الثاني: إن أصل القرء الوقت الجاري في الفعل على عادة

TABRISI:2:228/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228/r6.claim: A poet's line about the time when winds blow illustrates the sense of a regularly recurring time.
TABRISI:2:228/r6.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
شنئت العقر عقر بني شليل

TABRISI:2:228/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228/r7.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:2:228/r7.claim: Al-Aʿshā's lines about his wives' qurūʾ use the term for periods of purity, supporting that interpretation.
TABRISI:2:228/r7.anchor:
قول الأعشى:
وفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة

TABRISI:2:228/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228/r8.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, husband; the husband is called this because he is above the woman through marital authority.
TABRISI:2:228/r8.anchor: والبعولة جمع بعل ويقال بعل يبعل بعولة وهو بعل

TABRISI:2:228#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#2/r1.claim: In 37:125 baʿl means a lord or, alternatively, an idol; baʿl also names a palm watered by its roots.

TABRISI:2:228#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#2/r2.claim: Related uses describe being constricted by a matter, acting arrogantly, or a bewildered woman; the root's underlying idea is superiority.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r2.anchor: وبعل الرجل بأمره إذا ضاق به ذراعا لأنه علاه منه ما ضاق به ذرعه

TABRISI:2:228#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#2/r3.claim: Rijāl and related forms derive from strength; daraja means rank or degree.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r3.anchor: الرجال جمع رجل يقال رجل بين الرجلة أي القوة

TABRISI:2:228#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#2/r4.claim: The conditional answer is omitted: if they believe, they will not conceal; the answer to the husbands' condition is likewise omitted and understood as their being entitled to return them.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r4.anchor: إن كن يؤمن بالله } جواب الشرط محذوف وتقديره

TABRISI:2:228#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#2/r5.claim: The annexation in mithlu alladhī ʿalayhinna is not a true genitive construction because alladhī ʿalayhinna functions as its object.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r5.anchor: مثل الذي عليهن إضافة مثل غير حقيقية لأن الذي عليهن مفعوله

TABRISI:2:228#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#2/r6.claim: The waiting-period rule concerns divorced women who have consummated marriage, menstruate, and are not pregnant; they wait until three qurūʾ pass and may not marry meanwhile.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r6.anchor: يعني المطلقات المدخول بهن من ذوات الحيض غير الحوامل

TABRISI:2:228#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#2/r7.claim: The wording is grammatically declarative but functions as a command to wait.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r7.anchor: ينتظرن بأنفسهن انقضاء ثلاثة قروء فلا يتزوجن لفظه خبر ومعناه أمر

TABRISI:2:228#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#2/r8.claim: The author and the Imāmī position take qurūʾ as periods of purity; this is also attributed to Zayd ibn Thābit, ʿĀʾisha, Ibn ʿUmar, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the people of Medina.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r8.anchor: والمراد بالقروء الأطهار عندنا، وبه قال زيد بن ثابت

TABRISI:2:228#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r9.speaker: ابن شهاب
TABRISI:2:228#2/r9.claim: Ibn Shihāb says all the people of his region held that the aqrāʾ are periods of purity except Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن شهاب: ما رأيت أحدا من أهل بلدنا

TABRISI:2:228#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:228#2/r10.claim: The competing view takes qurūʾ as menstruations, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and also reported from ʿAlī; it is Abū Ḥanīfa's position.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r10.anchor: والمروي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن ومجاهد ورووه أيضا عن علي أن القرء الحيض

TABRISI:2:228#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#2/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
TABRISI:2:228#2/r11.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his followers support the menstruation interpretation with a report that the Prophet told a woman to stop praying during her days of qurūʾ.
TABRISI:2:228#2/r11.anchor: وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة وأصحابه واستشهدوا بقوله عليه السلام للمستحاضة

TABRISI:2:228#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#3/r1.claim: The cited instruction to a mustaḥāḍa to stop praying on her qurūʾ days supports the menstruation interpretation, since prayer is suspended during menstruation.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r1.anchor: والصلاة إنما تترك في أيام الحيض

TABRISI:2:228#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#3/r2.claim: For the purity interpretation, the author cites 65:1, understood as ordering divorce during a pure period in which the couple has not had intercourse.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r2.anchor: أي في طهر لم تجامع فيه كما يقال لغرة الشهر

TABRISI:2:228#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r3.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:228#3/r3.claim: When Ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife during menstruation, the Prophet told him to take her back and, once she was pure, either divorce or keep her.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r3.anchor: ويقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما طلق ابن عمر زوجته وهي حائض

TABRISI:2:228#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#3/r4.claim: The Prophet's recitation of 65:1 indicates that the waiting period begins with purity: a woman divorced during menstruation has not yet begun it.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r4.anchor: فأخبر أن العدة الأطهار دون الحيض لأنها حينئذ تستقبل عدتها

TABRISI:2:228#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r5.speaker: ربيعة الرأي
TABRISI:2:228#3/r5.claim: Rabīʿa al-Raʾy says the Qurʾānic aqrāʾ are the periods of purity between menstruations, not menstruations themselves.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r5.anchor: وروى أصحابنا عن زرارة قال: سمعت ربيعة الرأي يقول

TABRISI:2:228#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:2:228#3/r6.claim: Al-Bāqir says Rabīʿa did not reach the view independently but received it from ʿAlī.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r6.anchor: قال فدخلت على أبي جعفر فحدثته بما قال ربيعة فقال: كذب

TABRISI:2:228#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r7.speaker: علي
TABRISI:2:228#3/r7.claim: ʿAlī says qurʾ is purity: blood gathers during that period and is expelled when menstruation comes; the waiting period ends upon entering the third menstruation.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r7.anchor: قال: نعم. كان يقول إنما القرء الطهر تقرأ فيه الدم

TABRISI:2:228#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r8.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:2:228#3/r8.claim: Al-Bāqir rejects the Iraqi report that ʿAlī said a husband retains the right of return until the third menstruation has ended.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r8.anchor: إن أهل العراق يروون عن علي ع أنه كان يقول هو أحق بردها

TABRISI:2:228#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r9.speaker: إبراهيم وعكرمة
TABRISI:2:228#3/r9.claim: Ibrāhīm and ʿIkrima take what is hidden in the wombs to mean menstruation.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r9.anchor: قيل أراد به الحيض عن إبراهيم وعكرمة

TABRISI:2:228#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:2:228#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda take it to mean pregnancy.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r10.anchor: وقيل أراد به الحبل عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:2:228#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r11.speaker: ابن عمر والحسن والصادق
TABRISI:2:228#3/r11.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ṣādiq include both menstruation and pregnancy; the author prefers this broader interpretation.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r11.anchor: وقيل أراد به الحيض والحبل عن ابن عمر والحسن وهو المروي عن الصادق ع

TABRISI:2:228#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r12.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:2:228#3/r12.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says God entrusted women with three matters: menstruation, purity, and pregnancy.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r12.anchor: قال قد فوض الله إلى النساء ثلاثة أشياء الحيض والطهر والحمل

TABRISI:2:228#3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:228#3/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says concealment would wrong the husband by preventing him from returning to his wife.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r13.anchor: وإنما لم يحل لهن الكتمان لئلا يظلمن الزوج بمنع المراجعة عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:228#3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:228#3/r14.claim: Qatāda says concealment could falsely attribute a child to someone else, as in pre-Islamic practice.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r14.anchor: وقيل بنسبة الولد إلى غيره كفعل الجاهلية عن قتادة

TABRISI:2:228#3/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#3/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#3/r15.claim: The faith clause is not a legal condition permitting unbelievers to conceal; it warns that true faith prevents this sin.
TABRISI:2:228#3/r15.anchor: وليس هذا بشرط حتى أنها إذا لم تكن مؤمنة يحل لها الكتمان

TABRISI:2:228#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#4/r1.claim: While the waiting period remains, husbands may restore their wives to the prior marital state; that right expires when the period ends.
TABRISI:2:228#4/r1.anchor: يعني إن أزواجهن أولى بمراجعتهن وهي ردهن إلى الحالة الأولى

TABRISI:2:228#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#4/r2.claim: A husband alone may revoke a revocable divorce without his wife's consent, a new contract, or witnesses; the right applies only to revocable divorces although the opening is general.
TABRISI:2:228#4/r2.anchor: وفي هذا ما يدل على أن الزوج ينفرد بالمراجعة ولا يحتاج في ذلك إلى رضاء المرأة

TABRISI:2:228#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#4/r3.claim: Men used to divorce once, wait until the period nearly ended, revoke, and repeat the cycle before divorcing a third time, thereby harming the wife.
TABRISI:2:228#4/r3.anchor: وذلك أن الرجل كان إذا أراد الإضرار بامرأته طلقها واحدة وتركها

TABRISI:2:228#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#4/r4.claim: Revocation is permitted for reconciliation rather than harm, but this condition concerns permissibility, not legal effect; the community agrees the legal effects still apply when harm is intended.
TABRISI:2:228#4/r4.anchor: وإنما شرط الإصلاح في إباحة الرجعة لا في ثبوت أحكامها

TABRISI:2:228#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#4/r5.claim: This concise principle gives women rights corresponding to their obligations, governed by accepted standards of decent treatment.
TABRISI:2:228#4/r5.anchor: وهذا من الكلمات العجيبة الجامعة للفوائد

TABRISI:2:228#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#4/r6.claim: Women's rights include good companionship, freedom from harm, equitable division, maintenance, and clothing; the husband's include obedience, marital exclusivity, and preserving his paternity.
TABRISI:2:228#4/r6.anchor: كما أن للزوج حقوقا عليها مثل الطاعة التي أوجبها الله عليها له

TABRISI:2:228#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#4/r7.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:228#4/r7.claim: A report prompted by a woman identified as Muʿādh's wife says a husband must not strike his wife's face or insult her, and must feed and clothe her as he does himself and not abandon her.
TABRISI:2:228#4/r7.anchor: يا رسول الله ما حق الزوجة على زوجها

TABRISI:2:228#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#4/r8.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:228#4/r8.claim: The Prophet reminds men that they received women in God's trust; wives must preserve marital exclusivity, and husbands owe them customary maintenance and clothing, with any corrective strike non-injurious.
TABRISI:2:228#4/r8.anchor: وروي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

TABRISI:2:228#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#5/r1.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:2:228#5/r1.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say men's degree includes women's obedience, men's authority to dissolve the marriage, a larger inheritance share, and jihad.
TABRISI:2:228#5/r1.anchor: زيادة الميراث على قسم المرأة والجهاد هذا قول مجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:2:228#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:228#5/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the degree as a man's obligation to show extra generosity and not demand every right in full.
TABRISI:2:228#5/r2.anchor: جميع حقي ليكون لي عليها الفضيلة عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:228#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#5/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:228#5/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says women receive pleasure from men as men receive it from women, while men have a degree through spending and care.
TABRISI:2:228#5/r3.anchor: وله الفضل بنفقته وقيامه عليها عن الزجاج

TABRISI:2:228#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#5/r4.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
TABRISI:2:228#5/r4.claim: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm's tafsir says men's rights over women are greater than women's rights over men.
TABRISI:2:228#5/r4.anchor: وفي تفسير علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم قال: حق الرجال على النساء أفضل

TABRISI:2:228#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#5/r5.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:2:228#5/r5.claim: A report from al-Bāqir says a wife should obey her husband, seek permission for household charity, voluntary fasting, and leaving home, and not deny him sex; the husband's right is paramount, and the Prophet says he would have ordered prostration to him if it were permitted.
TABRISI:2:228#5/r5.anchor: وفي كتاب من لا يحضره الفقيه روي عن الباقر ع قال

TABRISI:2:228#6/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#6/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#6/r1.claim: God is powerful over whatever He wills, cannot be prevented or overcome, and acts according to wisdom.
TABRISI:2:228#6/r1.anchor: أي قادر على ما يشاء يمنع ولا يمنع ويقهر ولا يقهر

TABRISI:2:228#6/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#6/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#6/r2.claim: One view says the rule is abrogated for a woman divorced before consummation and for a pregnant divorcee by 33:49 and 65:4.
TABRISI:2:228#6/r2.anchor: وقد قيل في الآية إن المطلقة قبل الدخول والمطلقة الحاملة

TABRISI:2:228#6/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:228#6/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:228#6/r3.claim: Another view treats those two cases as specified exceptions to this verse rather than abrogated portions.
TABRISI:2:228#6/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنهما مخصوصتان من الآية كما ذكرناه في أول الآية

THALABI:v2p170/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p170/r1.speaker: من قال بهذا القول
THALABI:v2p170/r1.claim: Those who take qurʾ as menstruation say a divorced woman remains in her waiting period until the third menstruation ends; Ali says she cannot return to her husband until she bathes after it and prayer is permitted.
THALABI:v2p170/r1.anchor: فمن قال بهذا القول قال: لا تحل المرأة للأزواج ولا تخرج من عدتها ما لم تنقض الحيضة الثالثة

THALABI:v2p170/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p170/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وابن عمر وعائشة
THALABI:v2p170/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Umar, Aisha, Malik, al-Shafii, and the people of Medina take qurʾ as periods of purity, using the divorce instruction in 65:1 and the Prophet's direction to Ibn Umar as evidence.
THALABI:v2p170/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي الأطهار وهو قول زيد بن ثابت وابن عمر وعائشة ومذهب مالك والشافعي وأهل المدينة

THALABI:v2p170/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p170/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p170/r3.claim: When Ibn Umar divorced during menstruation, the Prophet told Umar to have him take her back, then divorce or keep her once she was pure, reciting 65:1 to show the waiting period starts in purity.
THALABI:v2p170/r3.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم- لما طلق ابن عمر امرأة وهي حائض- لعمر: مره فليراجعها

THALABI:v2p170/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p170/r4.speaker: علي
THALABI:v2p170/r4.claim: Ali says a man who divorces his wife once or twice cannot return to her until she has bathed after the third menstruation and prayer is permitted.
THALABI:v2p170/r4.anchor: ما روى الزهري عن ابن المسيب أن عليا قال في الرجل يطلق امرأته واحدة أو ثنتين: [لا] يحل لزوجها الرجعة إليها

THALABI:v2p170/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p170/r5.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v2p170/r5.claim: On the purity interpretation, Aisha says that once the divorced woman enters her third menstruation she is separated from her husband and may marry another; she explicitly defines qurʾ as purity, not menstruation.
THALABI:v2p170/r5.anchor: عن عائشة، قالت: إذا دخلت المطلقة في الحيضة الثالثة فقد بانت من زوجها وحلت للأزواج

THALABI:v2p170/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p170/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن
THALABI:v2p170/r6.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman says every jurist he encountered held Aisha's interpretation that the qurʾ are periods of purity.
THALABI:v2p170/r6.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر بن عبد الرحمن يقول: ما أدركت أحدا من فقهائنا

THALABI:v2p170/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p170/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p170/r7.claim: The disagreement arises because qurʾ is a contronym: Arabic uses it for menstruation and for purity, with أقرأت said of a woman in either state.
THALABI:v2p170/r7.anchor: وإنما وقع هذا الاختلاف لأن القرء في اللغة من الأضداد يصلح للمعنيين جميعا

THALABI:v2p170/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p170/r8.speaker: أبو عمر وأبو عبيدة
THALABI:v2p170/r8.claim: Abu Umar and Abu Ubayda derive qurʾ from a thing's appointed time of coming and going; al-A'sha's verse uses it of the purity missed while he campaigned away from his wives.
THALABI:v2p170/r8.anchor: فقال أبو عمر وأبو عبيدة هو وقت مجيء الشيء وذهابه

THALABI:v2p171/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171/r1.speaker: مالك بن الحارث الهذلي
THALABI:v2p171/r1.claim: Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali uses قاري for an appointed time, saying winds blow at their time.
THALABI:v2p171/r1.anchor: قال مالك بن الحرث الهذلي: كرهت العقر عقر بني شليل … إذا هبت لقارئها الرياح

THALABI:v2p171/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171/r2.claim: The source says the stars are said to أقرأت when they rise and when they set, further illustrating recurrent times.
THALABI:v2p171/r2.anchor: ويقال: أقرأت النجوم إذا طلعت، وأقرأت إذا أفلت.

THALABI:v2p171/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171/r3.speaker: كثير
THALABI:v2p171/r3.claim: Kathir's line uses أقرأت of the Pleiades setting, showing another recurrent appointed time.
THALABI:v2p171/r3.anchor: قال كثير: إذا ما الثريا وقد أقرأت

THALABI:v2p171/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171/r4.claim: On this derivation, qurʾ works for both menstruation and purity because each comes at an appointed time.
THALABI:v2p171/r4.anchor: فالقرء للوجهين، لأن الحيض يأتي لوقت والطهر يأتي لوقت

THALABI:v2p171/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171/r5.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v2p171/r5.claim: An alternative etymology derives qurʾ from gathering; it compares the term with water collected in a basin and a womb enclosing a fetus.

THALABI:v2p171/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171/r6.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
THALABI:v2p171/r6.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum's line uses لم تقرأ جنينا for a woman who has not conceived or gathered an embryo in her womb; Arabs say a camel has not gathered a fetus.
THALABI:v2p171/r6.anchor:
قال عمرو بن كلثوم:
ذراعي عيطل إذماء بكر … هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

THALABI:v2p171/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171/r7.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v2p171/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj chooses this etymology and connects it to qara'tu water in a basin; qurʾ is retained, gathered blood in either purity or menstruation, with purity preferred because it holds blood back while menstruation releases it.
THALABI:v2p171/r7.anchor: هذا اختيار الزجاج. قال: ومنه قريت الماء في المقراة، ترك همزها والأصل فيه الهمز

THALABI:v2p171/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171/r8.claim: Qurʾ is blood held together: it can describe menstruation or purity, but purity is stronger because it gathers and retains blood while menstruation releases it.
THALABI:v2p171/r8.anchor: فالقرء احتباس الدم واجتماعه وهو يكون في حال الطهر والحيض جميعا، إلا أن الترجيح للطهر لأنه يجمع الدم ويحبسه

THALABI:v2p171#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171#2/r1.claim: The verse is phrased as a report but functions as a command, like the instruction that mothers nurse their children.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن لفظها خبر ومعناها أمر،

THALABI:v2p171#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171#2/r2.claim: A menstruating divorcee waits three qurūʾ; a pregnant divorcee until delivery; a premenarchal or postmenopausal divorcee three months; pregnant widows until delivery, and other widows four months and ten days.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r2.anchor: والعدة على ضربين: عدة المطلقة وعدة المتوفى عنها زوجها،

THALABI:v2p171#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171#2/r3.claim: Enslaved women's applicable waiting periods are half of a free woman's, so their menstrual waiting period is two qurūʾ; an unconsummated divorce entails no waiting period.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r3.anchor: وعدة الإماء فيما له نصف ومن الأقراء قرآن

THALABI:v2p171#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة وإبراهيم
THALABI:v2p171#2/r4.claim: Ikrima and Ibrahim take what God created in the wombs to mean menstrual blood.

THALABI:v2p171#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل
THALABI:v2p171#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Muqatil take the phrase to mean a child, that is, pregnancy.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r5.anchor: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل: يعني الحمل في الولد،

THALABI:v2p171#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171#2/r6.claim: Women must not hide menstruation or pregnancy to defeat a husband's right of return or a child's claim; a woman is trusted about her sexual parts.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r6.anchor: فمعنى الآية لا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن من الحيض والحمل

THALABI:v2p171#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171#2/r7.claim: Buʿūla means husbands, plural of baʿl; baʿl originally means master or owner, and the husband is so called for managing his wife's affairs. The verse about worshipping Baal is cited.

THALABI:v2p171#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r8.speaker: مسلم بن محارب
THALABI:v2p171#2/r8.claim: Muslim ibn Muharib reads the tāʾ in buʿūlatuhunna with sukūn because of the succession of vowelled sounds.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ مسلم بن محارب وبعولتهن بإسكان التاء لكثرة الحركات،

THALABI:v2p171#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171#2/r9.claim: Thaʿlabī prefers the usual vocalized form as more eloquent, fitting, and sound.

THALABI:v2p171#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171#2/r10.claim: A husband may return his wife during her waiting period if he seeks reconciliation; he must not use repeated return near the end of the period to harm her.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r10.anchor: أحق أولى بردهن أي برجعتهن في ذلك أي في حال العدة إن أرادوا إصلاحا

THALABI:v2p171#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p171#2/r11.claim: Women have rights over their husbands corresponding to the rights husbands have over them, according to proper custom.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r11.anchor: ولهن أي وللنساء على أزواجهن مثل الذي عليهن من الحق

THALABI:v2p171#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p171#2/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p171#2/r12.claim: Asked about a wife's rights, the Prophet says her husband must not strike her face or insult her, must feed and clothe her as he does himself, and must not abandon her.
THALABI:v2p171#2/r12.anchor: يروى أن امرأة معاذ قالت: يا رسول الله ما حق الزوجة على زوجها؟

THALABI:v2p172/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p172/r1.claim: The Prophet urges kind treatment of women, describing them as dependent wards entrusted to husbands by God's trust and made lawful through God's word.
THALABI:v2p172/r1.anchor: المبارك بن فضالة عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «استوصوا

THALABI:v2p172/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p172/r2.claim: In a report from Maimuna, the Prophet praises spouses who serve one another: wives who comply except in sin receive the stated reward of a thousand martyrs, and gentle husbands the reward of a hundred.
THALABI:v2p172/r2.anchor: وعن ميمونة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

THALABI:v2p172/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p172/r3.claim: Answering Umar, the Prophet says women may surpass men in reward, a wife's contentment and prayer elevate her husband, and betraying him is grave after shirk; he warns about orphans and women and equates wives' rights with his own.
THALABI:v2p172/r3.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب (رضي الله عنه) : يا رسول الله فكيف يكون للمرأة

THALABI:v2p172/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p172/r4.claim: Thaʿlabī glosses the men's degree over women as superiority in merit.
THALABI:v2p172/r4.anchor: بالمعروف وللرجال عليهن درجة في الفضل

THALABI:v2p172/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p172/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the degree by the dowry and financial support a man provides his wife.
THALABI:v2p172/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بما ساق إليها من المهر،

THALABI:v2p172/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r6.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v2p172/r6.claim: One reported view explains the degree as a difference in intellect.
THALABI:v2p172/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بما ساق إليها من المهر، وأنفق عليها من المال، وقيل: بالعقل،

THALABI:v2p172/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r7.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v2p172/r7.claim: Another reported view explains the degree by inheritance.
THALABI:v2p172/r7.anchor: وقيل: بالعقل، وقيل: بالميراث، وقيل: بالدرجة،

THALABI:v2p172/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r8.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v2p172/r8.claim: A further reported view says the degree itself is the explanation.
THALABI:v2p172/r8.anchor: وقيل: بالميراث، وقيل: بالدرجة، قال قتادة: بالجهاد.

THALABI:v2p172/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r9.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v2p172/r9.claim: Qatada identifies the men's degree with jihad.
THALABI:v2p172/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: بالجهاد. عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي

THALABI:v2p172/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p172/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p172/r10.claim: A woman representing women asks about their reward when men fight and die; the Prophet replies that obedience to husbands and recognition of their rights equal that service, though few women do so.
THALABI:v2p172/r10.anchor: عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: بينما نحن عند رسول الله

THALABI:v2p173/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p173/r1.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v2p173/r1.claim: Anas reports that women came to the Prophet saying men had gained virtue through jihad and asking what deed remained for women in God's path.
THALABI:v2p173/r1.anchor: ثابت عن أنس، قال: جئن إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلن:

THALABI:v2p173/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p173/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p173/r2.claim: Asked whether women have jihad, the Prophet calls their jihad guarding their zeal and struggling against themselves; patient women are fighters and garrisoned, with two rewards.
THALABI:v2p173/r2.anchor: عن عمران بن الحصين قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل على النساء جهاد؟

THALABI:v2p173/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p173/r3.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v2p173/r3.claim: One view explains the men's degree as divorce and return.

THALABI:v2p173/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p173/r4.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v2p173/r4.claim: Another view explains the degree as testimony.

THALABI:v2p173/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p173/r5.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v2p173/r5.claim: Another view explains the degree as strength in worship.

THALABI:v2p173/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p173/r6.speaker: سفيان وزيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v2p173/r6.claim: Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam explain the degree as authority or governance.
THALABI:v2p173/r6.anchor: وقال سفيان وزيد بن أسلم: بالإمارة.

THALABI:v2p173/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p173/r7.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v2p173/r7.claim: Al-Qutaybi says the degree means a virtue or advantage concerning rights.
THALABI:v2p173/r7.anchor: وقال القتيبي: معناه: وللرجال عليهن درجة أي فضيلة للحق.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r1.claim: Al-mutallaqat are women released from their husbands' bonds; the verse concerns adult, consummated, nonpregnant divorcees whose waiting period is being explained.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r1.anchor: المطلقات: المخليات من حبال الأزواج (¬5) (¬6)، أراد المطلقات المدخول بهن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r2.claim: They must wait for three quruʾ to pass and not marry during that interval.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r2.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أنهن ينتظرن بأنفسهن (¬7) انقضاء ثلاثة قروء أو مضي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r3.claim: The wording is declarative in form but imperative in sense, as with the command that mothers nurse their children.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r3.anchor: لفظه خبر ومعناه الأمر، كقوله: {يرضعن أولادهن} [البقرة: 233]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj compares the declarative command to saying a dirham suffices, whose intended force is to be content with a dirham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: هو كما تقول: حسبك درهم، لفظه خبر ومعناه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r5.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r5.claim: Another explanation supplies the ellipsis: they wait under God's ruling, which He made obligatory for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: معناه (¬1): يتربصن في حكم الله الذي أوجبه، فحذف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r6.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r6.claim: Another grammatical explanation is that the lām of the imperative form ليتربصن has been omitted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r7.claim: Quruʾ is the plural of qarʾ; its few plural is aqruʾ, while its many plurals are aqraʾ and quruʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r7.anchor: والقروء: جمع قرء (¬4)، وجمعه القليل أقرء، والكثير: أقراء وقروء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r8.speaker: يونس وأبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r8.claim: Yunus, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, and Abu Ubayd treat qarʾ as a word with opposite senses: menstruation and purity, in both Arabic usage and religious law.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا يونس (¬6) وأبو عمرو بن العلاء (¬7) (¬8) وأبو عبيد أنها من الأضداد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r9.speaker: الراجز
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r9.claim: The rajaz poet's line shows that quruʾ can mean menstrual periods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r9.anchor: أنشد الأئمة حجة للحيض قول الراجز: له قروء كقروء الحائض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r10.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r10.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line supports quruʾ meaning purity intervals: the man left on campaign and did not have intercourse with his wives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r10.anchor: وأنشدوا حجة للطهر قول الأعشى: ما ضاع فيها من قروء نسائكا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r11.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r11.claim: The Prophet's instruction to a woman with irregular bleeding to wait through her usual menstruation days and wash afterward shows that aqraʾ can mean menstruation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r11.anchor: فقال (¬6) النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في المستحاضة "تنتظر (¬7) أيام أقرائها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r12.claim: Here quruʾ means three purity intervals: the command to divorce for the waiting period and the Prophet's instruction to Ibn Umar show divorce at purity so the waiting period begins prospectively.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r12.anchor: وأما استعمال الشرع إياها في الأطهار، فقوله تعالى: {يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r13.claim: The word's two Arabic senses explain why Companions and jurists disagreed about the waiting period.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p208/r13.anchor: ومن هذا الاختلاف في اللغة وقع الخلاف في الأقراء بين الصحابة وفقهاء الأمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq says qarʾ means gathering: menstrual blood gathers in the womb, and this gathering occurs during purity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: والذي عندي في حقيقة هذا أن القرء الجمع (¬8) في اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r2.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says three quruʾ is irregular: the measure should be three aqruʾ, because quruʾ is the many plural, as three aflus precedes fulus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r2.anchor: ذكر أبو حاتم عن الأصمعي أنه قال في قوله: {ثلاثة قروء}: جاء هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r3.claim: Abu Hatim says grammarians understand an omitted partitive phrase: three of the quruʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r3.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: وقال النحويون في هذا: أراد ثلاثة من القروء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r4.claim: The people of linguistic interpretation explain the many plural as signaling that this rule applies to numerous divorcees, though each is assigned three at a time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r4.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: لما كانت كل مطلقة يلزمها (¬8) هذا، دخله معنى الكثرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r5.speaker: من قال إن القرء حيض
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r5.claim: Those who take qarʾ as menstruation say a woman does not leave her waiting period until her third menstrual period has ended.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r5.anchor: فمن قال: القرء: الحيض، قال: لا تخرج المرأة من عدتها ما لم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r6.speaker: من قال إن القرء الأطهار
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r6.claim: Those who take quruʾ as purity say a divorce during menstruation does not count the partial interval, while divorce during purity counts its remainder as one interval followed by two complete ones.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p214/r6.anchor: ومن قال: إنها الأطهار، قال: إن طلقها في خلال الحيض لم يحتسب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r1.claim: The womb is the place where a child originates and the vessel that holds it in the abdomen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r1.anchor: الرحم: منبت الولد ووعاؤه في البطن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r2.speaker: عكرمة وإبراهيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r2.claim: Ikrima and Ibrahim interpret what is in the womb as menstruation, in the case of a woman claiming her third period has passed to prevent her husband from returning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة (¬3) وإبراهيم (¬4): يعنى: الحيض، وهو أن تكون المرأة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Muqatil interpret it as pregnancy and the child; concealment could defeat a husband's right of return or the child's rights.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬5) وقتادة (¬6) ومقاتل (¬7): يعنى: الحبل والولد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r4.claim: The author prefers pregnancy and the child because what God creates in wombs points more directly to a child than to menstruation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r4.anchor: وهذا القول أولى؛ لأن قوله: {ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} أدل على الولد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r5.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that a wicked wife may conceal pregnancy because she longs for her husband and wants to prolong the waiting period; a pregnant woman's period ends at childbirth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p216/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولا يحل لهن} الآية، وذلك أن المرأة السوء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r1.claim: This means that a believer is expected to act this way; the obligation is not limited to believers alone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r1.anchor: معناه: من كان مؤمنا (¬3) بالله واليوم الآخر (¬4) فهذه صفته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq compares it to telling a wrongdoer that if he is a believer he should not wrong the speaker; faith should restrain the wrong.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r2.anchor: قال (¬5) أبو إسحاق: وهذا كما تقول للرجل يظلم (¬6): إن كنت مؤمنا فلا تظلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r3.claim: Women must disclose what is in their wombs, since only they know it; concealment is sinful betrayal, a plausible declaration is accepted, and a suspected woman must swear an oath.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p217/r3.anchor: وفي هذه الآية أمر متوجه على النساء في إظهار ما يخلق (¬8) الله في أرحامهن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r1.claim: Baʿula is a collective plural of baʿl, like fuḥula, dhukura, khuʾula, and ʿumuma; its feminine tāʾ reinforces the group's grammatical femininity and is only used in attested forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r1.anchor: البعولة: جمع بعل، كالفحولة والذكورة والخؤولة والعمومة، وهذه الهاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r2.speaker: يعقوب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r2.claim: Baʿula is also the verbal noun of baʿala, becoming a husband, as Yaʿqub's poetic line uses the verb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r2.anchor: والبعولة أيضا: مصدر البعل، يقال: بعل الرجل يبعل بعولة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r3.speaker: الحطيئة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r3.claim: Baʿal and tubāʿil can refer to intercourse or a husband's play with his wife; al-Hutayʾa uses tubāʿil in a line about a wife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r3.anchor: ومن هذا يقال (¬5) للجماع وملاعبة الرجل أهله: بعال، يقال للمرأة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r4.claim: A woman praised for good tabaʿʿul treats her husband well; the author also cites a hadith about women excelling in their treatment of husbands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r4.anchor: وامرأة حسنة التبعل: إذا كانت تحسن عشرة زوجها. ومنه الحديث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r5.claim: Their husbands have the stronger right to restore them to marriage during the period in which they have been commanded to wait.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p218/r5.anchor: ومعنى {أحق بردهن}، أي: إلى النكاح والزوجية، يعني: أحق بمراجعتهن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r1.claim: The condition excludes harm: in pre-Islamic practice a husband repeatedly divorced and returned his wife near the end of each waiting period to prolong her distress; return is allowed for reconciliation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r1.anchor: {إن أرادوا إصلاحا} لا إضرارا، وذلك أن الرجل في الجاهلية إذا أراد الإضرار بامرأته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r2.claim: A husband may revoke without a guardian, her consent, or a newly specified dowry; the remaining waiting period ends and intercourse is immediately lawful, with witnesses recommended as a precaution and return expressed by words such as I have returned you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r2.anchor: ويستغني الزوج في المراجعة عن الولي وعن رضاها وعن تسمية مهر، وإذا راجعها سقطت بقية العدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r3.claim: Women have rights over men comparable to the rights men have over them, in the recognized manner and under the duties God has prescribed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف} أي: للنساء على الرجال مثل الذي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says he adorns himself for his wife just as she adorns herself for him, citing the verse's reciprocity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p219/r4.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: إني لأتزين لامرأتي كما تتزين لي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r1.claim: The root associations of rajul and related forms indicate strength: a powerful man or horse, forceful speech, and daylight gaining strength.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r1.anchor: يقال: رجل بين الرجلة (¬3)، أي: القوة، وهو أرجل الرجلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r2.claim: Daraja means rank or level and derives from progressing, folding, or passing away step by step; a road's passage is also called a madraja.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r2.anchor: والدرجة: المنزلة، وأصلها من درجت الشيء أدرجه درجا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains men's degree as the dowry they provide and the money they spend on their wives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بما ساق إليها من المهر، وأنفق عليها من المال (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r4.speaker: قيل بالعقل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r4.claim: One reported explanation says the degree is men's greater reason or intellect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r4.anchor: وأما المعنى (¬3) فقال ابن عباس: بما ساق إليها من المهر، وأنفق عليها من المال (¬4). وقيل: بالعقل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r5.speaker: قيل بالدية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r5.claim: Another reported explanation says the degree concerns blood money.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r5.anchor: وقيل: بالعقل. وقيل: بالدية. وقيل: بالميراث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r6.speaker: قيل بالميراث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r6.claim: Another reported explanation says the degree concerns inheritance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r6.anchor: وقيل: بالدية. وقيل: بالميراث (¬5). وقال قتادة: بالجهاد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r7.claim: Qatada explains men's degree as jihad.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq says women receive pleasure from men as men do from women, while men have the advantage of providing maintenance and care.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p220/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: المعنى: أن المرأة تنال من اللذة من الرجل، كما ينال الرجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p221/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p221/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p221/r1.claim: God is sovereign, commands and tests as He wills, and does so only with profound wisdom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p221/r1.anchor: أي: مالك يأمر كما أراد، ويمتحن كما أحب، ولا يكون ذلك إلا عن حكمة بالغة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r1.claim: These divorced women are adults whose marriages were consummated and who are not pregnant; the verse specifies their waiting period.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r1.anchor: { والمطلقات } أي: المخليات من حبال الأزواج. يعني: البالغات المدخول بهن غير الحوامل؛ لأن في الآية بيان عدتهن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r2.claim: The author understands qurūʾ as periods of purity, waiting until three such periods pass.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r2.anchor: { يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء } أي: ثلاثة أطهار، يعني: ينتظرن انقضاء مدة ثلاثة أطهار حتى تمر عليهن ثلاثة أطهار،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r3.claim: An alternative reported interpretation takes qurūʾ to mean three menstruations.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r3.anchor: حتى تمر عليهن ثلاثة أطهار، وقيل: ثلاث حيض.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r4.claim: What women must not conceal is a child in the womb, which they might hide to nullify the husband's right of return.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r4.anchor: { ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن } يعني: الولد؛ ليبطلن حق الزوج من الرجعة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r5.claim: The appeal to faith is a severe warning to disclose what is in the womb.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r5.anchor: { إن كن يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر } وهذا تغليظ عليهن في إظهار ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r6.claim: Their husbands have the right to take them back by revocation during the prescribed waiting period, if they seek reconciliation and not harm.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r6.anchor: بمراجعتهن { في ذلك } في الأجل الذي أمرن أن يتربصن فيه { إن أرادوا إصلاحا } لا إضرارا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r7.claim: Women have customary rights corresponding to men's rights, according to what God commands regarding a husband's rights over his wife.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r7.anchor: للنساء على الرجال مثل الذي للرجال عليهن من الحق بالمعروف، أي: بما أمر الله من حق الرجل على المرأة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r8.claim: Men have a degree over women because they paid the dowry and spend money.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r8.anchor: { وللرجال عليهن درجة } يعني: بما ساقوا من المهر، وأنفقوا من المال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r9.claim: God commands as He wills and tests as He wills.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:228/r9.anchor: { والله عزيز حكيم } يأمر كما أراد ويمتحن كما أحب.

ELMALILI:2:228/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r1.claim: The general category of divorced women is qualified by other texts to exclude menopausal, pregnant, unconsummated, minor, and enslaved women.
ELMALILI:2:228/r1.anchor: Âise, zât-ı haml, gayr-i medhûlün bihâ, sağīre ve câriye diğer nusûs ile bu umumdan muhassastırlar.

ELMALILI:2:228/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r2.claim: Qurūʾ, plural of qarʾ, has the opposed senses of menstruation and purity, making it a shared, ambiguous term whose intended sense must be determined.
ELMALILI:2:228/r2.anchor: “Kurû’” ve “akrâ’” قَرْء’ın cem‘idir ki ezdâddan olarak hayz ve tuhr mânaları beyninde lafz-ı müşterektir. Binâen‘aleyh mücmeldir.

ELMALILI:2:228/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r3.speaker: İmam Mâlik ve Şâfiî
ELMALILI:2:228/r3.claim: Mālik and Shāfiʿī interpret qurūʾ as periods of purity.
ELMALILI:2:228/r3.anchor: İmam Mâlik ve Şâfiî bunu tuhr ile tefsir etmişler

ELMALILI:2:228/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r4.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
ELMALILI:2:228/r4.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha, cited from Abū Dāwūd and Tirmidhī, attributes to the Prophet that a slave woman's divorce is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstruations; Elmalılı uses it to support the menstrual sense.
ELMALILI:2:228/r4.anchor: Ebû Dâvûd ve Tirmizî’de tahric olunduğu üzere Hazret-i Âişe’den rivayet olunan

ELMALILI:2:228/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r5.speaker: İbn Ömer
ELMALILI:2:228/r5.claim: A second Prophetic report, narrated by Imām Shāfiʿī from Ibn ʿUmar, likewise supports the menstrual interpretation.
ELMALILI:2:228/r5.anchor: buna mutâbık olarak İbn Ömer’den İmam Şâfiî hazretlerinin dahi rivayet eylediği diğer hadîs-i nebevî

ELMALILI:2:228/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r6.claim: Elmalılı adopts the Ḥanafī interpretation of qurūʾ as menstruation, supported by the purpose of establishing that the womb is clear and by further juristic proofs.
ELMALILI:2:228/r6.anchor: kütüb-i fıkhiyede mübeyyen olan daha bazı müeyyidâta binâen eimme-i Hanefiyye bunu hayz ile tefsir etmiştir

ELMALILI:2:228/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r7.speaker: Hulefâ-i Râşidîn, Âbâdile, Übey b. Ka‘b, Muâz b. Cebel, Ebü’d-Derdâ, Ubâde b. Sâmit, Zeyd b. Sâbit, Ebû Mûse’l-Eş‘arî ve Ma‘bed-i Cühenî
ELMALILI:2:228/r7.claim: The same interpretation of qurūʾ as menstruation is also attributed to these early authorities.
ELMALILI:2:228/r7.anchor: Hulefâ-i Râşidîn, Âbâdile, Übey b. Ka‘b, Muâz b. Cebel, Ebü’d-Derdâ, Ubâde b. Sâmit, Zeyd b. Sâbit, Ebû Mûse’l-Eş‘arî ve Ma‘bed-i Cühenî radıyallahu ‘anhüm hazerâtının kavilleri de budur.

ELMALILI:2:228/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r8.claim: A free, adult divorced woman must wait until she has completed three menstrual periods.
ELMALILI:2:228/r8.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh hür ve bâliğa olan mutallakalar tam üç âdet görünceye kadar nefislerini zapt edip bekleyeceklerdir.

ELMALILI:2:228/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r9.claim: A woman must not conceal menstruation or pregnancy; if she believes in God and the Last Day she should disclose it truthfully, and her statement governs this matter.
ELMALILI:2:228/r9.anchor: ve onlara Allah teâlâ’nın rahimlerinde halk ettiği hayz veya haml her ne ise onu ketm etmeleri câiz olmaz ve saklamakla intifâ‘a kalkışmaları helâl olmaz

ELMALILI:2:228/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r10.claim: Baʿl can name an idol once worshipped or, with the sense of height, a lord, owner, master, husband, or wife; attached to men it means wives, and to women it means their current husbands.
ELMALILI:2:228/r10.anchor: Ba‘l bir zamanlar perestiş edilen bir putun ismi olduğu gibi yükseklik mazmûnuyla seyyid ve mâlik, yani efendi ve zevc ve zevce mânalarına da gelir.

ELMALILI:2:228/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r11.claim: During the waiting period, husbands who divorced revocably retain their status and have the strongest right to take their wives back; even if she objects, the husband's decision prevails.
ELMALILI:2:228/r11.anchor: O hâlde meâli: Ve o mutallakaların efendileri, yani onları boşayan ve fakat talâk-ı ric‘î ile boşayıp henüz efendiliğini muhafaza eden kocaları

ELMALILI:2:228/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r12.claim: The return is permitted when the husbands seek reconciliation rather than harm or separation; this is legally shown by having issued a revocable rather than irrevocable divorce.
ELMALILI:2:228/r12.anchor: Eğer o efendiler aile beyninde bir ıslah isterler, ızrar ve beynûnet fikrinde bulunmazlarsa bunu yapabilirler

ELMALILI:2:228/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r13.claim: A husband's hidden intention to prolong the waiting period in order to harm his wife merits divine accountability under 2:225.
ELMALILI:2:228/r13.anchor: sırf kalbî olan bu noktada وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ [el-Bakara 2/225] medlûlünce muâhaze-i ilâhiyeye müstahık olurlar

ELMALILI:2:228/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r14.claim: Women have reciprocal rights against men according to recognized good custom, illustrated by verses on kind treatment, fair retention or release, support, guardianship, dowry, and equitable marital treatment.
ELMALILI:2:228/r14.anchor: vechile, yani tanınması ve muhafaza edilmesi vâcib hukūk mevcuddur ki bunlar müte‘addid âyetlerde beyan olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:228/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r15.claim: The general rule on reciprocal rights entails that if no dower was named at marriage, a dower matching her peers is still due.
ELMALILI:2:228/r15.anchor: İmdi bu hükmün umûmu içinde şu da anlaşılıyor ki hîn-i nikâhta mehir tesmiye edilmemiş ise mehr-i misil de lâzım gelir.

ELMALILI:2:228/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r16.claim: The husband's additional degree corresponds to his duties to protect, manage, and support the family and carry its expenses; he must not abuse this distinction.
ELMALILI:2:228/r16.anchor: erkekler kadınlara müşârik olmakla beraber üzerlerinde bulunurlar, onları ve ellerindekini gözetir, muhafaza ederler, idare ve infak eylerler

ELMALILI:2:228/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:228/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:228/r17.claim: God is mighty and wise: He punishes those who oppose His rulings, which are filled with wisdom and benefits.
ELMALILI:2:228/r17.anchor: Allah da Azîz, Hakîm’dir. Ahkâmına muhalefet edenlerden intikāmını alır ve onun ahkâmı hikem ü mesâlih ile doludur.

QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r1.claim: When the marital bond is severed, the spouses must not conceal the lineage God established.
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r1.anchor: يعني إن انقطع بينكما السبب فلا تقطعوا ما أثبت الله من النسب

QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r2.claim: The former husband has the stronger right to restore the marriage because of their prior companionship and the rupture in the union.
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r2.anchor: من سبق له الصحبة فهو أحق بالرجعة لما وقع في النكاح من الثلمة

QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r3.claim: Reconciliation must aim to repair the estrangement, not prolong the waiting period before divorcing her again.
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r3.anchor: أن يكون القصد بالرجعة استدراك ما حصل من الجفاء لا تطويل العدة عليها

QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r4.claim: The husband's right includes what he spent, while the wife's corresponding right is service for what has passed between them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r4.anchor: إن كان له عليها حق ما أنفق من المال فلها حق الخدمة لما سلف من الحال

QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r5.claim: Men have a degree of excellence, while women have a distinguishing merit in weakness and human incapacity.
QUSHAYRI:v1p106/r5.anchor: في الفضيلة ، ولهن مزية في الضعف وعجز البشرية

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r1.claim: Marriage ends through a husband’s divorce, judicial separation on an injured party’s application, khulʿ for payment by the wife, death, apostasy, or a newly arising marriage impediment; this verse group discusses divorce and khulʿ.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r1.anchor: İslâm’da evlilik hayatını sona erdiren beş tasarruf ve olay vardır: a) İlke olarak kocanın boşaması (talâk); b) sebepleri bulununca zarar gören tarafın başvurusu üzerine hakemlerin veya hakimin evliliğe son vermesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r2.claim: Iddat is the period that must pass after a marriage-ending event before a woman may marry again.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r2.anchor: Evliliği sona erdiren sebeplerden biri oluşunca kadının yeni bir evlilik yapabilmesi için aradan bir sürenin geçmesi gerekir ki buna iddet denilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r3.claim: The only women exempt from iddat are those divorced without sexual intercourse.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r3.anchor: İddetten muaf olanlar yalnızca cinsel ilişkide bulunulmadan boşanan kadınlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r4.claim: A pregnant divorcee’s iddat ends at childbirth, a woman who does not menstruate counts months, and a menstruating woman waits three qurūʾ.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r4.anchor: Boşanmış hâmile kadınların iddeti doğumla, herhangi bir sebeple aybaşı görmeyen kadınların iddeti ay hesabıyla olur (Talâk 65/4).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r5.claim: Qurʾ in Arabic denotes the transition boundary from menstruation to purity or from purity to menstruation, explaining juristic disagreement over its sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r5.anchor: “Aybaşı” olarak tercüme ettiğimiz “el-kur’u” kelimesi Arapça’da ay halinden temizliğe ve temizlikten aybaşı haline geçişi (geçiş sınırı) ifade ettiği için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r6.speaker: hayız mânası veren müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r6.claim: Some jurists understand qurʾ as menstruation, hayḍ.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r7.speaker: temizlik mânası veren müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r7.claim: Other jurists understand qurʾ as purity, tuhr.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r8.claim: A divorce conforming to the Sunnah takes place only while the woman is in a state of purity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r8.anchor: İslâm’da sünnete uygun boşama ancak kadın temizlik halinde iken yapılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r9.speaker: temizlik mânası veren müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r9.claim: On the purity interpretation, the purity days in which divorce occurs count as one qurʾ, shortening iddat.
