KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r9.anchor: Kelimeye temizlik mânası verenlere göre, içinde boşama yapılan temizlik günlerini bir kur’ saydıkları için iddet kısalır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r10.speaker: hayız mânası veren müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r10.claim: On the menstruation interpretation, iddat begins with the menstruation after the purity period, making the wait somewhat longer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r10.anchor: Hayız mânası verenlere göre ise iddet temizliği takip eden hayızla başlayacağı için biraz daha uzar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r11.claim: Iddat helps establish whether the woman is pregnant and gives the couple time to reflect calmly and resume married life if they see hope.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r11.anchor: İddetin gerekçeleri arasında kadının hâmile olup olmadığının anlaşılması ve boşayan koca ile boşanan kadının salim kafa ile düşünüp taşınmalarının, ümit görüyorlarsa tekrar evlilik hayatına dönmelerinin temini vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r12.claim: Jurists who calculate iddat by menstruation extend the period as a precaution that can help prevent the family from breaking up.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r12.anchor: İddeti hayızla hesaplayarak süreyi uzatan müctehidler, ailenin yıkılmamasına yardımcı olabilecek ihtiyatı ve tedbiri tercih etmiş olmaktadırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r13.claim: Iddat is calculated by childbirth, menstruation, or months; pregnancy and cessation of menstruation can be established by signs and, when needed, examination.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r13.anchor: İddet, doğum, hayız ve aylarla hesaplanmaktadır. Hâmilelik, ay halinin kesilmesi ve gerektiğinde muayene ile anlaşılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r14.claim: Believing women are urged to tell the truth and not conceal the conditions God has created in their wombs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r14.anchor: mümin kadınlar bu konularda doğru söylemeye, Allah’ın kendilerinde yarattığı bu durumları gizlememeye teşvik edilmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r15.claim: If the husband sincerely wants reconciliation before iddat ends and has not used all three divorces, a revocable divorce allows return by words or sexual relations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r15.anchor: Kadınlar henüz iddetlerini tamamlamamış ve kocalar da üç boşama haklarını kullanmamış olurlarsa, yani ric‘î denilen dönüşü mümkün boşamalarda, söz veya cinsel ilişki gibi fiille evliliğe dönmek mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r16.claim: After iddat ends, a woman not divorced for the third time can return to married life only if she agrees, with a newly specified mahr and marriage contract.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r16.anchor: Boşanmış kadınlar iddetlerini tamamlamış olurlarsa –üçüncü defa boşanmamış bulunan kadınlarla– yeniden evlilik hayatına dönebilmek için kadının da bunu istemesi gerekir ve yeniden mehir belirlenerek nikâh kıyılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r17.claim: Absent an important legitimate impediment, the former husband receives priority because of family life, children’s and relatives’ rights, and their shared married history.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r17.anchor: ortada önemli ve meşrû bir engel bulunmadığı takdirde aile hayatına saygı, çoluk çocuğun ve yakınların hakları, uzun veya kısa müddet paylaşılmış bulunan evlilik hayatı göz önüne alınmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r18.claim: Many pre-Islamic religions and cultures treated women as inferior in personhood and in rights and duties; Jahiliyya Arabs likewise left women’s rights to men’s wishes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r18.anchor: İslâm’dan önceki birçok dinde ve kültürde kadın cinsinin, hem insan olarak hem de haklar ve ödevler bakımından erkeğe nisbetle ikinci sınıf bir varlık olarak kabul edildiği bilinmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r19.speaker: Hz. Ömer
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r19.claim: Umar recalled that in Jahiliyya men did not regard women as significant until God revealed verses about them and granted them rights.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r19.anchor: Hz. Ömer bu tarihî gerçeği şöyle dile getirmiştir: “Câhiliye devrinde biz kadınları bir şey saymaz, hesaba katmazdık; bu durum Allah Teâlâ’nın onlar hakkında âyetler indirmesine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r20.claim: The rule that women have rights corresponding to their duties was an exceptional human-rights and women’s-rights charter in its historical setting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r20.anchor: “Kadınların da ödevlerine denk haklarının bulunduğunu” bildiren âyet, özellikle o günün şartları dikkate alınırsa eşi bulunmaz bir “insan hakkı” kuralı ve “kadın hakları vesikası”dır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r21.claim: Women are not absolutely identical to men in rights; the relation between their rights is one of likeness and equivalence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r21.anchor: Kadın haklar bakımından erkeğe mutlak anlamda eşit değildir; her ikisinin hakları arasındaki nisbet “benzerlik ve denklik”tir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r22.claim: Rights and duties not fixed by scripture may be adjusted as social conditions and publicly accepted standards of legitimacy change.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r22.anchor: Nasların değişmez kıldıklarının dışında kalan haklar ve ödevlerin değişim ve dengesi sosyal şartlara ve kamu vicdanındaki meşruiyet ölçülerine (ma‘rûf) göre ayarlanabilecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r23.claim: The verse also states that men have a one-degree surplus in rights when the respective rights and duties are compared.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r23.anchor: Haklar ve ödevler karşılaştırıldıkları zaman erkeklerin haklarında bir derecelik fazlalık bulunduğu görülecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r24.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r24.claim: Institutions from families to states require management, which in turn requires balanced and defined rights, authority, duties, and responsibilities between those who govern and those governed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r24.anchor: Devletten aileye kadar bütün kurumlarda düzen bir yönetimi, yönetim ise yöneten ve yönetilenlerin karşılıklı hak, salâhiyet, ödev ve sorumluluklarının belli ve dengeli kılınmasını gerekli kılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r25.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r25.claim: Women and men are equal in humanity and in rights and duties that derive from being human and servants of God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r25.anchor: Kadını ve erkeği ile bütün insanlar insanlıkta ve insanlığa bağlı haklarla yükümlülüklerde eşittirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r26.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r26.claim: For distinct social roles required by organization and division of labor, balance, justice, fairness, competence, and ability guide instead of identical treatment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r26.anchor: Yönetimin ve düzenin gerektirdiği iş bölümüne ve farklı rollere gelindiğinde eşitlik yerine “denge, adalet, hakkaniyet, ehliyet, kabiliyet” gibi değer ve kriterler devreye girer

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r27.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r27.claim: Claims that women are inferior to men in humanity or servanthood either lack sound religious authority or rest on misunderstanding and misinterpretation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r27.anchor: Kadınların insanlık ve kullukta erkeklerden aşağı derecede veya geri olduklarını ifade eden bütün söylemler ya dinî kaynakları bakımından sahih değildir ya da yanlış anlaşılmış ve yorumlanmışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r28.claim: For rights and obligations tied to distinct institutional and social roles, the measure is balance and corresponding equivalence rather than identical equality.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r28.anchor: Kurumlar ve toplum içindeki farklı rollere bağlı haklar ve yükümlülüklere gelindiğinde ise kadınlarla erkekler arasında eşitlik değil, dengeli ve erkek hakkının dengi, misli olma ölçüsü vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r29.claim: Examples of reciprocal duties include the wife preparing food while the husband provides tools and ingredients, her childcare alongside his provision, mutual fidelity, and his fair treatment of wife and children.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r29.anchor: kadın ekmek ve yemek pişirirken kocası da âlet ve malzemeyi temin edecektir, kadın çocuğuna bakarken kocası rızıklarını temin edecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r30.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r30.claim: Spouses must consult and cooperate on good relations, chastity, arbitration in discord, household management, and raising children.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r30.anchor: İyi geçinme, iffeti koruma, geçimsizlik halinde hakeme başvurma, aile idaresi ve çocukların yetiştirilmesi gibi konularda karı ve kocanın danışma ve işbirliği ilkeleri çevresinde davranma yükümlülükleri vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r31.claim: Maʿruf is a legitimating criterion for assessing and revising rights and duties that scripture has not fixed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r31.anchor: Nasların sabit kılmadığı hakların ve ödevlerin takdiriyle değişme ve gelişmesinde dinin hakem kıldığı ve rol verdiği bir meşrûluk ölçütü de “mâruf”tur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r32.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r32.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r32.claim: Maʿruf comprises sound human nature, unwarped reason, and values, rules, views, and customs formed within religion’s aims and sources that may develop and change.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r32.anchor: Ma‘rûf “bozulmamış fıtrat, olumsuz bir şekilde şartlanmamış akıl, dinin temel amacı ve nasları çerçevesinde oluşan, gelişen ve gerektiğinde değişen değerler, kurallar, telakkiler, kabuller, gelenekler”dir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r33.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r33.claim: Polyandry is forbidden by immutable religious texts and accords with maʿruf; equality claims or the spread of unmarried cohabitation cannot overturn this rule.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r33.anchor: Kadının birden fazla erkekle aynı zamanda evli olması câiz değildir. Bu kural hem değişmez dinî naslarla sabittir hem de mâruf ölçütüne uygundur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r34.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r34.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r34.claim: The roles of spouses inside and outside the home can change as maʿruf changes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r34.anchor: eşle kocanın ev içinde ve dışındaki rollerinde –mârufun değişmesine paralel olarak– değişiklikler olabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r35.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r35.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r35.claim: The Prophet assigned household tasks such as fetching water, cleaning, and cooking to Fatima, and outside tasks to Ali.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r35.anchor: Hz. Peygamber damadı Ali ile kızı Fâtıma arasında rolleri dağıtmış (su taşıma, ev temizliği, ekmek ve yemek pişirme vb. iç işleri Fâtıma, dışişleri ise Ali yapsın demiş)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r36.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r36.speaker: bazı fıkıhçılar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r36.claim: Some jurists, as cited by Ibn Qayyim, held that the Prophet’s household task allocation was not binding or permanent and could change according to maʿruf.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r36.anchor: bazı fıkıhçılar bu taksimin bağlayıcı ve devamlı olmadığını, mârufa göre değişebileceğini ifade etmişlerdir (İbn Kayyim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r37.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r37.speaker: Hz. Ömer
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r37.claim: Umar said that Quraysh men had dominated their women, while in Medina women asserted influence; Quraysh women began learning this pattern.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r37.anchor: Hz. Ömer şöyle işaret etmektedir: “Biz Kureyşliler kadınlarımıza hâkim bir topluluk idik. Medine’ye gelince orada, kadınları erkeklerine hâkim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r38.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r38.speaker: Hz. Ömer
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r38.claim: After his wife answered his objection, Umar asked Hafsa, who confirmed that the Prophet’s wives challenged him and that some stayed upset with him for a day.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r38.anchor: Hz. Ömer şöyle işaret etmektedir: “Biz Kureyşliler kadınlarımıza hâkim bir topluluk idik

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r39.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r39.speaker: أم سلمة
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r39.claim: In another report, Umm Salama rebuked Umar for interfering in the relationship between the Prophet and his wives.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r39.anchor: Hz. Ömer konuyu bir de Ümmü Seleme’ye sormuş; o da “Ömer, sana şaşıyorum! Her şeye karışıyorsun. Şimdi de Resûlullah ile eşlerinin arasına mı giriyorsun?” diyerek ona sitemde bulunmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r40.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r40.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r40.claim: These sound reports show the major changes in relations between women and men that occurred quickly through Islam’s revolution.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r40.anchor: Bu sahih rivayetler, İslâm’ın yaptığı büyük devrim sonucu kısa zamanda kadın-erkek ilişkilerinde meydana gelmiş bulunan önemli değişikliklere ışık tutmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r41.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r41.speaker: eski müfessir ve müctehidler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r41.claim: Earlier exegetes and jurists explained men’s one-degree surplus by men’s physical strength, superior intellect, and stronger will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r41.anchor: dayanak olarak erkeğin fizik gücünü, üstün aklını ve güçlü iradesini ileri sürmüşlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r42.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r42.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r42.claim: Because men are physically stronger, differences in rights and duties that rest on physical strength are natural.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r42.anchor: Erkeğin fizik gücünün kadınınkinden fazla olduğunda şüphe bulunmadığından buna dayalı bulunan hak ve ödev farklılıkları da tabiidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r43.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r43.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r43.claim: The claim of men’s greater intellect was based on a hadith saying that women described as deficient in reason and religion can prevail over men.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r43.anchor: “Aklı ve dini eksik olanlar içinden, sizden fazla, akıl sahiplerine hâkim (galip) olanları görmedim!..” meâlindeki hadise dayandırılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r44.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r44.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r44.claim: The hadith’s purpose is not to explain an intellectual difference between women and men.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r44.anchor: Halbuki bu hadisin söyleniş amacı kadınlarla erkekler arasındaki akıl farkını açıklamak değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r45.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r45.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r45.claim: When women asked the Prophet what the hadith meant, he identified deficient reason with requiring two female witnesses for one male witness, and deficient religion with not praying or fasting during menstruation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r45.anchor: hanımlar tarafından Hz. Peygamber’e sorulmuş; akıl eksikliği, “şahitlikte bir erkeğe karşılık iki kadın şahit istenmesi”; din eksikliği ise “hayız halinde namaz kılmamak ve oruç tutmamak” olarak tanımlanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r46.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r46.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r46.claim: Women do not pray during menstruation and later make up fasting; this exemption cannot be a negative deficiency in religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r46.anchor: Kadınlar, aybaşı halinde iken menedildikleri için namazlarını kılmazlar, oruçlarını da –sonradan kazâ etmek üzere– tutmazlar. Bunun olumsuz mânada din eksikliği ile bir ilgisi olamaz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r47.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r47.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r47.claim: Here “religion” means obligation, so deficiency in religion means being exempt from an obligation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r47.anchor: Buradaki “din”le bu kelimenin “yükümlülük” anlamının kastedildiği, dolayısıyla din eksikliğinin de “yükümlülükten muaf tutulma” anlamında kullanıldığı açıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r48.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r48.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r48.claim: The hadith describes a fact and warns women not to misuse the ability to influence and beguile men despite the stated conditions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r48.anchor: “Böyle olduğunuz, böyle yaptığınız halde yine de erkekleri etkiliyor ve kandırabiliyorsunuz. Bu özellik ve kabiliyetinizi kötüye kullanmayın” şeklinde bir uyarıda bulunmaktan ibarettir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r49.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r49.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r49.claim: The author does not deny psychological differences, including differences in will, or the physiological and biological differences between the sexes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r49.anchor: İrade gücü dahil olmak üzere kadınla erkeğin psikolojilerinde farkların bulunduğu inkâr edilmemektedir. İki cinsin fizyolojik ve biyolojik yapıları da birbirinden farklıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r50.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r50.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r50.claim: With exceptions, men generally bear the heavy burden and primary role of providing the household’s livelihood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r50.anchor: İstisnaları bulunmakla beraber genellikle evin geçimini sağlamada ağır yük ve temel rol de erkeğe aittir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r51.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r51.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r51.claim: Men’s one-degree surplus in rights rests on these fundamental and enduring differences.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r51.anchor: İşte bu temel ve değişmez farklılıklara dayalı olarak erkeklere bir derece fazla hak verilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r52.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r52.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r52.claim: The additional right is qiwāmah, the right of protection and management explained in Surat al-Nisa.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r52.anchor: Bu hak, Nisâ sûresinde (4/34) açıklanan “koruma ve yönetme” (kavvâmlık) hakkıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r53.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r53.speaker: Eski fıkıh âlimleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r53.claim: Earlier jurists unanimously accepted men’s precedence in family and state leadership, while differing in other legal and governance areas.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:228/r53.anchor: Eski fıkıh âlimleri aile ve devlet yönetiminde erkeklerin önceliğini ittifakla benimsemişlerdir. Diğer hüküm ve yönetim alanlarında ise farklı ictihadlar vardır

BURHAN:v2p320/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p320/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p320/r2.claim: Although phrased as statements, “the divorced women wait” and “mothers nurse” are commands, since context shows that treating them as factual reports would entail a falsehood.
BURHAN:v2p320/r2.anchor: ومنها الامر كقوله تعالى ﴿ والمطلقات يتربصن ﴾ 10 ﴿ والوالدات يرضعن ﴾ 11

BURHAN:v3p230/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p230/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p230/r4.claim: The wording names divorced women, but women whose marriages are annulled also observe a waiting period; divorce is mentioned as the usual cause of separation.
BURHAN:v3p230/r4.anchor: ولا شك أن من فسخت النكاح ايضا تتربص لأن السبب الغالب للفراق الطلاق

BURHAN:v2p216/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p216/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p216/r1.claim: Although المطلقات يتربصن is phrased as a report, it cannot literally predict that all divorced women will wait; it therefore means a command, preserving the truth of divine speech.
BURHAN:v2p216/r1.anchor: فإن صيغته صيغة الخبر ولكن لايمكن حمله على حقيقته فإنهن قد لايتربصن

BURHAN:v2p220/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p220/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p220/r8.claim: The waiting rule first addresses all divorced women, then the husbands’ right to take them back limits it to revocable divorce, since an irrevocable divorce cannot be reversed.
BURHAN:v2p220/r8.anchor: فإنه عام في البائنة والرجعية ثم خصها بالرجعية بقوله

BURHAN:v2p222/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p222/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p222/r7.claim: The waiting rule for divorced women is general, then excludes women divorced before consummation and specifies the periods for menopausal women, minors, and pregnant women.
BURHAN:v2p222/r7.anchor: فهذا عام في المدخول بها وغيرها ثم خصها فقال

BURHAN:v3p347/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p347/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p347/r2.claim: The declarative form المطلقات يتربصن is another example of a report used to express a command.

BURHAN:v4p23/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p23/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p23/r1.claim: Feminine plural subjects, whether small or large groups, most often take a feminine plural verb, as in these two verses.
BURHAN:v4p23/r1.anchor: ﴿ والوالدات يرضعن ﴾ 1 ﴿ والمطلقات يتربصن ﴾ 2 هذا هو الأكثر

BURHAN:v4p23/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p23/r6.speaker: الحريري
BURHAN:v4p23/r6.claim: Al-Hariri explains the plural of abundance قروء by saying each divorced woman must wait through three periods, though the rule is attributed to the group collectively.
BURHAN:v4p23/r6.anchor: قال الحريري المعنى لتتربص كل واحده منهن ثلاثة اقراء

BURHAN:v1p104/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p104/r12.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v1p104/r12.claim: Ibn Faris says بعل means husband except in al-Saffat, where it means an idol.
BURHAN:v1p104/r12.anchor: وما فى القرآن من ذكر البعل فهو الزوج

BURHAN:v4p27/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p27/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p27/r11.claim: The pronoun refers to divorced women, but the ruling concerns revocable divorce; jurists dispute whether this narrows the earlier general rule.
BURHAN:v4p27/r11.anchor: فانه عائد على المطلقات مع إن هذا خاص بالرجعى وهل يقتضي ذلك تخصيص الاول فيه خلاف اصولي

BURHAN:v4p29/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p29/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p29/r1.claim: Returning the pronoun to the meaning rather than the first wording in this example avoids requiring restriction of the earlier general category.

BURHAN:v4p119/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p119/r1.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p119/r1.claim: Ibn Malik explains that quru is used after three because its regular paucity plural is anomalous, so the eloquent plural of abundance is chosen, as with words having only that plural.
BURHAN:v4p119/r1.anchor: لان بناء القلة شاذ فانه جمع قرء بفتح القاف وجمع فعل على افعال شاذ

BURHAN:v4p119/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p119/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
BURHAN:v4p119/r2.claim: The paucity is relative to each divorced woman, who waits three periods; the plural of abundance instead reflects the many divorced women collectively.
BURHAN:v4p119/r2.anchor: القلة بالنسبة إلى كل واجد من المطلقات وانما اضاف جمع الكثرة نظرا إلى كثرة المتربصات

BURHAN:v4p119/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p119/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p119/r3.claim: One resolution supplies an omitted genitive, giving the sense three quruʾ periods.
BURHAN:v4p119/r3.anchor: انه على حذف مضاف أي ثلاثة أقراء قروء

BURHAN:v4p119/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p119/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p119/r4.claim: Alternatively, the genitive is an adjective in an underlying separated construction, with the partitive sense three of the quruʾ.
BURHAN:v4p119/r4.anchor: إن الإضافة نعت في تقدير الانفصال لأنه بمعنى من التي للتبعيض أي ثلاثة أقراء من قروء

BURHAN:v4p119/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p119/r5.speaker: المبرد
BURHAN:v4p119/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad permits constructions such as three donkeys or three dogs, understood partitivally as three of the animals.
BURHAN:v4p119/r5.anchor: كما أجاز المبرد ثلاثة حمير وثلاثة كلاب على إرادة من أي من حمير ومن كلاب

BURHAN:v4p119/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p119/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p119/r6.claim: Numerals are explicit and therefore do not take emphasis, which ordinarily blocks figurative use of a whole for only part of it.
BURHAN:v4p119/r6.anchor: القاعدة الثالثة الفاظ العدد نصوص ولهذا لايدخلها تاكيد لانه لدفع المجاز في اطلاق

ITQAN:v3p105/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p105/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p105/r4.claim: A declarative sentence can function as a command for emphasis, as though compliance had already occurred; the waiting period for divorced women is an example.
ITQAN:v3p105/r4.anchor: ورود الخبر والمراد الأمر أو النهي أبلغ من صريح الأمر أو النهي كأنه سورع فيه إلى الامتثال

ITQAN:v2p547#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r5.claim: Some pronouns refer to a later expression in syntactic rank, including the pronoun of the matter or story, نعم and بئس, and cases of syntactic competition.
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r5.anchor: أو رتبة أيضا في باب ضمير الشأن والقصة ونعم وبئس والتنازع

ITQAN:v2p547#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r9.claim: A pronoun may refer to only part of an earlier group: the husbands’ right to restore them concerns revocably divorced women within the broader class of divorced women.
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r9.anchor: وقد يعود على بعض ما تقدم نحو ﴿ يوصيكم الله في أولادكم ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿ فإن كن نساء ﴾ ﴿ وبعولتهن أحق بردهن ﴾

ITQAN:v2p552#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p552#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p552#3/r1.claim: Pronouns returning to rational plurals are usually plural, whether the group is small or large; أزواج مطهرة is a singular-form exception.
ITQAN:v2p552#3/r1.anchor: جمع العلاقات لا يعود عليه الضمير غالبا إلا بصيغة الجمع سواء كان للقلة أو للكثرة نحو ﴿ والوالدات يرضعن ﴾ ﴿ والمطلقات يتربصن ﴾

ITQAN:v3p44/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p44/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p44/r4.claim: A specification may come from a separate Quranic verse elsewhere, a hadith, consensus, or analogy.
ITQAN:v3p44/r4.anchor: والمنفصل آية أخرى في محل آخر أو حديث أو إجماع أو قياس

ITQAN:v3p44/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p44/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p44/r5.claim: The general waiting period for divorced women is specified by the exemption for divorce before consummation and by the pregnancy period ending at childbirth.
ITQAN:v3p44/r5.anchor: ومن أمثلة ما خص بالقرآن قوله تعالى ﴿ والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء ﴾ خص بقوله ﴿ إذا نكحتم المؤمنات ثم طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن فما لكم عليهن من عدة ﴾

ITQAN:v3p204#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r1.claim: A declarative sentence normally informs its hearer, but these examples use declarative form to prescribe a command.
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r1.anchor: القصد بالخبر إفادة المخاطب وقد يرد بمعنى الأمر نحو ﴿ والوالدات يرضعن ﴾ ﴿ والمطلقات يتربصن ﴾

ITQAN:v3p204#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects saying a report literally becomes a command or prohibition: these phrases deny legal authorization, not factual occurrence, so God’s report remains true.
ITQAN:v3p204#2/r5.anchor: ونازع ابن العربي في قولهم إن الخبر يرد بمعنى الأمر أو النهي قال في قوله تعالى ﴿ فلا رفث ﴾ ليس نفيا لوجود الرفث بل نفي لمشروعيته

ITQAN:v2p451#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p451#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v2p451#3/r1.claim: Some grammarians count إن in this passage among six Quranic conditional forms where the condition is not intended as a real condition.
ITQAN:v2p451#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم وقع في القرآن إن بصيغة الشرط وهو غير مراد في ست مواضع

ITQAN:v3p170/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p170/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p170/r11.claim: Some readings omit the inflectional or inflection-related vowel, including the cited forms with sukun, among them بعولتهن أحق.
ITQAN:v3p170/r11.anchor: حذف حركة الإعراب والبناء وخرج عليه قراءة ﴿ فتوبوا إلى بارئكم ﴾ و ( يأمركم ) ﴿ وبعولتهن أحق ﴾ بسكون الثلاثة

ITQAN:v3p46/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p46/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p46/r2.claim: The general waiting-period text is specified by the Sunnah for enslaved women.
ITQAN:v3p46/r2.anchor: وآية ﴿ ثلاثة قروء ﴾ خص منها الأمة بالسنة

ITQAN:v3p49/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p49/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p49/r1.claim: A mujmal text is one whose indication is unclear; such texts occur in the Quran, contrary to Dawud al-Zahiri, and the stronger view says a person obligated to act cannot be left with unresolved ambiguity.
ITQAN:v3p49/r1.anchor: المجمل مالم تتضح دلالته وهو واقع في القرآن خلافا لداود الظاهري وفي جواز بقائه مجملا أقوال أصحها لا يبقى المكلف بالعمل به بخلاف غيره

ITQAN:v3p49/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p49/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p49/r3.claim: Qurʾ is ambiguous because it denotes either menstruation or a period of purity.
ITQAN:v3p49/r3.anchor: ﴿ ثلاثة قروء ﴾ فإن القرء موضوع للحيض والطهر

ITQAN:v1p192/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p192/r1.claim: The Prophet directed Muslims to learn the Qur’an from Ibn Masʿud, Salim, Muʿadh, and Ubayy; the source glosses “take” as “learn.”
ITQAN:v1p192/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول خذوا القرآن من أربعة

ITQAN:v1p192/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p192/r2.claim: The four named reciters comprised two early-mentioned Emigrants and two Helpers; Salim was Abu Hudhayfa’s freedman and Muʿadh was Ibn Jabal.
ITQAN:v1p192/r2.anchor: والأربعة المذكورون اثنان من المهاجرين وهما المبتدأ بهما واثنان من الأنصار وسالم هو ابن معقل مولى أبي حذيفة ومعاذ هو ابن جبل

ITQAN:v1p192/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r3.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v1p192/r3.claim: Al-Kirmani suggests the Prophet foretold that these four would remain after him and become uniquely authoritative in Qur’an recitation.
ITQAN:v1p192/r3.anchor: قال الكرماني يحتمل أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أراد الإعلام بما يكون بعده أي أن هؤلاء الأربعة يبقون حتى ينفردوا بذلك

ITQAN:v1p192/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p192/r4.claim: The four did not retain exclusive mastery: Salim died at Yamama, Muʿadh under ʿUmar, and Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud under ʿUthman.
ITQAN:v1p192/r4.anchor: وقد قتل سالم مولى أبي حذيفة في وقعة اليمامة ومات معاذ في خلافة عمر ومات أبي وابن مسعود في خلافة عثمان

ITQAN:v1p192/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p192/r5.claim: Zayd outlived the four and later became the leading authority in recitation, contradicting an enduring exclusive status for them.
ITQAN:v1p192/r5.anchor: وقد تأخر زيد بن ثابت وانتهت إليه الرياسة في القراءة وعاش بعدهم زمنا طويلا

ITQAN:v1p192/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p192/r6.claim: The command to learn from the four applied when it was given; it does not imply that no other Companion then matched or surpassed their memorization.
ITQAN:v1p192/r6.anchor: فالظاهر أنه أمر بالأخذ عنهم في الوقت الذي صدر فيه ذلك القول ولا يلزم من ذلك ألا يكون أحد في ذلك الوقت شاركهم في حفظ القرآن

ITQAN:v1p192/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p192/r7.claim: A report in the Sahih says seventy Companions killed at Biʾr Maʿuna were known as the Qur’an readers.
ITQAN:v1p192/r7.anchor: وفي الصحيح في غزوة بئر معونة أن الذين قتلوا بها من الصحابة كان يقال لهم القراء وكانوا سبعين رجلا

ITQAN:v1p192/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ITQAN:v1p192/r8.claim: In Qatada’s report, Anas names four Qur’an collectors during the Prophet’s lifetime, all Helpers: Ubayy, Muʿadh, Zayd, and Abu Zayd, whom he calls an uncle.
ITQAN:v1p192/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قال سألت أنس بن مالك من جمع القرآن على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أربعة كلهم من الأنصار

ITQAN:v1p192/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ITQAN:v1p192/r9.claim: A second report from Anas says only four had collected the Qur’an when the Prophet died, naming Abu al-Dardaʾ instead of Ubayy.
ITQAN:v1p192/r9.anchor: من طريق ثابت عن أنس قال مات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يجمع القرآن غير أربعة أبو الدرداء ومعاذ بن جبل وزيد بن ثابت وأبو زيد

ITQAN:v1p192/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r10.speaker: جماعة من الأئمة
ITQAN:v1p192/r10.claim: The second report differs from Qatada’s in explicitly restricting the collectors to four and substituting Abu al-Dardaʾ for Ubayy; several Imams rejected that exclusivity.
ITQAN:v1p192/r10.anchor: وفيه مخالفة لحديث قتادة من وجهين أحدهما التصريح بصيغة الحصر في الأربعة والآخر ذكر أبي الدرداء بدل أبي بن كعب وقد استنكر جماعة من الأئمة الحصر في الأربعة

ITQAN:v1p192/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r11.speaker: المازري
ITQAN:v1p192/r11.claim: Al-Maziri argues that Anas’s statement need not describe the full historical reality; it may only report that he knew of four collectors.
ITQAN:v1p192/r11.anchor: وقال المازري لا يلزم من قول أنس لم يجمعه غيرهم أن يكون الواقع في نفس الأمر كذلك لأن التقدير أنه لا يعلم أن سواهم جمعه

ITQAN:v1p192/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p192/r12.speaker: المازري
ITQAN:v1p192/r12.claim: Al-Maziri says comprehensive knowledge was highly unlikely because Companions were numerous and dispersed; it would require asking each one individually.
ITQAN:v1p192/r12.anchor: وإلا فكيف الإحاطة بذلك مع كثرة الصحابة وتفرقهم في البلاد وهذا لا يتم إلا إن كان لقي كل واحد منهم على انفراده

ITQAN:v4p480/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p480/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p480/r7.claim: If equally plausible senses cannot both be meant, as with qurʾ for menstruation or purity, infer the intended one from indicators; absent indicators, scholars differ whether to choose freely or take the stricter or easier ruling.
ITQAN:v4p480/r7.anchor: فإن تنافى اجتماعهما ولم يمكن إرادتهما باللفظ الواحد كالقرء للحيض والطهر اجتهد في المراد منهما بالأمارات الدالة عليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r1.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r1.claim: Jurjānī cites a Prophetic saying comparing one who teaches good but does not practice it to a lamp that lights others while consuming itself; he also gives a wick variant and states no grading.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r1.anchor: من ان النبي قال مثل الذي يعلم الخير ولا يعمل به مثل السراج الذي يضىء للناس ويحرق نفسه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r2.claim: Parables strengthen meanings by moving the listener from what is hidden to what is clear and from abstract reasoning to familiar sensory or innate knowledge, which feels firmer and more certain.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r2.anchor: أول ذلك وأظهره أن أنس النفوس موقوف على أن تخرجها من خفي إلى جلى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r3.claim: He illustrates this method with concrete admonitions: one cannot harvest grapes from thorns, one reaps what one sows, pearls should not be cast before swine, and worldly life is a passing shadow or borrowed garment, with al-Shāfiʿī and Labīd cited.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p101/r3.anchor: فهذه جملة من القول تخبر عن صيغ التمثيل وتخبر عن حال المعنى معه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r1.claim: The poem personifies separation as a discerning rival who keeps the lovers apart out of jealousy, turning estrangement into a deliberate act with an imagined motive.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r1.anchor: الدعوى في إثبات الخصومة وجعل النوى كالشيء الذي يعقل ويميز ويريد ويختار

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r2.claim: The red eye is real, but its supposed redness from blood spilled by beauties is an invented cause; Jurjānī identifies Ibn al-Muʿtazz as the originator of this conceit.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r2.anchor: قد أتى بحمرة العين وهي تعرض لها من حيث هي عين معلة واتى بإراقة الدم في صورة العلة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r3.claim: This differs from saying the wind envies the speaker: the wind really blows his cloak onto his face, while envy is the invented cause; the eye image instead invents a cause for an existing condition.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r3.anchor: وبين هذا الجنس وبين نحو الريح تحسدني فرق وذلك أن لك هناك فعلا هو ثابت واجب في الريح

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r4.claim: Other poets reinterpret illness and fever as keen insight, minds ablaze, and strong resolve; Jurjānī treats this as an imaginative reinterpretation of a quality, without a separate cause-and-effect fiction.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p244/r4.anchor: فترت وما وجدت أبا العلاء سوى فرط التوقد والذكاء

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p51/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p51/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p51/r1.claim: Studying why expression is eloquent has religious value: it helps prevent errors about revelation and interpretation and equips readers to give a persuasive argument for a Qur'anic verse.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p51/r1.anchor: سببا إلى حسم كثير من الفساد فيما يعود إلى التنزيل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r1.claim: After mentioning a possessed noun, eloquence favors repeating the possessor’s explicit name instead of replacing it with a pronoun, whose use weakens the effect.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r1.anchor: فإن البلاغة تقتضي أن تذكره باسمه الظاهر ، ولا تضمره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r2.claim: Al-Sahib argues that the verse needs ‘sword’ repeated four times; replacing the latter instances with pronouns would spoil its quality, though not its meter.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r2.anchor: قال الصاحب : لو لم يعد أربع مرات فقال :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r3.claim: He cites Dibil’s repeated ʿAmr, an unnamed poet’s repeated ‘wood’, and al-Mutanabbi’s repeated ‘time’ as evidence that explicit repetition can be more graceful than pronouns.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r3.anchor: ومن الشاهد في ذلك قول دعبل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r4.claim: Ambiguity does not explain the preference for an explicit noun: a plural example remains stylistically awkward even when the pronoun cannot be confused with another referent.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r4.anchor: مع أن لا لبس مثل الذي وجدناه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r5.speaker: أبو يعقوب
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r5.claim: In an anecdote related to al-Jahiz, Abu Yaqub says indirect allusion does not affect understanding in the way explicit disclosure does; the author uses this to explain the force of repetition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r5.anchor: فقال أبو يعقوب : أما علمت أن الكناية والتعريض ، لا يعملان في العقول عمل الإفصاح

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r6.claim: The explicit repetitions in ‘By the truth We sent it down, and by the truth it descended’ and ‘God, the One, God, the Eternal’ create an effect that pronouns would lose.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r6.anchor: كان لإعادة اللفظ في قوله تعالى : ( ﴿ وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل ﴾ ) ، وقوله : ( ﴿ قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد ﴾ ) عمل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r7.claim: He introduces a Hamasa poem as another instance of the same point, saying it resembles Ibn al-Rumi’s example because it too is a simile.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p400/r7.anchor: ومن البين الجلي في هذا المعنى - وهو كبيت ابن الرومي سواء ، لأنه تشبيه مثله - بيت الحماسة

AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r1.claim: Qurūʾ is prolonged and hamzated, singular qurʾ is lightly hamzated, and aqraʾa al-marʾa means she became menstruating; the form also describes having had one or two periods.
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r1.anchor: قال {ثلاثة قروء} ممدودة مهموزة وواحدها "القرء" خفيفة مهموزة

AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r2.claim: A qurʾ is the cessation of menstruation.

AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r3.claim: Some instead define a qurʾ as the interval between two menstruations.

AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r4.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r4.claim: An unnamed poet uses qaraʾa janīnan for not conceiving, supporting the root's pregnancy-related usage.
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر: [من الوافر وهو الشاهد الثالث والاربعون بعد المئة] : [76ء] ذراعي بكرة أدماء بكر * هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r5.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p187#2/r5.claim: A second unnamed poet uses al-maqrāh for a watercourse, without hamza; it is unrelated to qurʾ in this sense.

DAMGHANI:v1p198/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r4.claim: Arḥām can mean women's wombs; what is created in them refers to the child.
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r4.anchor: " ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن " يعني الولد في الرحم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r1.claim: Ba'l can mean husband, companion, or lord; it can also refer to land watered by its own roots without rain.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r1.anchor: البعل يقال ويراد به : الزوج ، والصاحب ، والرب .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r2.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r2.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah says a husband is called a woman's ba'l because she is like the field in which a child grows, and the man's fluid is its irrigation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r2.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : وسمي الزوج بعلا للمرأة لأنها كأرض الحرث

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r3.claim: Another account derives ba'l from elevation: a husband is ba'l because he is above the woman.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r3.anchor: وقيل البعل : العلو في الأصل . والزوج بعل : لعلوه على المرأة .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r4.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is husband, in the divorce verse and in Shu'ayb's wife calling him her husband.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البعل في القرآن على وجهين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r5.claim: The second sense is the idol Ba'l, whom the people are asked whether they worship while abandoning the best of creators.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p188/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البعل في القرآن على وجهين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r1.claim: Rijal is the plural of rajul and ordinarily names human males after puberty; some derive it from strength, and the entry notes related senses including strong walkers, spontaneous speech, combed hair, a walker, and a locust segment.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r1.anchor: الرجال جمع : رجل ، فهو اسم لذكور بني آدم بعد البلوغ .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r2.claim: The first Qur'anic referent is messengers, as in the statement that only men were sent before Muhammad and received revelation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الرجال في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r3.claim: A second referent is angels, in the men on the heights who recognize people by their marks.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r3.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الرجال في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r4.claim: The third referent is the Prophet's steadfast Companions in battle, who remained true to their covenant with God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r4.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الرجال في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r5.claim: A fourth referent is the people of Quba, praised for loving purification.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r5.anchor: والرابع : أهل قباء . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r6.claim: A fifth referent is men who keep the appointed prayer times and are not distracted by trade.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r6.anchor: والخامس : المحافظون على أوقات الصلاة . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r7.claim: The sixth referent is oppressed believing men among the people of Mecca.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r7.anchor: والسادس : المقهورون من مؤمني أهل مكة .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r8.claim: The seventh referent is poor Muslims, whom the people of Hell say they once counted among the wicked.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r8.anchor: والسابع : فقراء المسلمين . ومنه قوله تعالى في صاد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r9.claim: The eighth sense is people walking on foot, in the permission to pray on foot or mounted and the pilgrimage command to come walking.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r9.anchor: والثامن : المشاة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r10.claim: The ninth sense is husbands, as in the statement that men have a degree over women and are responsible for them.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r10.anchor: والتاسع : الأزواج . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r11.claim: The tenth sense is males, in the statements that God spread many men and that Muhammad is not the father of any of the community's men.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p326/r11.anchor: والعاشر : الذكور . ومنه قوله تعالى في النساء

FARRA:v1p145/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p145/r4.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v1p145/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s reading has the form raddatahunna in place of raddihinna.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r1.claim: Qurūʾ can mean menstruations or periods of purity; its singular is qurʾ and another plural is aqrāʾ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r1.anchor: {يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} وهي الحيض: (1) وهي: الأطهار أيضا (2) . واحدها قرء. ويجمع على أقراء أيضا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse uses qurūʾ for pure intervals, since travel for raids kept him from visiting his wives.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r2.anchor:
قال الأعشى:
وفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة ... تشد لأقصاها عزيم عزائكا (3)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r3.claim: The Prophet's instruction that a woman with irregular bleeding abstain from prayer during her aqraʾ means her menstruation days.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r3.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم في المستحاضة: " تقعد عن الصلاة أيام أقرائها " (5) ؛ يريد أيام حيضها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r4.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r4.claim: An anonymous poet uses qurūʾ for menstruation, comparing an enemy's predictable surges of hostility to a woman's regular cycle.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r4.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
يا رب ذي ضغن علي فارض ... له قروء كقروء الحائض (6)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r5.claim: The basic Arabic sense of qurʾ is a time or appointed interval, which can be the time of either menstruation or purity.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r5.anchor: أصل القرء في كلام العرب: الوقت. يقال: رجع فلان لقرئه، أي لوقته الذي كان يرجع فيه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r6.speaker: الهذلي
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r6.claim: The Hudhalī verse uses qāriʾ for an appointed time, when the winds blow at their season.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p86/r6.anchor:
قال الهذلي:
كرهت العقر عقر بني شليل ... إذا هبت لقارئها الرياح (1)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r1.claim: What God created in their wombs refers to pregnancy.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r1.anchor: {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} يعني: الحمل (2) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r2.claim: Husbands retain the stronger right to take their wives back before the third menstrual period has ended.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r2.anchor: {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} ؛ يريد: الرجعة ما لم تنقض الحيضة الثالثة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r3.claim: Wives have rights over husbands corresponding to the rights husbands have over them.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p87/r4.claim: The degree men have over women is an excellence or precedence in rights.

MAJAZ:v1p74/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p74/r1.claim: Buʿūlatuhunna means their husbands; its singular is baʿl.

MAJAZ:v1p74/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p74/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p74/r2.anchor: «درجة» (228) : منزلة. «إلا أن يخافا ألا يقيما حدود الله» (229) معناها

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r1.claim: Al-muṭallaqātu is a subject with yatarabbaṣna as predicate; the sentence may be declarative in form but command divorced women to wait, or it may be literal description.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والمطلقات يتربصن }: مبتدأ وخبر، وهل هذه الجملة من باب الخبر الواقع موقع الأمر

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r2.claim: The Kufans say the wording is itself an imperative with an omitted imperative lām.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r2.anchor: وقال الكوفيون: إن لفظها أمر على تقدير لام الأمر،

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r3.claim: A literal declarative reading reconstructs ḥukm al-muṭallaqāti an yatarabbaṣna, omitting ḥukm and the maṣdar particle an; the author calls this very remote.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r3.anchor: ومن جعلها على بابها قدر: وحكم المطلقات أن يتربصن، فحذف " حكم " من الأول و " أن " المصدرية

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r4.claim: Tarabbaṣa takes a direct object because it means intazara, to wait for.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r4.anchor: و " تربص " يتعدى بنفسه لأنه بمعنى انتظر،

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r5.claim: The apparent analysis omits the object of tarabbaṣa, understood as marriage or husbands, and treats three quruʾ as a temporal adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية تحتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أن يكون مفعول التربص محذوفا وهو الظاهر،

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r6.claim: Alternatively, three quruʾ itself is the direct object: they wait for three cycles to pass.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون المفعول هو نفس " ثلاثة قروء " أي ينتظرون مضي ثلاثة قروء.

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r7.claim: The apparent attachment makes bi-anfusihinna modify yatarabbaṣna, with bāʾ marking cause, because of themselves; this construction requires an explicit detached self-reference rather than a bound pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r7.anchor: وأما قوله: { بأنفسهن } فيحتمل وجهين، أحدهما وهو الظاهر: أن يتعلق ب " يتربصن " ،

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r8.claim: Alternatively, anfusihinna emphatically restates the attached subject nun, with an extra bāʾ allowed before nafs or ʿayn; on this parse the phrase has no syntactic governor.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r8.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون " بأنفسهن " تأكيدا للمضمر المرفوع المتصل وهو النون، والباء زائدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r9.claim: The author answers that ordinary emphasis would require a separate nominative pronoun first, but the extra bāʾ makes this emphasis adjunct-like; he cites ba- phrases and al-Akhfash's report qāmū anfusahum.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r9.anchor: لا يقال: لا جائز أن تكون تأكيدا للضمير؛ لأنه كان يجب أن تؤكد بضمير رفع منفصل،

SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r10.claim: The emphasis requires the women themselves to observe the waiting period, not have someone else observe it for them, heightening the intended force.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228/r10.anchor: وفائدة التوكيد هنا أن يباشرن التربص هن

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r1.claim: For numerals three through ten, the counted noun normally takes a paucity plural; since aqraʾ exists, the use of the abundance plural qurūʾ needs explanation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r1.anchor: جمع كثرة، ومن ثلاثة إلى عشرة يميز بجموع القلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r2.claim: One explanation counts all the divorced women together: each waits three periods, making the aggregate number of periods large.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r2.anchor: لما جمع المطلقات جمع القروء، لأن كل مطلقة تتربص ثلاثة أقراء

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r3.claim: Another explanation allows one plural pattern to stand broadly in place of the other.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r3.anchor: أنه من باب الاتساع ووضع أحد الجمعين موضع الآخر

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r4.claim: A third explanation derives qurūʾ from qarʾ with fatḥa; aqraʾ would be irregular because afʿāl is not a regular plural for this faʿl pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r4.anchor: الثالث: أن قروءا جمع قرء بفتح القاف، فلو جاء على " أقراء " لجاء على غير القياس

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r5.speaker: المبرد
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad estimates “three of periods,” with min omitted; Abu al-Baqāʾ's expanded estimate is the same analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r5.anchor: والرابع - وهو مذهب المبرد -:أن التقدير " ثلاثة من قروء " ، فحذف " من "

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r6.claim: One proposed root sense is a recurring appointed time: the star's qarʾ is its rising or setting, and aqraʾa al-najm means it rose or set.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r6.anchor: أصله الوقت المعتاد تردده، ومنه: قرء النجم لوقت طلوعه وأفوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r7.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r7.claim: An unnamed poet uses qāriʾ for the appointed time when winds blow, supporting the time sense.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r7.anchor: شنئت العقر عقر بني شليل إذا هبت لقارئها الرياح

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r8.claim: Other proposed origins are transition from purity to menstruation or the reverse, and gathering; the gathering-water etymology is rejected because that verb has a weak y-root while qarʾ is hamzated.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r8.anchor: أصله الخروج من طهر إلى حيض أو عكسه، وقيل: هو من قولهم: قريت الماء في الحوض

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r9.claim: Linguists disagree whether menstruation and purity are homonyms or share an underlying common meaning such as gathering, time, or transition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r9.anchor: وإذا تقرر ما ذكرت لك فاعلم أن أهل العلم اختلفوا في إطلاقه على الحيض والطهر

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r10.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r10.claim: A woman’s qarʾ can denote her time of menstruation or purity; al-Akhfash distinguishes aqraʾat, becoming menstruating, from qaraʾat, menstruating.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r10.anchor: وقال الأخفش: أقرأت أي: صارت ذات حيض، وقرأت بغير ألف أي: حاضت

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r11.claim: Other definitions are menstruation together with purity, or the interval between two menstruations.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: القرء: الحيض مع الطهر، وقيل: ما بين الحيضتين

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r12.claim: Qarʾ may originally mean gathering, as in gathering water in a basin and reciting the Qurʾān.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: أصله الجمع، ومنه: قرأت الماء في الحوض: جمعته، ومنه: قرأ القرآن

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r1.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r1.claim: Ibn Kulthūm's verse uses taqraʾ for gathering a fetus; on the gathering derivation, menstruation gathers blood in the womb and purity gathers blood in the body.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r1.anchor: ذراعي عيطل أدماء بكر هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r2.speaker: جمهور أهل اللسان
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r2.claim: Most linguists, including Abū ʿAmr, Yūnus, and Abū ʿUbayda, take menstruation and purity as homonyms/opposites rather than senses sharing one meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r2.anchor: ولكن القائل بالاشتراك اللفظي وجعلهما من الأضداد هم جمهور أهل اللسان كأبي عمرو ويونس وأبي عبيدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r3.speaker: الأعشى
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā uses qurūʾ for periods of purity, as the context refers to the loss of the women's pure intervals.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r3.anchor: قول الأعشى: 973 أفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r4.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r4.claim: An unnamed poet uses qurūʾ for menstruation, likening a man's flowing blood to a menstruating woman's blood.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r4.anchor: قوله: 974 يا رب ذي ضغن علي فارض له قروء

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī transmits qarʾ with ḍamma, while Abū Zayd transmits it with fatḥa; both forms mean the same.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r5.anchor: ويقال " قرء " بالضم نقله الأصمعي، و " قرء " بالفتح نقله أبو زيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r6.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads thalāthata qarū, with fatḥa on qāf, silent rāʾ, light wāw, and no hamza; he treats the number as annexed to a generic noun and uses a dialect form of qarʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: " ثلاثة قرو " بفتح القاف وسكون الراء وتخفيف الواو من غير همز

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r7.speaker: الزهري
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r7.claim: Al-Zuhrī, also reported from Nāfiʿ, reads qurūww with doubled wāw, easing the hamza to wāw and assimilating the preceding wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ الزهري - ويروى عن نافع -: " قرو " بتشديد الواو

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r1.claim: The lām in lahunna is attached to yaḥillu and is the lām of communication, as in “I said to you.”
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r1.anchor: قوله: { لهن } متعلق ب " يحل، واللام للتبليغ

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r2.claim: The stronger parsing makes mā a relative pronoun meaning “that which”; its resumptive pronoun is omitted, estimated mā khalaqahu.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r2.anchor: قوله: { ما خلق } في " ما " وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها موصولة بمعنى الذي

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, mā is an indefinite noun described by the following clause; like the relative analysis, it has an omitted resumptive pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنها نكرة موصوفة، وعلى كلا التقديرين فالعائد محذوف لاستكمال الشروط

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r4.claim: Mā may refer to the fetus, treated grammatically as nonrational, or to menstrual blood.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r4.anchor: و " ما " يجوز أن يراد بها الجنين وهو في حكم غير العاقل

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r5.claim: Fī arḥāmihinna can attach directly to khalaqa, or modify the omitted resumptive pronoun circumstantially: what God created, existing in their wombs.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r5.anchor: قوله: { في أرحامهن } فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يتعلق بخلق. والثاني: أن يتعلق بمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r6.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls the circumstantial reading prospective, since at the time of creation the fetus is not yet a thing until its creation is complete.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r6.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " لأن وقت خلقه ليس بشيء حتى يتم خلقه "

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r7.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r7.claim: Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd reads both hāʾ pronouns with ḍamma, the original form and a Hijazi usage; kasra harmonizes with a preceding yāʾ or kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#4/r7.anchor: وقرأ مبشر بن عبيد: " في أرحامهن " و " بردهن " بضم هاء الكناية

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r1.claim: The conditional's answer may be omitted and recovered from the preceding prohibition: if they believe, they must not conceal.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r1.anchor: قوله: { إن كن } هذا شرط، وفي جوابه المذهبان المشهوران: إما محذوف، وتقديره من لفظ ما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r2.claim: The Kufans and Abū Zayd allow the answer to precede the conditional, with the earlier prohibition serving as its answer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r2.anchor: وإما أنه متقدم كما هو مذهب الكوفيين وأبي زيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r3.claim: Taking in as meaning idh, “when,” is a weak analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r3.anchor: وقيل: " إن " بمعنى إذ وهو ضعيف.

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r4.speaker: مسلمة بن محارب
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r4.claim: The majority pronounce the tāʾ of baʿūlatuhunna with fatḥa; Muslimah ibn Muḥārib silences it to avoid consecutive vowel movements, as in a reading of 43:30.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r4.anchor: الجمهور على رفع تاء بعولتهن، وسكنها مسلمة بن محارب، وذلك لتوالي الحركات فخفف، ونظيره قراءة:

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r5.claim: Abū Zayd reports silencing the nominative ending in rusulunā; Abū ʿAmr reports that Tamīm similarly silences nominatives such as yaʿlamuhum.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r5.anchor: ورسلنا لديهم يكتبون [الزخرف: 30] بسكون اللام حكاها أبو زيد، وحكى أبو عمرو

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r6.claim: Aḥaqqu is the predicate of baʿūlatuhunna and means “entitled,” not comparative: outsiders have no claim, and a wife's refusal does not invalidate a husband's revocation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r6.anchor: و " أحق " خبر عن " بعولتهن " وهو بمعنى حقيقون، إذ لا معنى للتفضيل هنا

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r7.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, husband; its tāʾ marks a feminine collective plural like fuhūla and dhukūra, a pattern that is not productive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r7.anchor: والبعولة: جمع " بعل " وهو زوج المرأة

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r8.claim: Baʿūla is also a verbal noun of baʿala; ḥasanat al-tabāʿul describes a good wife, while bāʿalahā is a euphemism for intercourse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#5/r8.anchor: والبعولة أيضا مصدر بعل الرجل بعولة وبعالا، وامرأة حسنة التبعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r2.claim: If fī dhālika attaches to aḥaqqu, dhālika means the waiting period: the husband has the right to revoke during it, restoring her to the marriage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أنه متعلق أيضا بأحق، ويكون المشار إليه بذلك على هذا العدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r3.claim: Alternatively, fī dhālika attaches to the act of revocation, and dhālika refers to marriage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r3.anchor: والثاني: أن تتعلق بالرد ويكون المشار إليه بذلك على هذا النكاح، قاله أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r4.claim: The pronoun in baʿūlatuhunna refers to some divorced women, specifically those whose divorces are revocable.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r4.anchor: والضمير في " بعولتهن " عائد على بعض المطلقات وهن الرجعيات خاصة

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r5.claim: The Shaykh prefers an understood annexed noun, “husbands of their revocably divorced women,” which makes the pronoun refer to all divorced women.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r5.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " والأولى عندي أن يكون على حذف مضاف دل عليه الحكم

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r6.claim: The clause has a fronted predicate; its balanced ellipsis removes “against their husbands” where “against them” appears, and “for their husbands” where “for them” appears.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#6/r6.anchor: وأصل التركيب. ولهن على أزواجهن مثل الذي لأزواجهن عليهن

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r1.claim: Bi-l-maʿrūf can attach to the predicate governing lahunna, meaning their due is established according to recognized practice.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أن يتعلق بما تعلق به " لهن " من الاستقرار أي: استقر لهن بالمعروف

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r2.claim: Alternatively, it modifies mithl as a deleted adjective; because mithl does not become definite through annexation, the phrase is nominative in this parse rather than accusative in the first.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه صفة لمثل، لأن " مثل " لا يتعرف بالإضافة

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r3.claim: The stronger parse makes li-l-rijāli a fronted predicate and darajatun the delayed subject; ʿalayhinna either attaches to that predicate or is a fronted circumstantial modifier of daraja.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r3.anchor: أظهرهما: أن " للرجال " خبر مقدم و " درجة " مبتدأ مؤخر

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows ʿalayhinna as predicate and li-l-rijāli as a circumstantial modifier, arguing that preposing a prepositional phrase before a semantic governor can be strong.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r4.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون " عليهن " هو الخبر، و " للرجال " حال من " درجة "

SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r5.claim: The Shaykh rejects this parse outright: the circumstantial precedes both sentence constituents, unlike the disputed intermediate order; Abū al-Ḥasan allows the latter, while others forbid it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:228#7/r5.anchor: قال: " فأبو الحسن يجيزها وغيره يمنعها "

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r1.claim: The feminine noun ṭāliq is used without tāʾ in ṭāliq, while ṭallaqat al-marʾatu and ṭuliqat are also reported forms.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r1.anchor: يقال طلقت المرأة طلاقا فهي طالق، وقد حكوا طلقت

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r2.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r2.claim: Some claim the feminine tāʾ is omitted from ṭāliq because the word only applies to women; Zajjāj rejects this since many shared masculine-feminine descriptors lack tāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r2.anchor: وقد زعم قوم أن تاء التأنيث حذفت من

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r3.speaker: سيبويه وأصحابه
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r3.claim: Sībawayh and his colleagues analyze ṭāliq as a masculine-form adjective applied to a feminine noun, underlyingly something divorced or dhāt ṭalāq, like descriptors meaning a bearer of sons, daughters, or a child.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r3.anchor: وزعم سيبويه وأصحابه أن هذا وقع على لفظ التذكير صفة للمؤنث لأن المعنى شيء طالق

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r4.claim: When ṭāliq is derived directly from the verb, the feminine form is ṭāliqa; al-Aʿshā's verse addresses a woman as ṭāliqa.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r4.anchor: فإذا أجريته على الفعل قلت طالقة. قال الأعشى:

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r5.speaker: أهل الكوفة
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r5.claim: The Kufans understand qurūʾ as menstrual periods.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r5.anchor: فأما أهل الكوفة فيقولون: الأقراء الحيض

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r6.speaker: أهل الحجاز ومالك
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r6.claim: The Hijazis and Mālik understand qurūʾ as periods of purity.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r6.anchor: وأما أهل الحجاز ومالك فيقولون الأقراء الطهر

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r7.speaker: أم سلمة
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r7.claim: The Kufans cite Umm Salama's report about Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubays: she was told to wait through her menstrual days and wash outside them.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r7.anchor: ما يروى عن أم سلمة إنها استفتت لفاطمة بنت أبي حبيش وكانت مستحاضة

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r8.speaker: النبي
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r8.claim: A second report says when Fāṭima's qurʾ arrives she should not pray; after it passes she should purify herself and pray until the next qurʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r8.anchor: وفي خبر آخر أن فاطمة سألته فقال إذا أتى قرؤك فلا تصلي

ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r9.speaker: الأصمعي
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r9.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says qurʾ means menstruation and aqraʾat al-marʾatu means she menstruated, strengthening the Kufan interpretation.
ZAJJAJ:v1p301/r9.anchor: الذي يقويه من مذهب أهل اللغة أن الأصمعي كان يقول: القرء الحيض

ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r1.claim: Qurʾ conveys gathering: it can mean blood gathering in the body during purity or gathering in the womb during menstruation, so both juristic interpretations are sound and the distinction reconciles them; miqraʾa and miqraʾ also name containers where water or provisions gather.
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r1.anchor: فإنما القرء اجتماع الدم في البدن، وذلك إنما يكون في الطهر، وقد يكون اجتماعه في الرحم

ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r2.claim: One view says women must not conceal a pregnancy, since doing so could assign the child to someone other than its father.
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r2.anchor: قيل فيه لا يحل لهن أن يكتمن أمر الولد لأنهن إن فعلن ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r3.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r3.claim: Another view identifies what is concealed as menstruation; Zajjāj prefers the child interpretation because God's creation in wombs more directly suggests the child, as other verses describe forming people there.
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r3.anchor: وقد قال قوم هو الحيض. وهو بالولد أشبه لأن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن أدل على الولد

ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r4.claim: The condition means that belief in God's threats and punishment for grave sins should restrain them from concealment, just as one tells an unjust person that faith should keep him from oppression.
ZAJJAJ:v1p305/r4.anchor: تأويله إن كن يصدقن بالله وبما أرهب به وخوف من عذابه لأهل الكبائر

ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r1.claim: Buʿūlāt is the plural of baʿl, like dhakar/dhukūra and ʿamm/ʿumūma.
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r1.anchor: بعولة جمع بعل، مثل ذكر وذكورة، وعم وعمومة أشبه ببعل وبعولة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r2.claim: The added feminine ending emphasizes a group; such forms occur only in usages attested by linguists, not freely by analogy.
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r2.anchor: وإنما هذه الهاء زيادة مؤكدة معنى تأنيث الجماعة، ولكنك لا تدخلها إلا في الأمكنة التي رواها أهل اللغة،

ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r3.claim: Here means during the waiting period: husbands may take their wives back before the three qurūʾ end if they intend reconciliation.
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r3.anchor: ومعنى (في ذلك) أي في الأجل الذي امرن أن يتربصن فيه، فأزواج قبل انقضاء القروء الثلاثة أحق بردهن

ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r4.claim: Women have corresponding rights to those owed by them, according to God's commands on a husband's rights over his wife; this is bi-l-maʿrūf.
ZAJJAJ:v1p306/r4.anchor: أي للنساء مثل الذي عليهن بما أمر الله به من حق الرجل على المرأة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p307/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p307/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p307/r1.claim: Men have an added prerogative: both sexes receive pleasure from the other, while the man's distinction is his spending and care for her.
ZAJJAJ:v1p307/r1.anchor: معناه زيادة فيما للنساء عليهن كما قال تعالى: (الرجال قوامون على النساء بما فضل الله بعضهم على بعض وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم).

ZAJJAJ:v1p307/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p307/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p307/r2.claim: God is sovereign to judge and test as He wills, yet His legislation and trials always proceed with consummate wisdom.
ZAJJAJ:v1p307/r2.anchor: معناه ملك يحكم بما أراد، ويمتحن بما أحب، إلا أن ذلك لا يكون إلا بحكمة بالغة

ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n214/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n214/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n214/r1.claim: The phrase translated 'without remarrying' literally means 'by themselves'.

ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n215/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n215/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n215/r1.claim: The waiting period establishes whether the wife is pregnant and the unborn child's parentage; it also gives the couple time to reconsider and resume the marriage.
ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n215/r1.anchor: The primary purpose of this waiting-period is the ascertainment of possible pregnancy, and thus of the parentage of the as yet unborn child

ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n216/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n216/r1.speaker: Asad
