ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n216/r1.claim: A divorced wife may refuse resumed relations even if her husband rescinds the provisional divorce during the waiting period; because he maintains the family, he has the first option to rescind.
ASAD-NOTES:2:228#n216/r1.anchor: A divorced wife has the right to refuse a resumption of marital relations even if the husband expresses, before the expiry of the waiting-period

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p278/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p278/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p278/r8.claim: The counted three qurūʾ cannot consist of two whole units plus part of a third, because an explicitly enumerated total requires three complete units.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p278/r8.anchor: وبعض الثالث قروء في قوله: ثلاثة قروء [البقرة/ 228]

NASHR:v2p213#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p213#2/r1.claim: Although analogy points otherwise, the imams’ consensus allowing an inflectional vowel to be sukun in assimilation supports that possibility here.
NASHR:v2p213#2/r1.anchor: وإجماع الأئمة على جواز تسكين حركة الإعراب في الإدغام دليل على جوازه هنا

NASHR:v2p213#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r2.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
NASHR:v2p213#2/r2.claim: The source cites an anonymous poetic line as an additional witness in the discussion of inflectional sukūn under assimilation.
NASHR:v2p213#2/r2.anchor: رحت وفي رجليك ما فيهما ... وقد بدا هنك من المئزر

NASHR:v2p213#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r3.speaker: جرير
NASHR:v2p213#2/r3.claim: Jarīr’s line about traveling to al-Ahwāz or the Tīrī river is cited as another poetic witness in the same discussion.
NASHR:v2p213#2/r3.anchor:
جرير:
سيروا بني العم فالأهواز موعدكم

NASHR:v2p213#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p213#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr lightly colors the hāʾ of يهدي and khāʾ of يخصمون with a trace of fatḥ.
NASHR:v2p213#2/r4.anchor: إن أبا عمرو وكان يشم الهاء من يهدي والخاء من يخصمون شيئا من الفتح

NASHR:v2p213#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p213#2/r5.claim: Al-Dānī rejects the claim that al-Yazīdī misheard Abū ʿAmr’s readings as true sukūn: precise reports of partial vowel coloring in أرنا show the same transmitter could register subtle articulation accurately.
NASHR:v2p213#2/r5.anchor: فلو كان ما حكاه سيبويه صحيحا لكانت روايته في (أرنا) ونظائره كروايته في: (بارئكم) وبابه سواء

NASHR:v2p213#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p213#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī says attributing unverified, uninformed transmission to the master reciters is unjustified; they are free of such carelessness.
NASHR:v2p213#2/r6.anchor: فإن من يزعم أن أئمة القراءة ينقلون حروف القرآن من غير تحقيق، ولا بصيرة، ولا توقيف

NASHR:v2p213#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r7.speaker: محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن محيصن
NASHR:v2p213#2/r7.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin, a Meccan reading imam, reads the verb lām with sukūn in forms such as يعلمهم and نحشرهم.
NASHR:v2p213#2/r7.anchor: نحو يعلمهم ونحشرهم وأحدهما محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن محيصن أحد أئمة القراء بمكة،

NASHR:v2p213#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r8.speaker: مسلم بن محارب
NASHR:v2p213#2/r8.claim: Muslim ibn Muḥārib reads the tāʾ in وبعولتهن أحق with sukūn.
NASHR:v2p213#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ مسلم بن محارب وبعولتهن أحق بإسكان التاء

NASHR:v2p213#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p213#2/r9.speaker: قارئ غير مسمى
NASHR:v2p213#2/r9.claim: Another unnamed reader reads the lām in رسلنا with sukūn.

NASHR:v1p475/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p475/r1.speaker: التميميون
NASHR:v1p475/r1.claim: The Tamīmī method deletes one of two meeting alifs and changes the other to wāw; a further graphic-form option بروا is rejected as semantically and phonologically corrupt because the wāw represents a ḍamma hamza and the following alif is extra.
NASHR:v1p475/r1.anchor: فيجتمع ألفان، فتحذف إحداهما وتقلب الثانية واوا على مذهب التميميين، وبالغ بعضهم فأجاز (بروا) بواو مفتوحة

NASHR:v1p475/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p475/r2.speaker: الهذلي عن الأنطاكي
NASHR:v1p475/r2.claim: Al-Hudhalī reports al-Anṭākī’s form with both hamzas changed to wāws, برواو; Ibn al-Jazarī rejects it as unsound.
NASHR:v1p475/r2.anchor: وأنكر وجه آخر حكاه الهذلي عن الأنطاكي، وهو قلب الهمزتين واوين، فيقول (برواو) قال: وليس ذلك بصحيح

NASHR:v1p475/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p475/r3.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
NASHR:v1p475/r3.claim: Some later authorities enumerate twenty-six forms from four combinations: qiyās on both hamzas, rasm on both, qiyās on the first with rasm on the second, or the reverse; Ibn al-Jazarī accepts only previously stated forms.
NASHR:v1p475/r3.anchor: وذكر بعض المتأخرين فيها ستة وعشرين وجها مفرعة عن أربعة أوجه: (الأول) الأخذ بالقياس في الهمزتين

NASHR:v1p475/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p475/r4.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
NASHR:v1p475/r4.claim: A fifth premise treats the wāw as the first hamza’s graphic form and adds five more options, making thirty-one; Ibn al-Jazarī says these are not sound.
NASHR:v1p475/r4.anchor: وزاد بعضهم وجها خامسا على أن الواو صورة الأولى، والألف صورة المضمومة، فأجاز ثلاثة مع إبدالها

NASHR:v1p475/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p475/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p475/r5.claim: For ثلاثة قروء, the valid stopping treatments are assimilation and, additionally, rawm, yielding two forms.
NASHR:v1p475/r5.anchor: مسألة: ثلاثة قروء) فيه وجه واحد، وهو الإدغام كما تقدم، ويجوز فيه أيضا الإشارة بالروم

NASHR:v1p475/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p475/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p475/r6.claim: In بريء and النسيء, assimilation and rawm are allowed, with a third option of ishāmām; reported deletion to follow the rasm is invalid and amounts to assimilation.
NASHR:v1p475/r6.anchor: وكذلك يجوز هذان الوجهان في (بريء، والنسيء) إلا أنه يجوز فيهما وجه ثالث، وهو الإشمام

NASHR:v2p135/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r1.speaker: البزي
NASHR:v2p135/r1.claim: Al-Bazzī is reported to use hāʾ al-sakt at the referenced stopping point; the source says only Ibn Ghalbūn read it with hāʾ, which Arabic grammarians favor here instead of deleted alif.
NASHR:v2p135/r1.anchor: وقطع فيه بالهاء عن البزي، ولم يقرأ بالهاء إلا على ابن غلبون كما نص عليه في جامع البيان

NASHR:v2p135/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r2.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p135/r2.claim: Yaʿqūb consistently pauses on هو and هي forms with hāʾ.
NASHR:v2p135/r2.anchor: فوقف على ذلك بالهاء يعقوب من غير خلاف عنه

NASHR:v2p135/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني وأبو طاهر بن سوار وابن مهران
NASHR:v2p135/r3.claim: Several authorities report hāʾ al-sakt for Yaʿqūb at pause on feminine plural doubled nūn, including words such as لهن and عليهن.
NASHR:v2p135/r3.anchor: فقطع في التذكرة بإثبات الهاء عن يعقوب في ذلك كله، وكذلك الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني، وذكره أبو طاهر بن سوار

NASHR:v2p135/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p135/r4.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī has read and accepts both forms from Yaʿqūb, but thinks the hāʾ rule likely applies only where a pronominal hāʾ precedes, unless a reliable authority establishes a wider scope.
NASHR:v2p135/r4.anchor: وأحسب أن الصواب تقييده بما كان بعد هاء كما مثلوا به، ولم أجد أحدا مثل بغير ذلك

NASHR:v2p135/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r5.speaker: طاهر بن غلبون والداني وابن سوار وابن مهران
NASHR:v2p135/r5.claim: Authorities transmit hāʾ at pause for Yaʿqūb on built forms ending in a geminated consonant, while most authorities omit it; the source examples include forms ending in yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p135/r5.anchor: فنص على الوقف عليه بالهاء ليعقوب بكماله أبو الحسن طاهر بن غلبون والحافظ أبو عمرو الداني

NASHR:v2p135/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p135/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī accepts both hāʾ and its omission for Yaʿqūb on these built forms, and likewise tentatively restricts the hāʾ to examples ending in yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p135/r6.anchor: وكلاهما ثابت عن يعقوب والظاهر أن ذلك مقيد بما كان بالياء كما مثلنا به

NASHR:v2p135/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p135/r7.claim: Al-Dānī alone adds hāʾ in the open and kasra forms of لكن وإن, by analogy with كأن.
NASHR:v2p135/r7.anchor: وانفرد الداني بالهاء في لكن وإن يعني المفتوحة والمكسورة وقياس ذلك كأن

NASHR:v2p135/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r8.speaker: بعضهم عن يعقوب
NASHR:v2p135/r8.claim: Some transmitters report that Yaʿqūb pauses with hāʾ on open-nūn forms such as العالمين and الذين; the source calls this a widespread, regular Arab usage.
NASHR:v2p135/r8.anchor: فروى بعضهم عن يعقوب الوقف على ذلك كله بالهاء، وحكاه أبو طاهر بن سوار، وغيره

NASHR:v2p135/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p135/r9.speaker: ابن سوار وابن مهران وابن مقسم
NASHR:v2p135/r9.claim: Ibn Sawwār’s examples suggest the rule includes nouns and verbs; Ibn Mihrān via al-Tammār restricts it to forms not confused with pronominal hāʾ, while Ibn Miqsam excludes verbs.
NASHR:v2p135/r9.anchor: ومقتضى تمثيل ابن سوار إطلاقه في الأسماء والأفعال فإنه مثل بقوله ينفقون، وروى ابن مهران عن هبة الله

QIRAAT-ER:2:228:43#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:228:43#1/r1.speaker: vhr
QIRAAT-ER:2:228:43#1/r1.claim: The pronoun suffix is read with either kasra or ḍamma, a dialectal phonological variant without semantic difference.
QIRAAT-ER:2:228:43#1/r1.anchor: Vowel change on pronoun suffix: kasra → ḍamma (hinna → hunna); dialectal phonological variant

QIRAAT-ER:2:228:49#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:228:49#1/r1.speaker: vhr
QIRAAT-ER:2:228:49#1/r1.claim: The suffix again has a kasra versus ḍamma reading, representing dialectal pronunciation without a semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:2:228:49#1/r1.anchor: Vowel change on pronoun suffix: kasra → ḍamma (hinna → hunna); dialectal phonological variant

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says women had concealed pregnancy so they could attribute the child to another man; God forbade this.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمـن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن ﴾ قال كانت المرأة تكتم حملها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says husbands have the stronger right to take their wives back during the waiting period.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك ﴾ قال أحق بردهن في العدة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r3.claim: Qatāda explains the men’s degree as a degree of merit over women.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p92#3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وللرجال عليهن درجة ﴾ قال للرجال درجة في الفضل على النساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that the period ends only after purity from the fourth menstruation; where it ends at the maximum duration, bathing, tayammum, or a prayer time must pass.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r1.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا تنقضي عدتها ما لم تطهر من الحيضة الرابعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r2.speaker: داود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r2.claim: The apparent general wording includes a slave wife in the three-cycle rule; Dawud, the Zahiris, and Ibn Kaysan al-Asamm hold this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r2.anchor: وظاهر عموم المطلقات دخول الزوجة الأمة في الاعتداد بثلاثة قروء، وبه قال داود، وجماعة أهل الظاهر، وعبد الرحمن بن كيسان الأصم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r3.speaker: ابن سيرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r3.claim: Ibn Sirin reportedly considered a slave woman's period the same as a free woman's unless the Prophetic practice establishes otherwise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن سيرين أنه قال: ما أرى عدة الأمة إلا كعدة الحرة، إلا إن مضت سنة في ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r4.claim: The majority assign a slave woman two qurūʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r5.claim: The majority read qurūʾ on the fuʿūl pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وقروء، على وزن فعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r6.speaker: الزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r6.claim: Al-Zuhri reads qurū with a doubled wāw and no hamza; this is also transmitted from Nafiʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r6.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: قرو، بالتشديد من غير همز، وروي ذلك عن نافع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r7.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r7.claim: Al-Hasan reads qarū, with fatḥa on qāf, a still rāʾ, and a light wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: قرو بفتح القاف وسكون الراء وواو خفيفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r8.claim: Using an abundance plural instead of aqraʾ reflects the broad interchange of Arabic plural patterns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r8.anchor: وتوجيه الجمع للكثرة في هذا المكان، ولم يأت: ثلاثة أقراء، أنه من باب التوسع في وضع أحد الجمعين مكان الآخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r9.claim: A frequently used plural may displace a rarer one, as shusūʿ is preferred over ashṣāʿ, leaving the latter nearly unused.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r9.anchor: وقد يكثر استعمال أحد الجمعين، فيكون ذلك سببا للإتيان به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r10.claim: One explanation is that the abundance plural fits because each divorced woman waits three qurūʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r10.anchor: وقيل: وضع بمعنى الكثرة، لأن كل مطلقة تتربص ثلاثة قروء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r11.claim: Another explanation prefers qurūʾ because the singular qarʾ has an irregular few plural on afʿāl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r11.anchor: وقيل: أوثر قروء على أقراء لأن واحده قرء، بفتح القاف، وجمع فعلى على أفعال شاذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r12.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r12.claim: Al-Mubarrad allows “three camels” or “three dogs,” understood as three from that class, which licenses “three qurūʾ.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r12.anchor: وأجاز المبرد: ثلاثة حمير، وثلاثة كلاب، على إرادة: من كلاب، ومن حمير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r13.claim: The doubled-wāw reading replaces hamza with wāw and assimilates the pattern's wāw into it, a regular easing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r13.anchor: وتوجيه تشديد الواو، وهو أنه أبدل من الهمزة واوا وأدغمت واو فعول فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r14.claim: Al-Hasan's form annexes the number to a generic noun, which can denote one or many; the number signals plurality.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r14.anchor: وتوجيه قراءة الحسن أنه أضاف العدد إلى اسم الجنس، إذ اسم الجنس يطلق على الواحد وعلى الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r15.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r15.claim: Ikrima, al-Nakhaʿi, and al-Zuhri identify the concealed matter as menstruation, including false claims intended to lengthen the period or hasten separation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r16.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r16.claim: Umar and Ibn ʿAbbās identify the concealed matter as pregnancy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r16.anchor: أو: الحبل، قاله عمر، وابن عباس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r17.speaker: ابن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r17.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and al-Rabiʿ take the phrase to include both menstruation and pregnancy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r17.anchor: أو الحيض والحبل معا، قاله ابن عمر، ومجاهد، والضحاك، وابن زيد، والربيع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r18.claim: The prohibition makes concealment unlawful and shows that women are entrusted to report what is in their wombs; inspection would defeat that trust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r18.anchor: فأخبر الله تعالى أن كتم ذلك حرام ودل قوله: ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن أنهن مؤتمنات على ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r19.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r19.claim: Sulayman ibn Yasar says people were not ordered to inspect women's private parts; the matter was entrusted to the women themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p455/r19.anchor: وقال سليمان بن يسار: لم نؤمر أن نفتح النساء فنظر إلى فروجهن، ولكن وكل ذلك إليهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r1.speaker: أهل العلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r1.claim: Scholars agree that women may not conceal pregnancy or menstruation; the wording strongly censures it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r1.anchor: وأجمع أهل العلم على أنه لا يجوز أن تكتم المرأة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari suggests concealment may euphemize aborting a fetus and denying its existence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يراد: اللاتي تبغين إسقاط ما في بطونهن من الأجنة، فلا يعترفن به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r3.claim: The verse can bear al-Zamakhshari's interpretation of concealment as abortion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يراد: اللاتي تبغين إسقاط ما في بطونهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r4.speaker: ابن المنذر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says the scholars he knew would not accept a claim of three periods within ten days, except a clearly formed miscarriage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r4.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: كل من حفظت عنه من أهل العلم قال: إذا قالت المرأة في عشرة أيام حضت أنها لا تصدق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r5.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r5.claim: Malik accepts a claimed completion within a possible ordinary span; if the span is rare, two opinions are reported.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r5.anchor: فقال مالك: إن ادعت الانقضاء في أمد تنقضي العدة في مثله، قبل قولها: أو في مدة تقع نادرا، فقولان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r6.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r6.claim: In al-Mudawwana, Malik accepts three periods in one month if other women corroborate; Ali and Shurayh agree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r6.anchor: قال في (المدونة) إذا قالت حضت ثلاث حيض في شهر، صدقت إذا صدقها النساء، وبه قال علي وشريح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r7.speaker: أبو ثور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r7.claim: Kitab Muhammad requires a month and a half; Abu Thawr says the minimum is forty-seven days, and another view sets sixty days.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r7.anchor: وقال في كتاب (محمد) لا تصدق إلا في شهر ونصف، ونحو منه قول أبي ثور، أقل ما يكون ذلك في سبعة وأربعين يوما، وقيل: لا تصدق في أقل من ستين يوما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r8.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r8.claim: Ali reportedly required an oath from a woman who had not completed menstruation; Uthman issued the same judgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r8.anchor: وروي عن علي أنه استحلف امرأة لم تستكمل الحيض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r9.claim: The lām in la-hunna attaches to yaḥillu and marks the person addressed; mā most likely is a relative pronoun with an omitted object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r9.anchor: و: لهن، متعلق: بيحل، واللام للتبليغ، و: ما، في: ما خلق، الأظهر أنها موصولة بمعنى الذي، والعائد محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r10.claim: Alternatively mā is an indefinite noun qualified by a clause; “in their wombs” attaches to “created” or describes the omitted object in an anticipatory state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r10.anchor: وجوز أن تكون نكرة موصوفة، والعائد محذوف أيضا التقدير: خلقه. و: في أرحامهن، متعلق بخلقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r11.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r11.claim: Mubashir ibn ʿUbayd reads the hāʾ in “their wombs” and “their return” with ḍamma, its original vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r11.anchor: وقرأ مبشر بن عبيد: في أرحامهن وبردهن، بضم الهاء فيهما والضم هو الأصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r12.claim: The conditional has an omitted answer, best supplied from the preceding phrase: if they believe, concealment is impermissible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r12.anchor: هذا شرط جوابه محذوف على الأصح من المذاهب، حذف لدلالة ما قبله عليه، ويقدر هنا من لفظه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r13.claim: Although the women already have faith, conditioning the prohibition on it threatens and magnifies concealment; a believer does not do what is forbidden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p456/r13.anchor: وعلق ذلك على هذا الشرط، وإن كان الإيمان حاصلا لهن إيعادا وتعظيما للكتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r1.claim: The exegetes' summary indicates that men's degree over women entails preference.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r1.anchor: وملخص ما قاله المفسرون، يقتضي أن للرجل درجة تقتضي التفضيل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r2.claim: “A degree” is an indefinite subject, “for men” its predicate, and “over them” attaches to the predicate's implied state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r2.anchor: و: درجة، مبتدأ، و: للرجل، خبره، وهو خبر مسوغ لجواز الابتداء بالنكرة، و: عليهن، متعلق بما تعلق به الخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r3.claim: Alternatively, “over them” may be a circumstantial phrase describing the indefinite “degree,” attached to an omitted governor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r3.anchor: وجوزوا أن يكون: عليهن، في موضع نصب على الحال، لجواز أنه لو تأخر لكان وصفا للنكرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r4.claim: It is invalid to make “over them” the predicate and “for men” a circumstantial phrase, because its semantic governor cannot precede both sentence parts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون: عليهن، الخبر، و: للرجال، في موضع الحال، لأن العامل في الحال إذ ذاك معنوي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r5.claim: Abu al-Hasan allows a circumstantial phrase between subject and predicate; other grammarians prohibit it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r5.anchor: فلو توسطت الحال وتأخر الخبر، نحو: زيد قائما في الدار، فهذه مسألة الخلاف بيننا وبين أبي الحسن، أبو الحسن يجيزها، وغيره يمنعها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r6.claim: Might and wisdom close the verse because it contains command, prohibition, permission, and obligation; dominance and wise ordering suit these legal duties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p462/r6.anchor: والله عزيز حكيم تقدم تفسير هذين الوصفين، وختم الآية بهما لأنه تضمنت الآية ما معناه الأمر في قوله: يتربصن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r1.claim: The intended group is free divorced women who menstruate and whose marriages were consummated; unconsummated wives have no waiting period, nonmenstruating women wait by months, pregnant women until delivery, and enslaved women by two menstruations or two months.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r1.anchor: أي ذوات الأقراء من الحرائر المدخول بهن لما قد بين في الآيات والأخبار

ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r2.claim: The noun is not universal, since the exceptions make universal application impossible; it denotes the relevant class, as in ordinary generic expressions.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r2.anchor: ههنا متعذر لما بين فتحمل على الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r3.speaker: الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r3.claim: The Hanafis say the independent, unconnected statement abrogates the earlier general rule; abrogation requires that the earlier rule’s universal scope had first been established, which it was not.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r3.anchor: وهذا مذهب ساداتنا الحنفية لأن الكلام المستقل الغير الموصول عندهم ناسخ للعام

ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r4.speaker: الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r4.claim: The Shāfiʿīs treat المطلقات as general and say separately stated material specified some cases; al-Rāzī objects that specification is apt only when most cases remain, but Alusi rejects his unsupported criterion because general wording may be specified until a plural sense remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p130/r4.anchor: وقال الشافعية : إن ( المطلقات ) عام وقد خص البعض بكلام مستقل غير موصول وأعترضه الإمام

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r1.claim: يتربصن means wait; the declarative predicate indirectly commands them, avoiding the need to reinterpret an imperative as a predicate. The alternative says the nominal sentence is declarative in form but imperative in meaning, which Alusi finds unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r1.anchor: أي ينتظرن وهو خبر قصد منه الأمر على سبيل الكناية فلا يحتاج في وقوعه خبرا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r2.claim: The declarative form emphasizes certainty and urges prompt compliance; delaying the predicate after the subject adds emphasis, following a path discussed by ʿAbd al-Qāhir and al-Sakkākī.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r2.anchor: وتغيير العبارة للتأكيد بدلالته على التحقيق لأن الأصل في الخبر الصدق والكذب

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r3.claim: The bāʾ makes the women restrain themselves; the wording suggests their inclination toward men and their reluctance to wait, thereby exhorting them. The previous waiting command addresses husbands, for whom restraint is not shameful.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r3.anchor: النساء على التربصلأن الباءللتعدية فيكون المأمور به أن يقمعن أنفسهن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r4.claim: ثلاثة قروء is an accusative time expression; the transitive verb’s object is omitted, understood as marrying, or as the passage of the period.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r4.anchor: نصب على الظرف لكونه عبارة عن المدة والمفعول به محذوف لأن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r5.claim: The omitted object also suggests abstaining from marriage throughout the waiting period without even speaking of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r5.anchor: وفي حذفه إشعار بأنهن يتركن التزوج في هذه المدة بحيث لا يتلفظن به

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r6.claim: Qurʾ, plural qurūʾ, is more eloquently vocalized with fatḥa and ḍamma; it can mean menstruation or the purity between two menstrual periods.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r6.anchor: وهو يطلق للحيض لما أخرج النسائي وأبو داؤد والدار قطني

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r7.claim: A report from Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh, narrated from the Prophet by al-Nasāʾī, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Dāraquṭnī, uses qurūʾ for menstruation days when she should stop praying.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r7.anchor: لما أخرج النسائي وأبو داؤد والدار قطني أن فاطمة إبنة أبي حبيش قالت

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r8.speaker: الأعشى
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r8.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse uses qurūʾ for the women’s purity periods, since this is the time for intercourse, which is barred during menstruation even in pre-Islamic practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r8.anchor: كما في ظاهر قول الأعشى : أفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r9.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r9.claim: Al-Rāghib says the root indicates transition from purity to menstruation, which entails either state; a woman continuously pure or continuously bleeding is not called a possessor of qurūʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r9.anchor: وأصله الإنتقال من الطهر إلى الحيض لإستلزامه كل واحد منهما والدليل على ذلك كما قال الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r10.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r10.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says qurūʾ means the transition from purity into menstruation in one strong view, or the purity just left in his better-known view; it does not mean menstruation. He argues that menstrual onset signals the womb is clear, while purity onset may indicate conception.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131/r10.anchor: والمراد بالقرء في الآية عند الشافعي الإنتقال من الطهر إلى الحيض في قول قوي له أو الطهر المنتقل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that after he divorced his wife while she menstruated, the Prophet angrily ordered him to take her back, wait through another period and purity, then either keep her or divorce before intercourse; this is called the divinely prescribed divorce timing.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r2.anchor: إن إبن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما طلق زوجته وهي حائض فذكر عمر لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فتغيظ

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r3.claim: Shāfiʿīs also use the Ibn ʿUmar report to argue that the waiting period is counted by purity intervals.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r3.anchor: وهو أحد الأدلة أيضا على أن العدة بالإطهار

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r4.speaker: الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r4.claim: The Hanafis understand qurūʾ as menstruations, following Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, and many others.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r4.anchor: وذهب ساداتنا الحنفية إلى أن المراد بالقرء الحيض وهو المروى عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r5.claim: Alusi answers that, even if transition into menstruation identifies non-pregnancy, menstrual bleeding itself causes the desired clearing; the indicator is not preferable to the cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r5.anchor: بأن سيلان الدم هو السبب للبراءة المقصودة ولا نسلم أن اعتبار المعرف أولى من اعتبار السبب

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r9.claim: Alusi says the Ṣaḥīḥayn report does not prove that the waiting period is purity; that conclusion depends on identifying the demonstrative’s referent as purity, for which he finds no evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r9.anchor: غير مسلم لأنه موقوف على جعل الإشارة للحالة التي هي الطهر ولا يقوم عليه دليل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r10.claim: The demonstrative is feminine to agree with its predicate; when a pronoun lies between a masculine antecedent and feminine predicate, the majority prioritize agreement with the predicate because the past is fixed.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p131#2/r10.anchor: وأنث أسم الإشارة مراعاة للخبر كالضمير إذا وقع بين مرجع مذكر وخبر مؤنث

ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports a prophetic statement that an enslaved woman’s divorce is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstruations; Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah, and al-Dāraquṭnī transmit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r1.anchor: وأما الإستدلال على أن ( القرء ) الحيض فهو ما أخرجه أبو داؤد والترمذي وإبن ماجه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r2.speaker: الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r2.claim: Hanafis infer that the free woman’s three qurūʾ are menstruations: free and enslaved women differ in waiting-period quantity, not kind, so the report clarifies the ambiguous term.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r2.anchor: عن عائشة أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : طلاق الأمة تطليقتان وعدتها حيضتان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r3.claim: Alusi disputes dismissing the report as weak because its transmitter Maẓāhir was supposedly known for only one narration: Ibn ʿAdī records another and Ibn Ḥibbān authenticates him; al-Ḥākim reports no early criticism.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r3.anchor: لضعفه لأن فيه مظاهرا ولم يعرف له سواه لا يخلو عن بحث

ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r4.speaker: الترمذي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhī calls the report gharīb but says scholars among the Companions and others acted on it; al-Dāraquṭnī reports Muslim practice, and Mālik says a report’s fame can replace its chain.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r4.anchor: قال الترمذي عقيب روايته : حديث غريب والعمل عليه عند أهل العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r5.speaker: الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r5.claim: Some Hanafis argue that if qurūʾ meant purity, the numeral three would be defeated because the common divorce period contains two full purities and part of a third.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r5.anchor: ومن أصحابنا من استدل بأنه لو كان المراد من القرء الطهر لزم إبطال موجب الخاص

ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r6.claim: Alusi says this objection misstates al-Shāfiʿī, who counted transition into menstruation or the purity left behind, not the purity between bleeding episodes; entering the third can also count as three, as in calling a child three years old before completing the third.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r6.anchor: ناشيء من قلة التدبر فيما قاله الإمام الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه فلهذا اعترضوا به عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r7.speaker: الخطابي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r7.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī argues that qurūʾ means purity because the Prophet’s phrase “that is the waiting period” follows mention of a purity.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r7.anchor: الأقراء التي تعتد بها المطلقة الأطهار لأنه ذكر فتلك العدة بعد الطهر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r8.claim: Alusi replies that mentioning purity before the Prophet’s statement does not establish that purity is its referent; the menstruation bounded by purity may be intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p132/r8.anchor: مجاب عنه بأن ذكره بعد الطهر لا يقتضي أن يكون مشارا إليه لجواز أن يكون ذكر الطهر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r1.speaker: الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r1.claim: Some Shāfiʿīs define qurʾ as menstruation bounded by two bleeding periods, extending it to some or all of the intervening purity just as water or honey names portions and wholes.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r1.anchor: قالوا : والإشتقاق مرشد إلى معنى الضم والإجتماع وهذا الطهر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r2.speaker: الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r2.claim: The Shāfiʿī derivation takes qurʾ to signify joining or gathering: blood gathers in the womb during purity, and all or part of that period equally indicates it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r2.anchor: والإشتقاق مرشد إلى معنى الضم والإجتماع وهذا الطهر يحصل فيه إجتماع الدم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r3.speaker: الإمامية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r3.claim: The Imāmīs agree with this account and cite their own narrations from the Imams; reports attributed to ʿAlī on the question differ.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r3.anchor: والإمامية وافقوهم فيه وأستدلوا عليه برواياتهم عن الأئمة والرواية عن علي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r4.claim: Alusi judges the Shāfiʿī discussion strong after considering its full arguments and replies, though al-Kashshāf does not satisfy his inquiry; he offers this as a sufficient example.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r4.anchor: وبالجملة كلام الشافعية في هذا المقام قوي كما لا يخفى على من أحاط بأطراف كلامهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r5.claim: Although the few plural aqraʾ might be expected, Arabic freely substitutes either plural pattern for the other. Qurūʾ suits all eligible free women collectively, whose three periods total many, and its plural marks that abundance.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r5.anchor: وكان القياس ذكر القرء بصيغة القلة التي هي الإقراء ولكنهم يتوسعون في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r6.claim: Using أنفسهن instead of نفوسهن hints that divorce should be rare.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r6.anchor: وهذا كما أستعمل أنفسهن مكان نفوسهن للإشارة إلى أن الطلاق ينبغي أن يقع على القلة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar takes what God created in their wombs as pregnancy and menstruation: women must not hide pregnancy to avoid delaying divorce or stirring a husband’s compassion, nor hide menstruation to shorten the waiting period and defeat reconciliation.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r7.anchor: قال ابن عمر : الحمل والحيض أي لا يحل لها إن كانت حاملا أن تكتم حملها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r8.speaker: الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r8.claim: The interpretation including both pregnancy and menstruation is also reported from al-Ṣādiq, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r8.anchor: وهذا القول هو المروي عن الصادق والحسن ومجاهد وغيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda restrict the phrase to pregnancy; Alusi answers that menstruation qualifies as created in the womb because it acquires its status there, even if the blood itself lies outside.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r9.anchor: وهو المروي عن ابن عباس وقتادة مدفوع بأن ذات الدم وإن كان غير مخلوق في الرحم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r10.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r10.claim: ʿIkrima argues that, since the passage addresses menstruating women, pregnancy cannot be intended and the phrase must mean menstruation; Alusi replies that externally limiting a general expression does not limit its referent here.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r10.anchor: وما قيل : إن الكلام في المطلقات ذوات الإقراء فلا يحتمل خلق الولد في أرحامهن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r11.speaker: ابن الفرس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r11.claim: Ibn al-Faras extends the verse to all matters concerning the private parts, including virginity, prior sexual experience, and defects, which women should be believed about; Alusi expresses reservation.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r11.anchor: قال ابن الفرس : وعندي أن الآية عامة في جميع ما يتعلق بالفرج من بكارة وثيوبة وعيب

ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r12.claim: Alusi marks the faith clause as a grammatical condition governing the following Quranic wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p133/r12.anchor: إن كن يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ( شرط لقوله تعالى :

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r1.claim: The faith clause does not make concealment permissible for unbelieving women; it underscores that concealment contradicts faith and magnifies its seriousness.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r1.anchor: ليس الغرض منه التقييد حتى لو لم يؤمن كالكتابيات حل لهن الكتمانبل بيان منافاة الكتمان للإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r2.claim: One parsing treats the faith clause as a condition with an omitted result, meaning they must not conceal; the following prohibition supplies its cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r2.anchor: إنه شرط جزاؤه محذوفأي فلا يكتمنوقوله سبحانه : ( لا يحل ) علة له أقيم مقامه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r3.claim: Al-Alusi objects that the proposed ellipsis makes the command explain itself, or oddly links future nonconcealment to past faith if read as a statement.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r3.anchor: وفيه أن لا يكتمن المقدر إن كان نهيا يلزم تعليل الشيء بنفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says buʿūla is the plural of baʿl, like ʿamm/ʿumūma and faḥl/fuḥūla; its feminine marker is emphatic, and these plurals are lexical rather than analogical.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r4.anchor: والأمثلة سماعية لا قياسية ولا يقال : كعب وكعوبة قاله الزجاح

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r5.speaker: القاموس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r5.claim: The Qamus defines baʿl as husband, lord, master, or owner; baʿla can denote a wife, and also a rain-fed palm.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r5.anchor: البعلالزوج والأنثى بعل وبعلة والرب والسيد والمالك والنخلة التي لا تسقي بماء المطر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r6.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r6.claim: Al-Raghib derives the husband sense from the rain-fed palm that stands on its roots, by analogy to a husband remaining with his wife.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r6.anchor: النخل الشارب بعروقه عبر به عن الزوج لإقامته على الزوجة للمعنى المخصوص

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r7.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r7.claim: Al-Raghib also relates baʿl to intercourse, and explains a baffled man as standing still like a palm that does not move.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r7.anchor: وقيل : باعلها جامعها وبعل الرجل إذا دهش فأقام كأنه النخل الذي لا يبرح

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r8.claim: The choice of baʿūla hints that restoration to marriage is originally effected by intercourse; alternatively it is a source meaning good conjugal companionship or stands for its omitted people.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r8.anchor: ففي إختيار لفظ البعولة إشارة إلى أن أصل الرجعة بالمجامعة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r9.claim: The husbands' right to restore the wives during the waiting period applies to revocable divorce, as the following verse indicates.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r9.anchor: وهذا إذا كان الطلاق رجعيا للآية بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r10.claim: Here aḥaqq means entitled or deserving, not a comparative implying that the wife shares a right of revocation; the comparative form instead intensifies the husband's right.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r10.anchor: بمعنى حقيقعبر عنه بصيغة التفضيل للمبالغة كأنه قيل : للبعولة حق الرجعة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r11.claim: An alternative gloss takes the wording to mean that the husbands' right of revocation is beloved to God, unlike divorce, which is detested.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r11.anchor: وقيل : بعولة المطلقات ( أحق بردهن ) وخصص بالرجعي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r12.claim: Al-Alusi cites the report that divorce is the most detested of lawful things, explaining why the verse's revocation right is framed positively.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r12.anchor: أبغض الحلال إلى الله تعالى الطلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r13.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r13.claim: Ubayy read the phrase with the variant form raddatihinna.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r14.claim: The phrase fī dhālika means during the waiting period and can syntactically modify either aḥaqq or raddihinna.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r14.anchor: أي زمان التربصوهو متعلق ب ( أحق 9 أو ( بردهن )

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r15.claim: Reconciliation means intending to repair the relationship rather than prolong the waiting period to harm the wife.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r15.anchor: إن أراد البعولة بالرجعة ( إصلاحا ) لما بينهم وبينهن ولم يريدوا الإضرار بتطويل العدة عليهن مثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r16.claim: Intending reconciliation is not a legal condition for a valid revocation; consensus permits revocation regardless, and the wording exhorts husbands to seek reform.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r16.anchor: وليس المراد من التعليق اشتراط جواز الرجعة بإرادة الإصلاح حتى لو لم يكن قصده ذلك لا تجوز

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r17.claim: The verse uses elegant ihtibāk ellipsis: each half supplies the omitted reciprocal phrase in the other, conveying mutual rights and duties.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r17.anchor: فيه صنعة الاحتباك ولا يخفى لطفه فيما بين الزوج والزوجة حيث حذف في الأول بقرينة الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r18.claim: The likeness is equality in obligation, not identical kinds of acts; a husband need not mirror cooking or laundry but owes what befits men.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r18.anchor: والمراد بالمماثلة المماث في الوجوب لأ في جنس الفعلفلا يجب عليه إذا غسلت ثيابه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r19.speaker: عمرو بن الأحوص
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r19.claim: A report from the Prophet, transmitted by al-Tirmidhi (who grades it sound), al-Nasaʾi, and Ibn Majah, lists wives' rights to kind treatment, clothing, and food, and husbands' right to sexual fidelity and household boundaries.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r19.anchor: أخرج الترمذي وصححه والنسائي وإبن ماجه عن عمرو بن الأحوص أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : ألا إن لكم على نسائكم حقا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r20.claim: Ibn Abbas says he likes to adorn himself for his wife as he likes her to adorn herself for him, citing this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r20.anchor: وأخرج وكيع وجماعة عن أنس عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : إني لأحب أن أتزين للمرأة كما أحب أن تتزين المرأة لي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r21.claim: Jurists include among wives' rights that a husband not hasten intercourse before she has satisfied her need.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r21.anchor: وجعلوا مما يجب لهن عدم العجلة إذا جامع حتى تقضي حاجتها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r22.claim: The degree denotes an additional right for men, since their rights concern the women themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r22.anchor: زيادة في الحق لأن حقوقهم في أنفسهن فقد ورد أن النكاح كالرق

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r23.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r23.claim: Another explanation makes the degree an honor and merit: men maintain and protect women, share marriage's aims, and uniquely bear care and expenses.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r23.anchor: أو شرف فضيلة لأنهم قوام عليهن وحراس لهن يشاركوهن في غرض الزواج

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r24.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r24.claim: Al-Raghib says daraja denotes a rank, especially one conceived as ascent and elevated status.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r24.anchor: وقال الراغب ( الدرجة نحو المنزلة لكن تقال إذا أعتبرت بالصعود دون الإمتداد على البسيط

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r25.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r25.claim: Al-Kashf traces the root to gradual, measured movement; a stair rises by stages, unlike descent or level walking, and the term extends to progression and divine leading on.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r25.anchor: وفي الكشف ( إن أصل التركيب لمعنى الأناة والتقارب على مهل من درج الصبي إذا حباوكذلك الشيخ

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r26.claim: The explicit noun al-rijāl replaces a pronoun to highlight manhood as the quality associated with the stated distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r26.anchor: وأتى بالمظهر بدل المضمر للتنويه بذكر الرجولية التي بها ظهرت المزية

ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r27.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r27.claim: Almighty means that God can punish those who violate these rulings; Wise means He knows the outcomes and interests behind His legislation, and the closing warns and encourages.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p134/r27.anchor: غالب لا يعجزه الإنتقام ممن خالف الأحكام ( حكيم 822 ( عالم بعواقب الأمور والمصالح التي شرع ما شرع لها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r2.claim: Al-muṭallaqāt are women released from their husbands' bonds; yataraṣṣan means that they wait and do not remarry.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: {والمطلقات} أي المخليات من حبال أزواجهن {يتربصن} ينتظرن {بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} فلا يتزوجن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r3.claim: Qurūʾ is the plural of qarʾ, with أقرؤ as the smaller plural and أقراء as the larger plural.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r3.anchor: والقروء: جمع قرء، مثل فرع، وجمعه القليل أقرؤ والجمع الكثير أقراء، واختلف أهل العلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r4.speaker: عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r4.claim: One group, including Umar, Ali, Ibn Masud, and Ibn Abbas, reads qurūʾ as menstrual periods; the view is also attributed to al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Awzaʿi, al-Thawri, and the jurists of opinion. They cite the instruction to a woman with irregular bleeding to leave prayer during her qurūʾ, meaning her menses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r4.anchor: فذهب جماعة إلى أنها الحيض وهو قول عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وابن عباس وبه قال الحسن ومجاهد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وعبد الله بن عمر وعائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r5.claim: Another group, including Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Umar, and Aisha, reads qurūʾ as intervals of purity; the view is held by the seven jurists, al-Zuhri, Rabiʿa, Malik, and al-Shafiʿi. They cite the Prophet's instruction after Ibn Umar's improper divorce: keep her until purity, then divorce before intercourse, which identifies purity as the appointed waiting time.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r5.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أنها الأطهار وهو قول زيد بن ثابت وعبد الله بن عمر وعائشة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r6.speaker: مالك بن الحارث الهذلي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r6.claim: The cited Hudhali poem uses qurūʾ for the periods of purity wasted while the poet went on campaigns without approaching his wives; the author says travel wastes the time of purity, not menstruation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r6.anchor: مورثة مالا وفي الحي رفعة … لما ضاع فيها من قروء نسائكا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r7.claim: The disagreement changes when the waiting period ends: on the purity view it ends when the third menses begins, counting the remaining purity at divorce as one qurʾ; Aisha said the woman is free from him as soon as blood starts in the third period. On the menses view, she waits until the third menses ends.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r7.anchor: وفائدة الخلاف تظهر في أن المعتدة إذا شرعت في الحيضة الثالثة تنقضي عدتها على قول من يجعلها أطهارا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r8.claim: The noun covers both purity and menstruation: a woman is said to have aqraʾ when she menstruates and when she becomes pure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r8.anchor: وهذا الاختلاف من حيث أن اسم القرء يقع على الطهر والحيض جميعا، يقال أقرأت المرأة: إذا حاضت وأقرأت: إذا طهرت،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r9.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala and Abu Ubayda derive qarʾ as the time when something comes and goes: a person's return has its appointed time, as winds have a time of blowing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p265#2/r9.anchor: فقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيدة: هو الوقت لمجيء الشيء وذهابه، يقال: رجع فلان لقرئه ولقارئه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r1.claim: The divorced women meant are those whose marriages were consummated and who menstruate; verses and reports show that other categories have different rules.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r1.anchor: يريد بها المدخول بهن من ذوات الأقراء لما دلت عليه الآيات والأخبار أن حكم غيرهن خلاف ما ذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r2.claim: Although phrased as a statement, “they wait” functions as a command; this wording stresses its binding force and prompt compliance, while the initial predicate construction adds emphasis.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r2.anchor: خبر بمعنى الأمر، وتغيير العبارة للتأكيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r3.claim: The wording stirs women to wait: because their souls incline toward men, they must restrain them and make them wait.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r3.anchor: تهييج وبعث لهن على التربص، فإن نفوس النساء طوامح إلى الرجال، فأمرن بأن يقمعنها ويحملنها على التربص

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r4.claim: The three qurūʾ are an accusative of time or a direct object: women wait for their passage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r4.anchor: نصب على الظرف، أو المفعول به. أي يتربصن مضيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r5.claim: Qurūʾ can mean menstrual periods, as in the Prophetic instruction to stop praying during them, or the intervals of purity, as in al-Aʿshā’s verse.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r6.claim: The word originally denotes transition from purity to menstruation; Bayḍāwī prefers purity here because it indicates the womb is clear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r6.anchor: وأصله الانتقال من الطهر إلى الحيض، وهو المراد به في الآية لأنه الدال على براءة الرحم لا الحيض، كما قاله الحنفية

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r7.speaker: الحنفية
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r7.claim: The Ḥanafīs take qurūʾ here as periods of purity, which indicate the womb’s being clear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r7.anchor: وهو المراد به في الآية لأنه الدال على براءة الرحم لا الحيض، كما قاله الحنفية

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r8.claim: The command “divorce them for their waiting period” supports purity as the intended sense, since lawful divorce does not occur during menstruation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r8.anchor: لقوله تعالى؛ فطلقوهن لعدتهن [الطلاق: 1] أي وقت عدتهن. والطلاق المشروع لا يكون في الحيض

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r9.claim: The report “a slave woman’s divorce is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstruations” does not outweigh the rigorously transmitted Ibn ʿUmar report.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r9.anchor: فلا يقاوم ما رواه الشيخان في قصة ابن عمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r10.claim: In the report about Ibn ʿUmar, the Prophet ordered him to take his wife back, wait through purity, menstruation, then purity, and only then retain or divorce her before intercourse; this is the prescribed waiting period.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r10.anchor: مره فليراجعها، ثم ليمسكها حتى تطهر ثم تحيض ثم تطهر، ثم إن شاء أمسك بعد وإن شاء طلق قبل أن يمس، فتلك العدة التي أمر الله تعالى أن تطلق لها النساء

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r11.claim: Although the expected plural for three is the paucity form aqruʾ, Arabic freely uses either plural pattern in place of the other; broad coverage of divorced women may also suit the abundance form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r11.anchor: وكان القياس أن يذكر بصيغة القلة التي هي الأقراء، ولكنهم يتسعون في ذلك فيستعملون كل واحد من البناءين مكان الآخر، ولعل الحكم لما عم المطلقات ذوات الأقراء تضمن معنى الكثرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r12.claim: They must not conceal a child or menstruation to shorten the waiting period and nullify the husband’s right of revocation; doing so is incompatible with faith.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r12.anchor: من الولد، أو الحيض استعجالا في العدة وإبطالا لحق الرجعة، بل التنبيه على أنه ينافي الإيمان، وأن المؤمن لا يجترىء عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r13.claim: Buʿūl means the husbands of the divorced women.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r14.claim: Husbands have the stronger right to restore their wives to marriage by revocation during the waiting period, when the divorce is revocable as the next verse specifies.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r14.anchor: إلى النكاح والرجعة إليهن، ولكن إذا كان الطلاق رجعيا للآية التي تتلوها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r15.claim: The pronoun refers more narrowly than its antecedent, which is permissible as if the explicit noun had been repeated and restricted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r15.anchor: فالضمير أخص من المرجوع إليه ولا امتناع فيه، كما لو كرر الظاهر وخصصه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r16.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, with tāʾ marking a collective plural like ʿumūma and khuʾūla; it may instead be a verbal noun used adjectivally or stand for omitted “people of their husbands.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r16.anchor: والبعولة جمع بعل والتاء لتأنيث الجمع

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r17.claim: Afʿal here has the sense of an active participle.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r18.claim: “During that” means during the waiting period.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r19.claim: Seeking reconciliation is not a condition for a valid revocation; the phrase urges reconciliation and bars intending harm to the woman.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r19.anchor: بالرجعة لا لإضرار المرأة، وليس المراد منه شرطية قصد الإصلاح للرجعة بل التحريض عليه والمنع من قصد الضرار

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r20.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r20.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r20.claim: Women have rights against men corresponding in obligation and enforceability to the duties they owe, though the rights are not of the same kind.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r20.anchor: أي ولهن حقوق على الرجال مثل حقوقهم عليهن في الوجوب واستحقاق المطالبة عليها، لا في الجنس

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r21.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r21.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r21.claim: The men’s degree may be an additional right and advantage, since their rights concern themselves while women’s include dower, maintenance, and freedom from harm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r21.anchor: زيادة في الحق وفضل فيه، لأن حقوقهم في أنفسهم وحقوقهن المهر والكفاف وترك الضرار ونحوها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r22.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r22.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r22.claim: Alternatively, the degree is honor and merit: men maintain and care for women and share marriage’s purpose, while being specially charged with care and spending.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r22.anchor: أو شرف وفضيلة لأنهم قوام عليهن وحراص لهن يشاركوهن في غرض الزواج ويخصون بفضيلة الرعاية والإنفاق

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r23.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r23.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r23.claim: God is mighty to punish those who violate these rulings and wise in legislating them for purposes and benefits.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:228/r23.anchor: يقدر على الانتقام ممن خالف الأحكام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p426/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p426/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p426/r10.claim: Here the divorced women are those whose marriages were consummated; pregnant women and those whose waiting periods are counted in months for young or old age are outside this discussion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p426/r10.anchor: أي المدخول بهن بما أفهمه الإيلاء من أن الكلام فيهن غير الحوامل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r1.claim: The declarative form, built on a subject and phrased as an accomplished fact, emphasizes the waiting duty and urges prompt compliance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r1.anchor: في صيغة الخبر الذي من شأنه أن يكون قد وجد وانقضى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r2.claim: Yatarabbaṣna means that divorced women wait and count out the prescribed period.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r2.anchor: أي ينتظرن اعتدادا . ولما كانت النفس داعية إلى الشهوات

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r3.claim: The phrase calls women to restrain themselves from seeking another husband or signaling availability through adornment, eye makeup, or suggestive speech before the waiting period ends.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r3.anchor: خص الأول معبرا لها بالنفس هزا إلى الاحتياط في كمال التربص والاستحياء مما يوهم الاستعجال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r4.claim: The waiting protects against eagerness to resume relations with another man before the prescribed period ends.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r4.anchor: فلا يطمعنها في مواصلة رجل قبل انقضاء العدة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r5.claim: Qurūʾ can mean purity or menstruation, but the author prefers purity: the root concerns gathering, actual in purity; menstruation is named because it causes that gathering.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r5.anchor: وأن المراد بالقروء الأطهار لأنها زمن جمع الدم حقيقة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r6.claim: The author argues that quruʾ, masculine in form with a feminine numeral, fits purity; the feminine noun menstruation takes a masculine numeral, supporting his preference.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r7.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r7.claim: Al-Asbahani says purity is pluralized aqraʾ and qurūʾ, while menstruation is pluralized only aqraʾ; the forms therefore favor purity.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r7.anchor: والمشهور من كلام أهل اللغة أن جمع القرء بمعنى الطهر أقراء وقروء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r8.claim: Al-Harali says qurūʾ is the boundary between purity and menstruation, attributable to either; this liminal meaning explains scholarly disagreement.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r8.anchor: قال الحرالي : قروء جمع قرء وهو الحد الفاصل بين الطهر والحيض

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r9.claim: Al-Harali's sequence begins with divorce in a clean period without intercourse; each purity ending in bleeding completes a cycle, and the third bleed completes the waiting period.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r9.anchor: فإذا انتهى الطهر وابتدأ الحيض كان ما بينهما قرءا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r10.claim: On al-Harali's account, the waiting period ends when the woman sees blood of the third menstruation, which accords with purity and is nearer than menstruation as the meaning of qurūʾ.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r10.anchor: فلذلك يعرب معناه عن حل المرأة عند رؤيتها الدم من الحيضة الثالثة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r11.claim: Desire may lead women to conceal pregnancy to shorten the waiting period and attribute a child to a new husband, or to conceal menstruation out of desire for their former husband's return.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p427/r11.anchor: وكان حبك للشيء يعمي ويصم وكان النساء أرغب في ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r1.claim: What God created in their wombs means either a child or menstrual blood.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r1.anchor: أي الذي له الأمر كله من ولد أو دم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r2.claim: Al-Harali defines the womb as reproductive organs containing the fetus as it develops from a sperm drop into another form of creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r2.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو ما يشتمل على الولد من أعضاء التناسل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r3.claim: The verse does not prove that pregnancy can be known with certainty; only its signs can be known.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r3.anchor: وليس فيه دليل على أن الحمل يعلم , إنما تعلم أماراته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r4.claim: Although phrased as a report denying permissibility, the wording establishes prohibition and emphasizes it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r4.anchor: ولما كان معنى هذا الإخبار النهي ليكون نافيا للحل بلفظه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r5.claim: Concealing such matters indicates lack of faith in God and the Last Day, when God's greatness will be fully manifest and deeds repaid.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r5.anchor: الذي تظهر فيه عظمته أتم ظهور ويدين فيه العباد بما فعلوا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r6.claim: Al-Harali takes the wording to imply a kind of hypocrisy in a woman who conceals what is in her womb; the author notes that this is a qualified attribution.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r6.anchor: وقال الحرالي : ففي إشعاره إثبات نوع نفاق على الكاتمة ما في رحمها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r7.claim: Buʿūla means their husbands and is the plural of baʿl.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r8.claim: Al-Harali defines baʿl as a man prepared and able to marry a woman; it also means husband or master.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r8.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو الرجل المتهيئ لنكاح الأنثى المتأتي له ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r9.claim: A husband may restore the bond during the waiting period of a revocable divorce; after it ends, the woman has the stronger claim over herself.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r9.anchor: في أيام الأقراء فإذا انقضت صارت أحق بنفسها منه بها لانقضاء حقه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r10.claim: The husband's right of return is conditioned on intending reconciliation; without that intent, if she seeks separation, his act is inwardly adulterous.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r10.anchor: وهذا تنبيه على أنه إن لم يرد الإصلاح وأرادت هي السراح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r11.claim: Al-Harali says repairing the first marriage is more fitting in God's wisdom than beginning another bond, because the past can trouble the present.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r11.anchor: قال الحرالي : الإصلاح لخلل ما بينهما أحق في علم الله وحكمته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r12.claim: Al-Harali invokes the Prophet's warning against marrying al-lafoot, a woman who has a child from a previous husband; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r12.anchor: مما حذر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نكاح اللفوت وهي التي لها ولد من زوج سابق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r13.claim: Women have reciprocal rights in recognized good conduct, though the rights need not be identical in kind because each suits its holder's role.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r13.anchor: أي في كونه حسنة في نفسه على ما يليق بملك منهما لا في النوع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r14.claim: Examples include the husband's return right balanced by her right to good companionship, and his ability to retain her balanced by her right to a companion who relieves loneliness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r14.anchor: فكما للرجال الرجعة قهرا فلهن العشرة بالجميل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r15.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r15.claim: Al-Harali defines maʿrūf as what the law approves, reason accepts, and noble character welcomes.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r15.anchor: قال الحرالي : والمعروف ما أقره الشرع وقبله العقل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r16.claim: Men have a degree over women, including but not limited to husbands, in such matters as maintenance and the bridal payment.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r16.anchor: أي فضل من جهات لا يخفى كالإنفاق والمهر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r17.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r17.claim: Al-Harali attributes the degree to men's greater steadiness of intellect and completeness of religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r17.anchor: وقال الحرالي : لما أوثروا به من رصانة العقل وتمام الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r18.claim: The author quantifies the difference as one degree in three, citing the equivalence of two women to one man.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r18.anchor: فالرجل يزيد على المرأة بدرجة من ثلاث لأن كل امرأتين بمنزلة رجل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r19.claim: God alone has true might; any might He lends others is His power's garment, so all should fear His force.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r19.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه أعز بل لا عزيز إلا هو ليخشى كل من أعاره ثوب عزة سطوته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r20.claim: God's wisdom explains the arrangement and reassures women that what He establishes through might and perfects through wisdom cannot be undone.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p428/r20.anchor: تنبيها على أنه ما فعل ذلك إلا لحكمة بالغة تسلية للنساء وإن ما أوجده بعزته وأتقنه بحكمته لا يمكن نقضه

DURR-FULL:v1p655/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r1.claim: An incomplete report counsels placing the matter in what is lawful and avoiding the forbidden: God alone creates, guides, and provides, and controls life and death while the person earns reward.
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r1.anchor: قال: فأنت خلقته قلت: بل الله

DURR-FULL:v1p655/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that intercourse with one’s wife each Friday earns two rewards, the man’s ritual bath and his wife’s bath.
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيعجز أحدكم أن يجامع أهله في كل يوم جمعة

DURR-FULL:v1p655/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r3.claim: ʿUmar says he makes himself have intercourse in hope that God will bring forth from him a soul that glorifies Him.
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r3.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال والله إني لأكره نفسي على الجماع رجاء أن يخرج الله مني نسمة تسبح

DURR-FULL:v1p655/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that when a woman complained that her husband did not approach her, ʿUmar asked about their frequency and told her that intercourse once each period of purity was sufficient.
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال بلغني أنه جاءت امرأة إلى عمر بن الخطاب فقالت إن زوجها لا يصيبها

DURR-FULL:v1p655/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r5.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن الأنصارية
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r5.claim: Asma bint Yazid says she was the first divorcee for whom a waiting period was established by revelation, after she was divorced in the Prophet’s time.
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r5.anchor: عن أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن الانصارية قالت: طلقت على عهد رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v1p655/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r6.claim: Qatada says that in pre-Islamic practice a man could divorce without imposing any waiting period.
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} قال: كان أهل الجاهلية

DURR-FULL:v1p655/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the waiting-period rule was specified by 65:4 for women past menstruation and those who do not menstruate, and excludes women divorced before consummation under 33:49.
DURR-FULL:v1p655/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} {واللائي يئسن من المحيض

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r1.claim: Aisha identifies qurūʾ as purity periods.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: إنما الأقراء الاطهار

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r2.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r2.claim: Aisha’s account says Hafsa bint ʿAbd al-Rahman reached the bleeding of her third menstrual period.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r2.anchor: عن عروة عن عائشة أنها انتقلت حفصة بنت عبد الرحمن حين دخلت في الدم من الحيضة الثالثة

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r3.speaker: عمرة بنت عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r3.claim: ʿUmra bint ʿAbd al-Rahman confirms Urwa’s account against objectors who cited three qurūʾ; Aisha’s explanation is that they are purity periods.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r3.anchor: فذكرت ذلك لعمرة بنت عبد الرحمن فقالت: صدق عروة

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r4.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman says every jurist he encountered held the view Aisha expressed.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r4.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر بن عبد الرحمن يقول: ما أدركت أحدا من فقهائنا إلا وهو يقول

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r5.speaker: ابن عمر وزيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar and Zayd ibn Thabit say qurūʾ means purity periods.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر وزيد بن ثابت قالا: الإقراء الإطهار

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r6.speaker: أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r6.claim: ʿAmr ibn Dinar reports that the Prophet’s Companions understood qurūʾ to mean menstruation.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r6.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار قال: الإقراء الحيض عن أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the three qurūʾ as three menstrual periods.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ثلاثة قروء} قال: ثلاث حيض

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r8.claim: Mujahid interprets the three qurūʾ as menstruation.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} قال: حيض

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r9.claim: Qatada says the divorce waiting period is three menstrual periods.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r9.anchor: عن قتادة {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} فجعل عدة الطلاق ثلاث حيض

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r10.claim: Qatada says the three-period rule excludes a wife divorced before consummation; she has no waiting period and may marry immediately, as 33:49 states.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} فجعل عدة الطلاق ثلاث حيض

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r11.claim: Qatada says postmenopausal women and those who never menstruate wait three months, under 65:4, rather than counting menstrual periods.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r11.anchor: وقد نسخ من الثلاثة فقال (واللاتي يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم) (الطلاق الآية 4)

DURR-FULL:v1p656/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r12.claim: Qatada says pregnant divorcees are outside the qurūʾ count and wait until delivery, as 65:4 states.
DURR-FULL:v1p656/r12.anchor: ونسخ من الثلاثة قروء الحامل فقال (أجلهن أن يضعن حملهن) (الطلاق الآية 4)

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab says a woman with irregular uterine bleeding has a one-year waiting period.
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: عدة المستحاضة سنة

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r2.claim: Qatada says women sometimes concealed pregnancy to assign the child to another man, and God forbade this; some did so maliciously to take the child from their husbands.
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} قال: علم الله أن منهن كواتم يكتمن ضرارا

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says what God creates in the womb includes pregnancy and menstruation, neither of which a woman may conceal.
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} قال: الحمل والحيض

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r4.claim: Mujahid says the phrase covers menstruation and a child; a divorcee must not falsely claim or deny either pregnancy or menstruation.
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} قال: الحيض والولد

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r5.speaker: ابن شهاب
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r5.claim: Ibn Shihab says reports he received identify what is in the womb as either pregnancy or menstruation.
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r5.anchor: عن ابن شهاب في قوله {ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} قال: بلغنا أن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن الحمل

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r6.claim: Ibrahim says menstruation is the principal or predominant referent of what is in the womb.
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم في الآية قال: أكبر ذلك الحيض

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r7.claim: ʿIkrima interprets what is in the womb as menstruation.

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says a husband who divorced once or twice may take his pregnant wife back during the waiting period until she gives birth; she must not conceal the pregnancy.
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} يقول: إذا طلق الرجل امرأته تطليقة أو تطلقتين

DURR-FULL:v1p659/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r9.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
