DURR-FULL:v1p659/r9.claim: Muqatil says the recall-in-waiting-period ruling followed a Ghifar man unknowingly taking back his pregnant wife; she and the baby died, then 2:229 replaced this verse and clarified divorce and waiting rules.
DURR-FULL:v1p659/r9.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حبان في قوله {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} يعني المراجعة في العدة نزلت في رجل من غفار

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r1.claim: Mujahid says husbands may take wives back during the three qurūʾ.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} قال: في القروء الثلاث

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r2.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the right of return lasts during the waiting period.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r2.anchor: عن الربيع {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} قال: في العدة

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r3.claim: Qatada says the right of return lasts during the waiting period unless the husband has divorced her three times.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك} قال: في العدة ما ام يطلقها ثلاثا

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says that if a wife obeys God and her husband, he must treat her well, refrain from harming her, and support her according to his means.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {ولهن مثل الذي عليهن} قال: إذا أطعن الله وأطعن أزواجهن فعليه أن يحسن خطبتها

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r5.claim: The Prophet states reciprocal marital rights: wives should not admit men their husbands dislike to beds or homes, while husbands must provide food and clothing kindly; al-Tirmidhi authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r5.anchor: عن عمرو بن الأحوص أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ألا إن لكم على نسائكن حقا ولنسائكم عليكم حقا

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r6.claim: The Prophet says a husband should feed and clothe his wife as he does himself, not strike her face, insult her, or abandon her outside the home; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r6.anchor: عن معاوية بن حيدة القشيري أن سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما حق المرأة على الزوج قال: أن تطعمها إذا طعمت

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r7.claim: The Prophet says a man should not hurry through intercourse before his wife has satisfied her need as he wishes to satisfy his own.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r7.anchor: عن قيس بن طلق عن أبيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إذا جامع أحدكم أهله فلا يعجلها

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r8.claim: The Prophet says a husband should be considerate in intercourse and not hurry if he climaxes before his wife; ʿAbd al-Razzaq’s wording specifies that she has not yet satisfied her need.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r8.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا جامع أحدكم أهله فليصدقها فإن سبقها فلا يعجلها

DURR-FULL:v1p660/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas likes to adorn himself for his wife as he likes her to adorn herself for him, and does not seek to take all his rights because men have a degree over women.
DURR-FULL:v1p660/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إني لأحب أن أتزين للمرأة كما أحب أن تتزين المرأة لي لأن الله يقول

DURR-FULL:v1p662/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r1.claim: Mujahid says the degree includes God’s favor to men in jihad, inheritance, and every other advantage granted to them.
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وللرجال عليهن درجة} قال: فضل ما فضله الله به عليها من الجهاد

DURR-FULL:v1p662/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r2.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r2.claim: Abu Malik interprets the degree as the husband’s ability to divorce her without her control over the matter.
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r2.anchor: عن أبي مالك قال: يطلقها وليس لها من الأمر شيء

DURR-FULL:v1p662/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the degree means authority.
DURR-FULL:v1p662/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم {وللرجال عليهن درجة} قال: الإمارة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r1.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r1.claim: Asmāʾ bint Yazīd says divorced women initially had no waiting period; when she was divorced, God revealed the waiting period, first revealed for her.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r1.anchor: عن ابيه ، ان اسماء بنت يزيد بن سكن الانصاريه قالت : طلقت على عهد رسول الله عليه السلام ، ولم يكن للمطلقة عدة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha says qurūʾ means periods of purity.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r2.anchor: عن الزهري ، عن عمرة ، عن عائشة ، قالت : الاقراء : الاطهار

IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وابن عمر وابن عباس وسالم بن عبد الله والقاسم بن محمد وعروة بن الزبير وسليمان بن يسار وأبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن وعطاء وقتادة والزهري
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r3.claim: Abū Muḥammad reports these authorities share ʿĀʾisha's gloss of purity periods.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن زيد بن ثابت وابن عمر وابن عباس وسالم بن عبد الله والقاسم بن محمد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r4.speaker: عمر وعبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r4.claim: ʿUmar and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar consider a woman divorced once or twice still his wife until the time she may pray.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r4.anchor: فقال عمر لعبد الله اراها امراته مادون ان يحل لها الصلاة . قال : فانا ارى ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid interprets the three qurūʾ as three menstruations.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد 1 يتربصن بانفسهن ثلاثة قروء قال : ثلاث حيض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r6.speaker: علي وابن عباس وأبو الدرداء وعبادة بن الصامت وأبو موسى وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وعكرمة والشعبي وقتادة والربيع بن أنس ومقاتل بن حيان والسدي وعطاء الخراساني
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r6.claim: Abū Muḥammad reports these authorities also interpret qurūʾ as menstruations; Qatāda held this in one report.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن علي وابن عباس وابي الدرداء عبادة بن الصامت وابي موسى وسعيد بن جبير

IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r7.claim: A pregnant divorced woman hid her pregnancy until birth; ʿUmar identified her as concealing what God created in her womb.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r7.anchor: عن علي بن رباح ، قال : كانت تحت عمر بن الخطاب امراة من قريش

IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي والسدي والنخعي وقتادة ومقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r8.claim: These authorities explain what is concealed as pregnancy; al-Nakhaʿī held this in one view.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p414#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن محمد بن كعب القرظى والسدى والنخعي ، في أحد قوليه وقتادة ومقاتل بن حيان ، انهم قالوا الحبل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says a woman may not conceal pregnancy or menstruation.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والشعبي والحكم بن عتيبة ومجاهد والربيع بن أنس والضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r2.claim: These authorities are reported to include both pregnancy and menstruation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r2.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس والشعبي والحكم بن عتيبة ومجاهد والربيع بن انس

IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says what is concealed is menstruation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة ، في هذه الاية ولا يحل لهن ان يكتمن ما خلق الله في ارحامهن قال : هو الحيض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r4.speaker: عطية والنخعي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r4.claim: ʿAṭiyya and al-Nakhaʿī in one view are reported to share the menstruation gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r4.anchor: وروى عن عطية ، واحد الروايات عن النخعي ، نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r5.claim: Saʿīd tells a Bedouin that his nephew may not take back a wife who hid pregnancy until birth, asking what he wants with a woman who does not believe.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r5.anchor: سعيد : ما تصنع بامراة لا تؤمن بالله واليوم الاخر .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r6.claim: Saʿīd glosses belief in the Last Day as belief in the unseen in which deeds are requited.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : واليوم الاخر يعني : ويصدقون بالغيب الذي فيه جزاء الاعمال

IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a husband divorcing his pregnant wife once or twice may take her back until delivery.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r7.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة ، عن ابن عباس ، في قوله وبعولتهن احق بردهن

IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r8.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وإبراهيم النخعي وعكرمة والضحاك والربيع بن أنس وقتادة ومقاتل بن حيان وزيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r8.claim: These authorities are reported to share Ibn ʿAbbās's ruling on taking back a pregnant wife before delivery.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p415/r8.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن مجاهد والحسن وابراهيم النخعي وعكرمة والضحاك والربيع بن انس وقتادة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās likes to adorn himself for his wife as he likes her to adorn herself for him.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : اني احب ان اتزين للمراة ، كما احب ان تزين لي المراة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r2.claim: Muqātil says women have rights corresponding to their duties in fairness.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان : ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف يقول : لهن من الحق مثل الذي عليهن

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās does not want to claim all his due from his wife.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : ما احب ان استنظف جميع حقي عليها ، لان الله يقول

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r4.claim: Mujāhid calls the degree God's favor to men, including jihad, inheritance, and other privileges.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد : وللرجال عليهن درجة قال : فضل . ما فضله الله به عليها من الجهاد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r5.speaker: أبو مالك عن السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says a man may divorce her and she has no say in that matter.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r5.anchor: عن السدي ، عن أبي مالك : وللرجال عليهن درجة قال : يطلقها ، وليس لها من الامر شيء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets the degree as authority.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r6.anchor: سمعت زيد بن اسلم يقول في قول الله : وللرجال عليهن درجة قال : الامارة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r7.claim: Qatāda says men have a degree of excellence over women.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : وللرجال عليهن درجة قال : للرجال درجة في الفضل على النساء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r8.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r8.claim: Muqātil says the privilege reflects men's spending on women.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r8.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان وللرجال عليهن درجة يعني : فضيلة بما انفقوا عليهن من اموالهم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r9.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda explain God's might here as might in blessing.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r9.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة ، انهما قالا : العزيز في نعمته

IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r10.speaker: أبو العالية والربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r10.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Rabīʿ say it is might in vengeance.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p417/r10.anchor: وروى عن أبي العالية والربيع بن انس : انهما قالا : العزيز في نقمته اذ انتقم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p418/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p418/r1.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p418/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās's gloss of ḥakīm as one who makes firm whatever He wills.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p418/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن بعاس ، في قوله : حكيم يقول : محكم لما اراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r1.claim: بعولة is the plural of بعل, ‘husband’; بعل originally meant ‘master’ and is an old Semitic word. The Canaanite/Phoenician deity Baal is named at 37:125.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وبعولتهن } . البعولة جمع بعل ، والبعل اسم زوج المرأة . وأصل البعل في كلامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r2.claim: Husband was called بعل because he held authority over the marital bond and was regarded as a woman’s owner and master. As family law developed from Abraham onward, that ownership sense diminished and Arabic زَوْج came to name either spouse fairly, since each completes a pair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r2.anchor: وسمي به الزوج لأنه ملك أمر عصمة زوجه ، ولأن الزوج كان يعتبر مالكا للمرأة وسيدا لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r3.claim: The Quran usually calls spouses زَوْج; exceptions occur in accounts of earlier peoples, as at 11:72, or when recalling male authority, as at 4:128 and here, where the husband has the right of return.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r3.anchor: وقد عبر القرآن بهذا الاسم في أغلب المواضع ، غير التي حكى فيها أحوال الأمم الماضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r4.claim: Another view derives بعل from ‘male’: the deity Baal symbolizes masculine power, and a tree that grows without irrigation is also called بعل.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r4.anchor: وقيل : البعل : الذكر ، وتسمية المعبود بعلا لأنه رمز إلى قوة الذكورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r5.claim: The plural بَعُولة has the pattern faʿūla, built on the regular faʿūl plural of faʿl and given an extra tāʾ marbūṭa by attested usage to suggest a collective, as in فحولة and ذكورة; it adds emphasis to group plurality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r5.anchor: وجاء جمعه على وزن فعولة ، وأصله فعول المطرد في جمع فعل ، لكنه زيدت فيه الهاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r6.claim: The pronoun in بعولتهن refers to the previously mentioned revocably divorced women. They are called divorced because husbands initiated divorce, although divorce breaks the bond; during the waiting period they occupy a middle status, so ‘their husbands’ is a metaphor based on their prior status.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r6.anchor: وضمير { بعولتهن } ، عائد إلى ( المطلقات ) قبله ، وهن المطلقات الرجعيات كما تقدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r7.claim: The waiting period gives men room to regret and seek reconciliation, as 65:1 says, ‘perhaps God will bring about something after that’; this resembles the rule of īlāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r7.anchor: وإنما جعل الله مدة العدة توسعة على المطلقين ، عسى أن تحدث لهم ندامة ورغبة في مراجعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r8.claim: During the waiting period divorced women are between the status of wives and strangers; calling their former husbands بَعُولة is a transparent metaphor based on their prior status, like continuing to call grown wards ‘orphans’ at 4:2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p393/r8.anchor: وعلى اعتبار هذه الحالة الوسط أوقع عليهم اسم البعولة هنا ، وهو مجاز قرينته واضحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r1.claim: ذلك points to the waiting period’s duration: husbands may return their wives during the three quruʾ, not afterward. The verse legislates reconciliation while the divorce waiting period lasts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r1.anchor: الإشارة بقوله : { ذلك } إلى التربص بمعنى مدته ، أي للبعولة حق الإرجاع في مدة القروء الثلاثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r2.claim: He says the verse both establishes reconciliation and urges divorced husbands to pursue it: since one or both spouses may want reunion, men are urged to overlook causes of divorce, being more likely to judge patiently while women are more prone to anger and refusal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r2.anchor: وعندي أن هذا ليس مجرد تشريع للمراجعة بل الآية جامعة لأمرين : حكم المراجعة ، وتحضيض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r3.claim: رد was discussed at 2:217; here it means returning to married life, or reconciliation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r3.anchor: والرد تقدم الكلام عليه عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r4.claim: Malik treats ‘returning’ literally, supporting the view that divorce legally severs the marriage bond.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r4.anchor: وتسمية المراجعة ردا يرجح أن الطلاق قد اعتبر في الشرع قطعا لعصمة النكاح ، فهو إطلاق حقيقي على قول مالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومن وافقوه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa and his followers read ‘return’ figuratively: during the waiting period the bond is already on a path to dissolution at its end, and reconciliation turns it back from that course.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395/r5.anchor: وأما أبو حنيفة ومن وافقوه فتأولوا التعبير بالرد بأن العصمة في مدة العدة سائرة في سبيل الزوال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.claim: The condition ‘if they intend reconciliation’ exhorts husbands to seek repair; it does not restrict the right to return.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { إن أرادوا إصلاحا } شرط قصد به الحث على إرادة الإصلاح ، وليس هو للتقييد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.claim: لَهُنّ cannot refer to the nearest ‘divorced women,’ who no longer have mutual marital rights; it refers to wives implied by ‘returning them.’ Accordingly الرجال means their husbands, as ‘the man of a woman’ means her husband, like ‘his wife’ at 11:71 and 11:81.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون ضمير { لهن } عائدا إلى أقرب مذكور وهو ( المطلقات ) ، على نسق الضمائر قبله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may refer to wives in 2:226: since unjustified īlāʾ harms their rights, the general rule follows that specific context. The discourse moves from wives to divorced women and, through return, back to them as wives, a ring composition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يعود الضمير إلى النساء في قوله تعالى { للذين يؤلون من نسائهم } ( البقرة : 226 ) بمناسبة أن الإيلاء من النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r4.claim: The reminder of equal rights fits the preceding mention of īlāʾ, which can involve husbands asserting control over the marital bond at women’s expense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r4.anchor: والمناسبة أن في الإيلاء من النساء تطاولا عليهن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r5.claim: The verse uses symmetrical ellipsis: its full sense is that women have against men rights like the rights men have against women, with each half elided because the other supplies it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r5.anchor: وفي الآية احتباك ، فالتقدير : ولهن على الرجال مثل الذي للرجال عليهن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r6.claim: Women’s rights are stated first because men’s claims over women were long familiar and accepted, while women’s rights were neglected or left to a wife’s standing with her husband; Islam established them, and this verse is a central foundation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p395#2/r6.anchor: وكان الاعتناء بذكر ما للنساء من الحقوق على الرجال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r1.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r1.claim: The majority read qurūʾ on the fuʿūl pattern with hamza; Nafiʿ is reported to double wāw without hamza, and al-Hasan reads qurū with a light tanwīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r1.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «قروء» على وزن فعول، اللام همزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r2.claim: This waiting period serves to establish that the womb is clear, not as worship; it excludes a woman divorced before consummation, unlike the worship-based waiting period after widowhood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r2.anchor: وحكم هذه الآية مقصده الاستبراء لا أنه عبادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r3.claim: The general term is restricted to consummated marriages, excluding pre-consummation divorces, pregnant women, those who never menstruated, and postmenopausal women.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r3.anchor: والمطلقات لفظ عموم يراد به الخصوص في المدخول بهن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r4.claim: Some say those categories were included by the general wording and later abrogated; the author rejects this as weak because the verse concerns menstruating women, the usual case.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: تناولهن العموم ثم نسخن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r5.claim: Qurʾ is a regularly recurring time, such as a star’s rising or setting or the time a wind blows; a rajaz line uses it for anger’s time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r5.anchor: والقرء في اللغة الوقت المعتاد تردده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r6.claim: The Prophet told a woman to leave prayer during her aqraʾ, meaning the days of menstruation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r6.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اتركي الصلاة أيام أقرائك»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r7.claim: Purity is also called qurʾ because it recurs and alternates with menstruation; al-Aʿsha’s poetry uses qurūʾ for women’s periods of purity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r7.anchor: وكذلك على هذا النظر يسمى الطهر قرءا، لأنه وقت معتاد تردده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r8.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r8.claim: Some derive qurʾ from gathering water in a basin: the womb gathers blood during menstruation, and the body gathers it during purity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r8.anchor: وقال قوم: القرء مأخوذ من قرء الماء في الحوض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r9.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي وابن عباس والضحاك ومجاهد والربيع وقتادة وأصحاب الرأي وجماعة كبيرة من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r9.claim: These authorities take the three qurūʾ as menstruations; after divorce during a non-conjugal purity, she waits three periods and exits after bathing from the third.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r9.anchor: فقال أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي وابن عباس والضحاك ومجاهد والربيع وقتادة وأصحاب الرأي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r10.claim: Some who take qurūʾ as menstruations say the waiting period ends as soon as she becomes pure from the third period, before bathing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r10.anchor: وقال بعض من يقول بالحيض إذا طهرت من الثالثة انقضت العدة قبل الغسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r11.speaker: عائشة وابن عمر ومالك وسليمان بن يسار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r11.claim: Aisha, Ibn ʿUmar, Malik, Sulayman ibn Yasar, and many scholars take qurūʾ as periods of purity; the waiting period ends when the third menstruation begins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p304/r11.anchor: وقالت عائشة وابن عمر وجماعة من الصحابة والتابعين ومن بعدهم منهم سليمان بن يسار ومالك: المراد الأطهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r1.claim: A divorce during a purity in which intercourse occurred takes effect, though the husband acted wrongly; the waiting period counts the remainder of that purity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r1.anchor: واعتدت بما بقي من ذلك الطهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r2.speaker: ابن القاسم ومالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r2.claim: Ibn al-Qasim and Malik hold that the marital bond ends when a divorcee sees the first spot of her third menstrual period.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r2.anchor: وقول ابن القاسم ومالك: إن المطلقة إذا رأت أول نقطة من الحيضة الثالثة خرجت من العصمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit and others share that view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r3.anchor: وهو مذهب زيد بن ثابت وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r4.speaker: أشهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r4.claim: Ashhab says the bond and inheritance rights continue until bleeding is confirmed as menstruation, since it could be a nonmenstrual spot.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r4.anchor: وقال أشهب: لا تنقطع العصمة والميراث حتى يتحقق أنه دم حيض لئلا يكون دفعة دم من غير الحيض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r5.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد والربيع وابن زيد والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r5.claim: These exegetes understand what God created in the wombs to include menstruation and pregnancy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عمر ومجاهد والربيع وابن زيد والضحاك هو الحيض والحبل جميعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r6.claim: The prohibition protects the husband from harm and preserves his right of revocation; false menstrual claims can defeat that right or impose unowed maintenance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r6.anchor: ومعنى النهي عن الكتمان النهي عن الإضرار بالزوج وإذهاب حقه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r7.claim: Qatada says pre-Islamic women concealed pregnancy to attribute a child to a new husband, and that the verse was revealed about this practice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r7.anchor: «كانت عادتهن في الجاهلية أن يكتمن الحمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says husbands asked about pregnancy before divorcing to avoid harm to themselves and the child; God commanded truthfulness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r8.anchor: «سبب الآية أن الرجل كان إذا أراد أن يطلق امرأته سألها أبها حمل؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r9.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي وعكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r9.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Ikrima take the phrase to mean menstruation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r10.speaker: عمر وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r10.claim: A view transmitted from Umar and Ibn Abbas takes the phrase to mean pregnancy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r10.anchor: وروي عن عمر وابن عباس أن المراد الحبل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r11.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the broad reading that includes menstruation and pregnancy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r11.anchor: والعموم راجح، وفي قوله تعالى: ولا يحل لهن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r12.claim: The wording implies women are trusted to report what is in their wombs; otherwise withholding it would not count as concealment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r12.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: ولا يحل لهن ما يقتضي أنهن مؤتمنات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r13.claim: The faith condition stresses that genuine faith requires not concealing truth, like telling a free person to stand up for himself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r13.anchor: وهذا كما تقول: إن كنت حرا فانتصر، وأنت تخاطب حرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r14.claim: Ba'l means husband; its plural ba'ulah is anomalous and not productive, but attested usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r14.anchor: البعل: الزوج، وجمعه على بعولة شاذ لا ينقاس.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r15.claim: Some grammarians treat h in ba'ulah as marking a feminine collective; another treats it as a feminine ending added to ba'ul, a regular plural.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r15.anchor: وقال قوم: الهاء فيه دالة على تأنيث الجماعة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r16.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r16.claim: Mubashshir ibn Ubayd reads the h in arhamihinna with damma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r16.anchor: وقرأ مبشر بن عبيد «في أرحامهن» بضم الهاء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r17.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r17.claim: Ibn Masud reads raddatihin with an additional ta.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r18.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r18.claim: Mubashshir ibn Ubayd reads raddihinna with damma on the h.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r18.anchor: وقرأ مبشر بن عبيد «بردهن» بضم الهاء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r19.claim: A husband may revoke a revocable divorce while his wife remains in her waiting period; the demonstrative refers to that period.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r19.anchor: ونص الله تعالى بهذه الآية على أن للزوج أن يرتجع امرأته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r20.claim: The husband may use revocation only to reconcile, not to harm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r20.anchor: ثم اقترن بما لهم من الرد شرط إرادة الإصلاح دون المضارة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r21.claim: Worldly rulings follow outward appearances, while God judges inner states and deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305/r21.anchor: فأحكام الدنيا على الظاهر، والبواطن إلى الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r1.claim: The verse weakens the view that after four months of ila the bond ends irrevocably; the Quran indicates determination to divorce, leaving possible revocation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r1.anchor: وتضعف هذه الآية قول من قال في المولي:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas includes adornment, beautification, and responsiveness in reciprocal rights.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «ذلك في التزين والتصنع والمؤاتاة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd explain reciprocal rights as good companionship, mutual care, and mindfulness of God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك وابن زيد: ذلك في حسن العشرة وحفظ بعضهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r4.claim: The verse broadly encompasses all marital rights.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r5.claim: Mujahid and Qatada take the degree to indicate men's greater share in jihad, inheritance, and similar matters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: ذلك تنبيه على فضل حظه على حظها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم وابنه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and his son interpret the degree as obedience: a wife must obey her husband, while he need not obey her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r6.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم وابنه: ذلك في الطاعة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r7.speaker: عامر الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r7.claim: Al-Sha'bi identifies the degree as dowry and the legal asymmetry in li'an and the penalty for accusation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r7.anchor: وقال عامر الشعبي: «ذلك الصداق الذي يعطي الرجل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the degree urges men to treat women well and be generous in wealth and character; Ibn Atiyya praises this reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p305#2/r8.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: «تلك الدرجة إشارة إلى حض الرجال على حسن العشرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the degree as maintenance and the husband's position as caretaker.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r1.anchor: «الدرجة الإنفاق وأنه قوام عليها» ، وقال ابن زيد:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the degree to mean the husband's control of the marital bond, including that divorce is in his hand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r2.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: «الدرجة ملك العصمة وأن الطلاق بيده» ،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r3.speaker: حميد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r3.claim: Humayd identifies the degree with the beard; Ibn Atiyya says this is weak if authentic and unsupported by the wording or meaning.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r4.claim: The reported interpretations together imply male preference; Ibn Atiyya rejects the beard explanation as textually and semantically weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r4.anchor: وهذا إن صح عنه ضعيف لا يقتضيه لفظ الآية ولا معناها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r5.claim: God cannot be thwarted and is wise in the rulings and affairs He executes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p306/r5.anchor: وعزيز لا يعجزه أحد، وحكيم فيما ينفذه من الأحكام والأمور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that women manipulated pregnancy claims to secure or prevent their husbands' return; the practice continued into Islam and prompted the waiting-period ruling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r1.anchor: سبب نزولها أن المرأة كانت إذا طلقت وهي راغبة في زوجها قالت أنا حبلى وليست حبلى لكي يراجعها وإن كانت حبلى وهي كارهة قالت لست بحبلى لكي لا يقدر على مراجعتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r2.claim: The author says the divorce instruction in 65:1 was revealed first, followed by this waiting-period verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r2.anchor: فلما جاء الإسلام ثبتوا على هذا فنزل قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari derives talaq from releasing a camel that had been tied; the woman's former marital bonds are likened to a tether that the husband releases.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r3.anchor: فالطلاق التخلية قال ابن الأنباري هي من قول العرب أطلقت الناقة فطلقت إذا كانت مشدودة فأزلت الشد عنها وخليتها فشبه ما يقع للمرأة بذلك لأنها كانت متصلة الأسباب بالرجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r4.claim: Another linguist derives talaq from releasing something from one's hand and says frequent usage differentiates the form used for wives from the general verb “to release.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r4.anchor: وقال غيره الطلاق من أطلقت الشئ من يدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r5.claim: Quruʾ can mean either periods of purity or menstruation; the verb is used for both when a woman enters either state.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r5.anchor: وأما القروء فيراد بها الأطهار ويراد بها الحيض يقال أقرأت المرأة إذا حاضت وأقرأت إذا طهرت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r6.speaker: النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r6.claim: The Prophet's instruction to a woman with irregular bleeding to sit through her quruʾ days uses quruʾ to mean menstruation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r6.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المستحاضة تقعد أيام أقرائها يريد أيام حيضها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r7.claim: Al-Aʿsha's verse about missing the quruʾ of one's women uses the word for periods of purity while away on a campaign.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r7.anchor: لما ضاع فيها من قروء نسائكا أراد بالقروء الأطهار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the root means a time or appointed period: both menstruation and purity occur at their proper times.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r8.anchor: واختلف أهل اللغة في أصل القروء على قولين أحدهما أن أصله الوقت يقال رجع فلان لقرئه أي لوقته الذي كان يرجع فيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r9.speaker: الشاعر الهذلي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r9.claim: A Huthayli poet's phrase about winds returning to their qariʾ supports the sense of a recurrent time.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r9.anchor: ورجع لقارئه أيضا قال الهذلي كرهت العقر عقر بني شليل إذا هبت لقارئها الرياح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives the word from gathering: Qurʾan is recited as collected speech, while menstrual blood gathers in the body or womb; either account is possible.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p258#2/r10.anchor: والثاني أن أصله الجمع وقولهم قرأت القرآن أي لفظت به مجموعا والقرء اجتماع الدم في البدن وذلك إنما يكون في الطهر وقد يجوز أن يكون اجتماعه في الرحم وكلاهما حسن هذا قول الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r1.speaker: عمر، علي، ابن مسعود، أبو موسى، عبادة بن الصامت، أبو الدرداء، عكرمة، الضحاك، السدي، سفيان الثوري، الأوزاعي، الحسن بن صالح، أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، أحمد بن حنبل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r1.claim: They interpret qurūʾ as menstruations; Ahmad says he once held that it meant clean intervals but now adopts menstruation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r1.anchor: واختلف الفقهاء في الأقراء على قولين أحدهما أنها الحيض روي عن عمر وعلي وابن مسعود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت، ابن عمر، عائشة، الزهري، أبان بن عثمان، مالك بن أنس، الشافعي، أحمد بن حنبل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r2.claim: They interpret qurūʾ as clean intervals; Ahmad had indicated this view before adopting menstruation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها الأطهار روي عن زيد بن ثابت وابن عمر وعائشة والزهري وأبان بن عثمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r3.claim: The declarative wording that divorced women wait functions as a command, like the command phrased as a report in 2:233; conversely, a command can be phrased as a report in 19:75.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r3.anchor: لفظ الخبر ومعناه الأمر كقوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r4.claim: Here the divorced women are adult women whose marriages were consummated and who are not pregnant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p259/r4.anchor: والمراد بالمطلقات في هذه الآية البالغات المدخول بهن غير الحوامل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r1.speaker: عمر، ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة، مقاتل، ابن قتيبة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r1.claim: One view is that what women must not conceal in their wombs is pregnancy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r1.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه الحمل قاله عمر و ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r2.speaker: عكرمة، عطية، النخعي، الزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r2.claim: A second view identifies what must not be concealed as menstruation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه الحيض قاله عكرمة وعطية والنخعي والزهري والثالث الحمل والحيض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r3.speaker: ابن عمر، ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r3.claim: A third view includes both pregnancy and menstruation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r3.anchor: والثالث الحمل والحيض قاله ابن عمر وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r4.claim: The condition is phrased as a threat and emphasis, like telling a man, “If you are a believer, do not act unjustly.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r4.anchor: خرج مخرج الوعيد لهن والتوكيد قال الزجاج وهو كما تقول للرجل إن كنت مؤمنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r5.claim: One reason for the threat is the husband's entitlement to take his wife back during the waiting period.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r5.anchor: وفي سبب وعيدهم بذلك قولان احدهما أنه لأجل ما يستحقه الزوج من الرجعة قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r6.claim: Another reason for the warning is to prevent a child from being attributed to someone other than his father.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r6.anchor: والثاني لأجل إلحاق الولد بغير أبيه قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r7.claim: A woman who wanted her husband might claim menstruation after becoming clean; one who no longer wanted him could conceal menstruation until bathing and thereby forfeit his chance to return.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r7.anchor: كانت المرأة إذا رغبت في زوجها قالت إني حائض وقد طهرت و إذا زهدت فيه كتمت حيضها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r8.speaker: مجاهد، النخعي، قتادة وآخرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r8.claim: Baʿūla means husbands, and “that” points to the waiting period.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r8.anchor: والبعولة الأزواج و ذلك إشارة إلى العدة قاله مجاهد والنخعي وقتادة في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r9.claim: A specific qualification at the end does not restrict the general opening: divorced women broadly must wait, while the right to take them back applies specifically to revocable divorces.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p260/r9.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على أن خصوص آخر اللفظ لا يمنع عموم اوله ولا يوجب تخصيصه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r1.claim: Men used to harm wives by repeatedly divorcing them once, returning as the waiting period neared its end, leaving them for a while, then divorcing again; they were forbidden this practice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r1.anchor: قيل إن الرجل كان إذا أراد الإضرار بامرأته طلقها واحدة وتكرها فاذا قارب انقضاء عدتها راجعها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r2.claim: The verse's apparent sense allows return only when the husband does not intend harm by prolonging her waiting period.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r2.anchor: وظاهر الآية يقتضي أنه إنما يملك الرجعة على غير وجه المضارة بتطويل العدة عليها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r3.claim: Yet 2:231 shows a return intended to cause harm is valid: otherwise the husband would not be a wrongdoer by carrying it out.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r3.anchor: لو لم تكن صحيحة إذا وقعت على وجه الضرار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r4.claim: The reciprocal rights mean good treatment and beautiful companionship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r4.anchor: وهو المعاشرة الحسنة والصحبة الجميلة روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سئل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r5.claim: The Prophet said a wife's rights include food and clothing on the same basis as her husband, no striking her face or insulting her, and no banishment except within the home.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r5.anchor: أنه سئل عن حق المرأة على الزوج فقال أن يطعمها إذا طعم ويكسوها إذا اكتسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas said he likes to adorn himself for his wife just as he likes her to adorn herself for him, citing this verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس إني احب أن أتزين للمرأة كما أحب أن تتزين لي لهذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the husband's degree as the dowry he paid and the money he spent on her.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس بما ساق إليها من المهر وأنفق عليها من المال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the degree as jihad and inheritance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد بالجهاد والميراث وقال أبو مالك يطلقها وليس لها من الأمر شيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r3.claim: Abu Malik says the husband may divorce her while she has no control over the matter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو مالك يطلقها وليس لها من الأمر شيء وقال الزجاج تنال منه من اللذة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r4.claim: Zajjaj says she derives pleasure from him as he does from her, but he has a further advantage through his spending on her.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج تنال منه من اللذة كما ينال منها وله الفضل بنفقته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that, if commanded to prostrate to anyone, he would command a wife to prostrate to her husband.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r5.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لو أمرت أحدا أن يسجد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r6.speaker: ابنة سعيد بن المسيب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib's daughter said women addressed their husbands only as people address their governors.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r6.anchor: وقالت ابنة سعيد بن المسيب ما كنا نكلم ازواجنا إلا كما تكلمون أمراءكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r7.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r7.claim: One group counts this verse among abrogated passages and identifies the waiting rule as abrogated in cases specified by other verses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r7.anchor: اختلف العلماء في هذه الآية هل تدخل في الآيات المنسوخات أم لا على قولين أحدهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك وآخرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r8.claim: Within the abrogation view, they say the three-cycle rule was superseded for pregnant women by 65:4 and for women divorced before consummation by 33:49.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r8.anchor: فكان يجب على كل مطلقة أن تعتد بثلاثة قروء فنسخ حكم الحامل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r9.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r9.claim: Another abrogation view says the return clause was superseded by 2:230, since a husband had formerly been entitled to return his wife even after three divorces.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r9.anchor: قالوا كان الرجل إذا طلق امرأته كان أحق برجعتها سواء كان الطلاق ثلاثا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r10.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r10.claim: The opposing position holds the whole verse to be operative: later waiting-period verses specify the general rule rather than abrogate it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r10.anchor: والقول الثاني أن الآية كلها محكمة فأولها عام والآيات الواردة في العدد خصت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi prefers that the verse is wholly operative: husbands may return wives only during the three-cycle waiting period, before it ends.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p261#2/r11.anchor: في العدة قبل انقضاء القروء الثلاثة وهذا القول هو الصحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r1.claim: Divorced wives who have consummated marriages and menstruate must wait three quruʾ before they may marry again.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r1.anchor: هذا الأمر من الله سبحانه وتعالى للمطلقات المدخول بهن من ذوات الأقراء، بأن يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r2.speaker: الأئمة الأربعة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r2.claim: The four imams hold that an enslaved woman waits two quruʾ, half the free woman's term; a quruʾ cannot be divided, so the count is completed as two.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r2.anchor: وقد أخرج الأئمة الأربعة من هذا العموم الأمة إذا طلقت، فإنها تعتد عندهم بقرءين، لأنها على النصف من الحرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r3.speaker: عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r3.claim: A report says an enslaved woman's divorce count is two and her waiting period is two menstruations; Ibn Kathir calls its transmitter Mzahir extremely weak, and al-Daraqutni says the correct version is al-Qasim's own statement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r3.anchor: عن عائشة: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "طلاق الأمة تطليقتان وعدتها حيضتان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r4.speaker: ابن عمر وعمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r4.claim: Ibn Majah transmits a raised report from Ibn Umar, but al-Daraqutni prefers Salim and Nafi's version as Ibn Umar's own view, similarly reported from Umar; they say no Companion's disagreement was known.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r4.anchor: ورواه ابن ماجه من طريق عطية العوفي عن ابن عمر مرفوعا. قال الدارقطني: والصحيح ما رواه سالم ونافع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r5.speaker: ابن سيرين وبعض أهل الظاهر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r5.claim: Some early scholars say enslaved women have the free woman's waiting period because the verse is general and menstruation is a natural bodily process common to both; Ibn Abd al-Barr reports and weakens this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r5.anchor: حكى هذا القول الشيخ أبو عمر بن عبد البر، عن محمد بن سيرين وبعض أهل الظاهر، وضعفه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r6.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن الأنصارية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r6.claim: Asma says she was the first divorced woman for whom a waiting period was established when this verse was revealed; Ibn Abi Hatim calls this report strange by this chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p606#2/r6.anchor: أن أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن الأنصارية قالت: طلقت على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولم يكن للمطلقة عدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r1.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman says every jurist he knew held Aisha's view that quruʾ are intervals of purity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر بن عبد الرحمن يقول: ما أدركت أحدا من فقهائنا إلا وهو يقول ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r2.claim: Ibn Umar says a woman is clear of her husband once she enters the blood of her third menstrual period; Malik says this is the established practice in his community.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r2.anchor: عن نافع، عن عبد الله بن عمر، أنه كان يقول: إذا طلق الرجل امرأته فدخلت في الدم من الحيضة الثالثة فقد برئت منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، وزيد بن ثابت، وسالم، والقاسم، وعروة، وسليمان بن يسار، وأبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن، وأبان بن عثمان، وعطاء، وقتادة، والزهري وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r3.claim: These authorities, and Malik, al-Shafi'i, Dawud, Abu Thawr, and one report from Ahmad, count quruʾ as purity; the purity in which divorce is pronounced counts among the three.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r3.anchor: وروي مثله عن ابن عباس وزيد بن ثابت، وسالم، والقاسم، وعروة، وسليمان بن يسار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r4.claim: For the purity-view jurists, the waiting period ends when the third menstruation begins, and the shortest time a woman can truthfully report is 32 days and two moments.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r4.anchor: إن المعتدة تنقضي عدتها وتبين من زوجها بالطعن في الحيضة الثالثة، وأقل مدة تصدق فيها المرأة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r5.speaker: الأعشى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r5.claim: Abu Ubayd and others cite al-Aʿsha's poem as evidence for quruʾ meaning intervals of purity, describing wives' purity days lost to their husbands' campaigning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r5.anchor: واستشهد أبو عبيد وغيره على ذلك بقول الشاعر -وهو الأعشى -: ففي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r6.speaker: الثوري ومن وافقه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r6.claim: The second view takes quruʾ as menstruations: the waiting period ends only when the third period finishes, with some requiring a ritual bath; the shortest asserted duration is 33 days and one moment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r6.anchor: والقول الثاني: أن المراد بالأقراء: الحيض، فلا تنقضي العدة حتى تطهر من الحيضة الثالثة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r7.speaker: علقمة عن عمر وابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r7.claim: A woman whose husband had divorced her asks about remarriage after her bleeding stopped but before she could pray; Ibn Masud says she remains his wife until prayer is lawful, and Umar agrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p607/r7.anchor: قال الثوري: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، عن علقمة قال: كنا عند عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، فجاءته امرأة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r1.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي وابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r1.claim: Many early authorities count quruʾ as menstruations; this is the Hanafi position, the stronger report from Ahmad, and the views of al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, and others; senior Companions are cited in support.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r1.anchor: وهكذا روي عن أبي بكر الصديق، وعمر، وعثمان، وعلي، وأبي الدرداء، وعبادة بن الصامت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r2.speaker: فاطمة بنت أبي حبيش عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r2.claim: A report tells Fatima to stop praying during her quruʾ, which would plainly mean menstruation if authentic; Abu Hatim calls its transmitter Mundhir ibn al-Mughira unknown, though Ibn Hibban lists him among trustworthy narrators.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r2.anchor: عن عروة بن الزبير، عن فاطمة بنت أبي حبيش أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لها: "دعي الصلاة أيام أقرائك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir defines quruʾ as the appointed time for a regularly recurring thing to arrive or depart; this allows the word to cover both menstruation and purity, a shared-word analysis adopted by some legal theorists.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: أصل القرء في كلام العرب: "الوقت لمجيء الشيء المعتاد مجيئه في وقت معلوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r4.speaker: الأصمعي وأبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r4.claim: Al-Asma'i says quruʾ means a time; Abu Amr says Arabs use it for menstruation, purity, and both together.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r4.anchor: وهذا قول الأصمعي: أن القرء هو الوقت. وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: العرب تسمي الحيض: قرءا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r5.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r5.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says Arab linguists and jurists agree that quruʾ can mean either menstruation or purity; their disagreement is which sense the verse intends.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p608/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو عمر بن عبد البر: لا يختلف أهل العلم بلسان العرب والفقهاء أن القرء يراد به الحيض ويراد به الطهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر ومجاهد والشعبي وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r1.claim: What divorced women may not conceal in their wombs means pregnancy or menstruation, according to Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, al-Hakam ibn Utayba, and others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r1.anchor: أي: من حبل أو حيض. قاله ابن عباس، وابن عمر، ومجاهد، والشعبي، والحكم بن عيينة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r2.claim: The warning makes the woman's truthful report authoritative because she alone normally knows whether she is pregnant or menstruating and proof is usually unavailable; she must not lie to shorten or lengthen the waiting period for advantage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r2.anchor: المرجع في هذا إليهن؛ لأنه أمر لا يعلم إلا من جهتين، وتتعذر إقامة البينة غالبا على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r3.claim: A husband may take back his wife during her waiting period if he seeks reconciliation and good; this applies to revocable divorces.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r3.anchor: وزوجها الذي طلقها أحق بردتها ما دامت في عدتها، إذا كان مراده بردتها الإصلاح والخير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r4.claim: At this verse's revelation, a husband could take back a wife even after a hundred divorces; the next verse's limit of three created irrevocable as well as revocable divorces, so this passage does not fit the legal-theory example of a pronoun restricting an earlier general term.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609/r4.anchor: فأما حال نزول هذه الآية فكان الرجل أحق برجعة امرأته وإن طلقها مائة مرة، فلما قصروا في الآية التي بعدها على ثلاث تطليقات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r1.claim: Women have rights over men comparable to men's rights over them; each spouse should discharge the other's due fairly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r1.anchor: ولهُن على الرجال من الحق مثل ما للرجال عليهن، فليؤد كل واحد منهما إلى الآخر ما يجب عليه بالمعروف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r2.speaker: جابر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r2.claim: In the Farewell Pilgrimage sermon, the Prophet tells men to fear God concerning women, notes the marital trust, sets household and sexual obligations, and requires food and clothing for wives according to customary standards; Muslim records the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r2.anchor: كما ثبت في صحيح مسلم، عن جابر، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال في خطبته، في حجة الوداع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r3.speaker: معاوية بن حيدة عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r3.claim: Asked about a wife's rights, the Prophet says to feed and clothe her as oneself, not strike her face or insult her, and not abandon her except within the home.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r3.anchor: وفي حديث بهز بن حكيم، عن معاوية بن حيدة القشيري، عن أبيه، عن جده، أنه قال: يا رسول الله، ما حق زوجة أحدنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says he likes to adorn himself for his wife as he likes her to adorn herself for him, citing this verse; al-Tabari and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p609#2/r4.anchor: وقال وكيع عن بشير بن سليمان، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: إني لأحب أن أتزين للمرأة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p610/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p610/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p610/r1.claim: Men have a degree in virtue, status, being obeyed, financial provision, managing interests, and merit in this world and the next; Ibn Kathir links this to 4:34.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p610/r1.anchor: في الفضيلة في الخلق، والمنزلة، وطاعة الأمر، والإنفاق، والقيام بالمصالح، والفضل في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p610/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p610/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p610/r2.claim: God is mighty in requiting those who disobey and oppose His command, and wise in His command, law, and decree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p610/r2.anchor: عزيز في انتقامه ممن عصاه وخالف أمره، حكيم في أمره وشرعه وقدره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet’s comparison: a Qur’an reader resembles a citron with pleasant taste and scent, while a nonreader resembles a date with pleasant taste but no scent; a wicked reader is like fragrant but bitter basil, and a wicked nonreader like a bitter, scentless colocynth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى، رضي الله عنهما، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " مثل الذي يقرأ القرآن كمثل الأترجة، طعمها طيب وريحها طيب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.claim: The chapter fits the report because fragrance tracks the presence of Qur’an recitation, showing the Qur’an’s superiority over speech from both righteous and wicked people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.anchor: ووجه مناسبة الباب لهذا الحديث: أن طيب الرائحة دار مع القرآن وجودا وعدما، فدل على شرفه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Muslim community’s allotted time is like the span from afternoon prayer to sunset, after the Jews’ morning-to-noon span and the Christians’ noon-to-afternoon span; Muslims receive two qirāṭs per worker while each earlier community received one.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.anchor: قال: سمعت ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إنما أجلكم في أجل من خلا من الأمم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.claim: Although its era is shorter, the Muslim community surpasses earlier communities by God’s favor, as 3:110 states; the workers’ extra reward is grace, not an injustice to the earlier communities.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.anchor: أن هذه الأمة مع قصر مدتها فضلت الأمم الماضية مع طول مدتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.claim: Bahz ibn Ḥakīm reports from his father and grandfather that the Prophet said Muslims complete seventy nations and are the best and most honored before God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.anchor: عن بهز بن حكيم، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أنتم توفون سبعين أمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.claim: The community’s distinction comes through the blessed Qur’an, which God made superior to, authoritative over, abrogating, and final among the revealed books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.anchor: ببركة الكتاب العظيم الذي شرفه الله تعالى على كل كتاب أنزله، جعله مهيمنا عليه، وناسخا له، وخاتما له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r7.claim: Earlier scriptures came down all at once, but the Qur’an came in stages according to events; each descent was like the arrival of one earlier book, reflecting special care for it and its Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r7.anchor: لأن كل الكتب المتقدمة نزلت إلى الأرض جملة واحدة، وهذا القرآن نزل منجما بحسب الوقائع لشدة الاعتناء به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r8.claim: The Jews’ period ran from Moses to Jesus, the Christians’ from then until Muḥammad, and the Muslim community’s until the Hour; its doubled reward is God’s favor, supported by 57:28–29.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57#2/r8.anchor: فاليهود استعملهم الله من لدن موسى إلى زمان عيسى، والنصارى من ثم إلى أن بعث محمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p66/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p66/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p66/r1.claim: Abū Kabsha al-Anmārī reports the Prophet’s comparison of four people: the knowledgeable wealthy person who spends rightly and the knowledgeable poor person who wishes to do the same share reward; the wealthy wrongdoer and the poor person who wishes to do the same share sin. Ibn Kathir grades the isnad sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p66/r1.anchor: عن أبي كبشة الأنماري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " مثل هذه الأمة مثل أربعة نفر

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r1.claim: Ṭalāq derives from release or loosening the marital bond; in legal usage it specifically means divorce of wives and takes effect without intention.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r1.anchor: الطلاق: عن الإطلاق، وهو التخلية من حبالة الزوج، يقال: أطلقت البعير، وطلقت المرأة، وقد صار التطليق في عرف الشرع يختص بالزوجات حتى يقع من غير نية

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r2.claim: Iṭlāq and inṭilāq are used both for wives and for other things.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r2.anchor: والإطلاق والانطلاق يستعمل فيه وفي غيره

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r4.claim: Qurūʾ can mean either purity or menstruation, making it a word with opposite senses.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r4.anchor: والقرء: الطهر والحيض، وهو من الأضداد

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r5.speaker: الأصمعي والأخفش والفراء والكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r5.claim: One proposed origin is gathering: blood gathers in the womb, hence menstruation is called a qurʾ; examples include stars gathering at setting and a basin gathering water.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما: من الاجتماع، ومنه أقرأت النجوم

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r6.claim: The plural qurūʾ is used for purity in one account, supported by a line about women's cycles; another explanation uses qurūʾ for menstruation, as in a line likening them to a menstruating woman's cycles.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن أريد به الطهر، تجمع على قروء

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r7.claim: A second proposed origin is a customary time of occurrence; on this account the word works for both purity and menstruation.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r7.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون من الوقت، وأصله وقت الفعل الذي يجري على عادة، عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء وهو يصلح للحيض والطهر

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r8.claim: On the time-based account, quruʾ is the plural used for many, aqraʾ for few; menstruation is the more analogous of the two meanings.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r8.anchor: وجمعه في التكثير قروء، وفي التقليل: أقراء

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda says qurʾ means transition, but the author judges that etymology poor.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r9.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبيدة أنها عبارة عن الانتقال، وليس بالجيد

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r10.claim: Asked whether qurʾ means menstruation or purity, Abu Amr answered that it means both, but menstruation is the more analogical sense.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r10.anchor: وسئل أبو عمرو غلام ثعلب: ما القرء؟ قال: الوقت

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r11.claim: Ḥalāl is the opposite of forbidden: something one may benefit from and that others may not prohibit after it is made lawful.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r11.anchor: والحلال ضد الحرام، وهو ما له أن ينتفع به، وليس لأحد منعه لإحلال غيره له

JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r13.claim: Baʿl means husband; its plural is buʿūl, like fuḥūl and dhukūr.
JISHUMI:v1p906#2/r13.anchor: والبعل الزوج، والجمع: بعول كالفحول والذكور

JISHUMI:v1p908/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r1.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p908/r1.claim: One explanation uses the intensive plural because the waiting period necessarily includes repeated cycles.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r1.anchor: منها لما كانت مطلقة يلزمها هذا دخله معنى الكثرة، فذكر بناء على التكثير

JISHUMI:v1p908/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p908/r2.claim: Another explanation says the plural form fuʿūl is more common for this pattern, whereas the expected small-count form is afʿul rather than afʿāl.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن بناء التكثير فيه أغلب على قياس الباب في جمع فعل، فأما القليل فقياسه أفعل دون أفعال

JISHUMI:v1p908/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p908/r3.claim: A third explanation treats the phrase as a genus plural, like saying three dogs to mean three from the genus.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنه ذهب به مذاهب الجنس، كقولهم: ثلاثة كلاب، أي: ثلاثة من الكلاب

JISHUMI:v1p908/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p908/r4.claim: The numeral is masculine because it follows the grammatical gender of the masculine noun qurʾ.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r4.anchor: لأنه أتبع التذكير اللفظ، ولفظ القرء مذكر

JISHUMI:v1p908/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r5.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
JISHUMI:v1p908/r5.claim: They report that in early Islam a man who divorced a pregnant wife could reclaim her until she delivered; the divorce verse abrogated that practice and established three divorces.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r5.anchor: عن مقاتل والكلبي قالا: كان الرجل في ابتداء الإسلام إذا طلق امرأة وهي حبلى فهو أحق برجعته ما لم تضع ولدها، فنسخ ذلك بآية الطلاق، وجعل التطليقات ثلاثا

JISHUMI:v1p908/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r6.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v1p908/r6.claim: Maqatil tells of an Ansari named Malik who divorced his pregnant wife Qutayla without knowing of the pregnancy; after he learned, he reclaimed her, and she and the child later died, prompting the verse.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هو رجل من الأنصار يسمى مالكا

JISHUMI:v1p908/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r7.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p908/r7.claim: Al-Qadi says husbands used to reclaim wives near the end of the waiting period to harm them through repeated divorces; the verse set a three-divorce limit, barred harmful revocation, and specified its time.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r7.anchor: وذكر القاضي أن الآية نزلت، وكانوا يطلقون، فإذا تشارف انقضاء العدة راجعوا ضرارا بذلك في طلاق بعد طلاق، فنزلت الآية، وبين ثلاثة أحكام

JISHUMI:v1p908/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p908/r8.claim: Divorced women wait and do not remarry for three qurūʾ.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r8.anchor: يعني المخليات عن حبالة الأزواج بالطلاق و(يتربصن بأنفسهن) ينتظرن فلا يتزوجن ثلاثة قروء

JISHUMI:v1p908/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r9.speaker: عمرو وعلي وابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبو موسى والحسن ومجاهد ومقاتل وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه
JISHUMI:v1p908/r9.claim: One legal view counts the three qurūʾ as three menstrual periods.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r9.anchor: قيل: ثلاث حيض، عن عمرو وعلي وابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبي موسى والحسن ومجاهد ومقاتل وأبي حنيفة وأصحابه

JISHUMI:v1p908/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r10.speaker: زيد وعائشة وابن عمر ومالك والشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p908/r10.claim: Another legal view counts the three qurūʾ as three periods of purity.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r10.anchor: وقيل: ثلاثة أطهار، عن زيد وعائشة وابن عمر ومالك والشافعي

JISHUMI:v1p908/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r11.speaker: عكرمة وإبراهيم
JISHUMI:v1p908/r11.claim: One view says women may not conceal menstrual blood.

JISHUMI:v1p908/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p908/r12.claim: Another view says women may not conceal pregnancy.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r12.anchor: وقيل: الحبل، عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p908/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r13.speaker: ابن عمر والحسن
JISHUMI:v1p908/r13.claim: A third view says the concealed matter includes both menstrual blood and pregnancy.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r13.anchor: وقيل الحيض والحبل، عن ابن عمر والحسن

JISHUMI:v1p908/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p908/r14.claim: The prohibition protects the husband from being wronged by the wife's preventing his revocation right.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r14.anchor: وإنما نهى عن ذلك لئلا يظلم الزوج بمنع المراجعة، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p908/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p908/r15.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p908/r15.claim: Another explanation is that concealment prevents the woman from attributing a child to someone other than its father, as in pre-Islamic practice.
JISHUMI:v1p908/r15.anchor: وقيل: بنسبة الولد إلى غيره كفعل الجاهلية، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v1p909/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r1.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r1.claim: Women are trusted to report when the waiting period ends, so they should neither hasten nor delay that report.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r1.anchor: وقيل: لأنها أمينة في انقضاء العدة، فلا ينبغي أن تقدم أو تؤخر

JISHUMI:v1p909/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p909/r2.claim: For a believer, this is the proper rule and characteristic, and she should not act against it.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r2.anchor: يعني من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فهذه صفته وحكمه، فلا ينبغي أن تخالفه

JISHUMI:v1p909/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p909/r3.claim: Husbands have the superior right to restore their wives while the wives remain in the waiting period.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r3.anchor: وبعولتهن يعني أزواجهن أحق أولى بردهن بمراجعتهن ما دمن في العدة

JISHUMI:v1p909/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p909/r4.claim: The phrase refers to the time of menstruation and the waiting period; reconciliation means observing God's obligations and avoiding harm such as prolonging the wait.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r4.anchor: (في ذلك) أي في وقت الحيض والعدة إن أرادوا إصلاحا قيل: أرادوا أداء ما أوجب الله عليهم من ترك الإضرار، بتطويل العدة وغيرها

JISHUMI:v1p909/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p909/r5.claim: Wives and husbands each have corresponding rights, especially in good companionship and avoiding harm.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r5.anchor: (ولهن) أي للنساء على أزواجهن (مثل الذي) لهم (عليهن) من الحق في حسن العشرة، وترك المضارة

JISHUMI:v1p909/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p909/r6.claim: The required obedience of wives is what is recognized as the husband's lawful right over them.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r6.anchor: بالمعروف أي أن الطاعة التي تجب عليهن هو المعروف، وهو ما عرف من حق الزوج على المرأة

JISHUMI:v1p909/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r7.claim: Another explanation takes maʿrūf as good, beautiful conduct that accords with the law.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r7.anchor: وقيل: بالمعروف بالحسن الجميل الموافق للشرع

JISHUMI:v1p909/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p909/r8.claim: One view understands men's degree as superiority or merit.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r8.anchor: قيل: في الفضل، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p909/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r9.claim: Another view ties men's degree to the dowry they provide and their spending on wives.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r9.anchor: بما يساق إليها من المهر، وأنفق عليها من المال

JISHUMI:v1p909/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r10.claim: Another view identifies the degree with men's reason or intellect.

JISHUMI:v1p909/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r11.claim: Another view identifies the degree with inheritance.

JISHUMI:v1p909/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r12.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p909/r12.claim: Qatada interprets men's degree as their duty of jihad.

JISHUMI:v1p909/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p909/r13.claim: Another view, attributed to Ibn Abbas, is that men must exceed women in gracious treatment.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r13.anchor: وقيل: بالأخذ عليها بالفضل في المعاملة، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p909/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r14.claim: Other explanations identify men's degree with maintenance, taking additional wives, divorce and revocation, or testimony.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r14.anchor: وقيل: بالقيام عليهن، وقيل: في التزوج عليهن، وقيل: بالطلاق والرجعة، وقيل: بالشهادة

JISHUMI:v1p909/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r15.speaker: القتبي وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p909/r15.claim: Al-Qutbi and Abu Muslim explain the degree as a special privilege in rights.

JISHUMI:v1p909/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r16.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p909/r16.claim: Al-Qadi says the verse can encompass all of the reported explanations.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r16.anchor: قال القاضي: ولا مانع من حمله على الجميع

JISHUMI:v1p909/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p909/r17.claim: God is powerful, nothing can prevent Him, and wise in that He does only what is good.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r17.anchor: والله عزيز حكيم أي قادر على ما يشاء لا يمتنع، حكيم فيما يفعل، فلا يفعل إلا الحسن

JISHUMI:v1p909/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r18.claim: Another explanation takes al-ḥakīm to mean that God knows everything.

JISHUMI:v1p909/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r19.speaker: author
