JISHUMI:v1p909/r19.claim: Although phrased as a statement, the verse means a command: the divorced woman is legally bound to observe the waiting period.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r19.anchor: فالآية وإن كان لفظها الخبر فمعناها الأمر؛ إذ الخبر بأنها متعبدة بذلك فتؤول معناه إلى الأمر

JISHUMI:v1p909/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p909/r20.claim: The waiting requirement applies to every divorced woman except those excluded by other evidence.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r20.anchor: وتدل على أن كل مطلقة يلزمها ذلك إلا ما قام الدليل

JISHUMI:v1p909/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p909/r21.claim: A woman divorced before consummation has no waiting period, as stated in 33:49.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r21.anchor: فأما غير المدخول بها فلا عدة عليها

JISHUMI:v1p909/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r22.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r22.claim: One view treats the waiting-period rule as specified by the verse in al-Ahzab.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r22.anchor: وقيل: إن هذه الآية مخصوصة بآية سورة الأحزاب

JISHUMI:v1p909/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p909/r23.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p909/r23.claim: Another view says the rule for women divorced before consummation is abrogated; the author prefers this because delaying clarification past the time of address is impermissible.
JISHUMI:v1p909/r23.anchor: وقيل: منسوخة، وهو الأولى؛ لأن تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب لا يجوز

JISHUMI:v1p910/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r1.claim: The rule concerns women who menstruate; postmenopausal women and girls are covered instead by the three-month rule, and enslaved women are outside this verse's three-cycle count.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r1.anchor: وتدل على أن ذلك يلزم صاحبة الأقراء، فالآيسة والصغيرة غير داخلة في الآية، فدخلت في قوله: ثلاثة أشهر، وكذلك الأمة غير داخلة في الآية

JISHUMI:v1p910/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r2.claim: A woman may not conceal menstruation or pregnancy, and her statement about it is accepted, since otherwise the prohibition would have no purpose.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r2.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا يحل كتمان الحيض والحبل. وتدل أن في ذلك القول قولها لولا ذلك لما كان للنهي عن الكتمان معنى

JISHUMI:v1p910/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r3.claim: Concealing these facts to harm the husband is prohibited.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r3.anchor: وتدل على تحريم المضارة بالزوج بكتمانه

JISHUMI:v1p910/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r4.claim: Anyone who knows a religious ruling may not hide it; forbidding concealment of menstruation information makes concealment of religious teachings even more clearly forbidden.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن من علم شيئا في الشرع يحرم عليه كتمانه؛ لأنه إذا حرم عليها كتمان الحيض لما يتعلق به من الحكم فتحريم كتمان الشرائع أولى

JISHUMI:v1p910/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r5.claim: The reference to husbands shows that marriage remains in effect, since divorce does not itself eliminate the right to revoke.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r5.anchor: ويدل قوله: وبعولتهن على بقاء الزوجية؛ لأن الطلاق لا يمنع منه

JISHUMI:v1p910/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r6.claim: Divorce has an effect that a return can remove; scholars differ whether that effect is approach to final separation or prohibition of intercourse.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r6.anchor: وتدل أن للطلاق تأثيرا يزال بالرد لو لم يكن كذلك لم يكن للرجعة معنى، واختلفوا في ذلك، فقيل: إنها صارت بغرض أن تبين، وقيل: تحريم الوطء

JISHUMI:v1p910/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r7.claim: The right of return exists during the waiting period.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r7.anchor: وتدل على أن حق الرد ثابت في العدة

JISHUMI:v1p910/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r8.claim: The passage also says that apostasy removes the effect established by divorce.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r8.anchor: وتدل أن الردة تزيل الأثر الثابت بالطلاق

JISHUMI:v1p910/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r9.claim: The right of return applies to a divorce short of the final divorce, as the next verse says she is not lawful after he divorces her again.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r9.anchor: وتدل أن تلك الردة في طلاق دون طلاق؛ لأنه قال: فإن طلقها فلا تحل له

JISHUMI:v1p910/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r10.claim: The husband alone may revoke during the waiting period; he needs neither his wife's consent nor a new contract or witnesses.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r10.anchor: وتدل على أن الزوج ينفرد بالمراجعة، ولا يحتاج إلى رضاها، وعقد وإشهاد

JISHUMI:v1p910/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r11.claim: Reconciliation is required for the return to be proper, but not for its legal effects to take hold; the community agrees that a harmful return still has those effects, as with divorce during menstruation.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r11.anchor: وتدل أن الرجعة إنما تحسن إذا أراد به الإصلاح، وإنما شرط ذلك في إباحة الرجعة لا في ثبوت أحكامه؛ لإجماع الأمة أنه مع إرادة الأضرار أن يثبت أحكام الرجعة

JISHUMI:v1p910/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r12.claim: Each spouse has rights corresponding to those of the other, especially in marital companionship; the author calls this a remarkably concise statement.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r12.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ولهن مثل الذي عليهن) على حق لكل واحد من الزوجين، وهذا من العجيب الجامع من الفوائد مع قلة الحروف

JISHUMI:v1p910/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r13.claim: Divorce is limited to three for a free man with a free wife and two for an enslaved woman married to an enslaved man.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r13.anchor: لا خلاف أن الطلاق محصور بثلاث: في الحر إذا كان تحته حرة، وثنتين في الأمة إذا كانت تحت عبد

JISHUMI:v1p910/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p910/r14.claim: Abu Hanifa counts the number of divorces by the wife: an enslaved wife has a limit of two.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r14.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة بالمرأة، فإذا كانت أمة فطلاقها تطليقتان

JISHUMI:v1p910/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r15.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p910/r15.claim: Al-Shafi‘i counts the number of divorces by the husband.

JISHUMI:v1p910/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p910/r16.claim: The prescribed time for divorce is a period of purity in which the husband has not had intercourse with her; divorce during menstruation is disliked.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r16.anchor: ولا خلاف أن لها وقتا مسنونا، وهو طهر لم يجامعها فيه، وأنها تكره في حال الحيض

JISHUMI:v1p910/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r17.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p910/r17.claim: Abu Hanifa considers a triple divorce pronounced at once to be a sinful innovation that nevertheless takes effect.
JISHUMI:v1p910/r17.anchor: واختلفوا في الجمع بين الثلاث، فهو بدعة، ويقع عند أبي حنيفة

JISHUMI:v1p910/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r18.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p910/r18.claim: Al-Shafi‘i permits pronouncing three divorces at once.

JISHUMI:v1p910/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r19.speaker: قوم
JISHUMI:v1p910/r19.claim: Some jurists count a triple divorce pronounced at once as one divorce.

JISHUMI:v1p910/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p910/r20.speaker: قوم
JISHUMI:v1p910/r20.claim: Other jurists say a triple divorce pronounced at once does not take effect.

JISHUMI:v1p912/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r1.claim: After three divorces, a woman cannot return to her former husband until she validly marries another man, consummates the marriage, and completes her waiting period.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r1.anchor: واتفقوا أنها لا تحل بعد وقوع الثلاث حتى تنكح زوجا غيره نكاحا صحيحا، ويدخل بها، وتنقضي عدتها

JISHUMI:v1p912/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r2.claim: Divorce is either revocable or irrevocable; an irrevocably divorced woman requires a new contract to return, while a revocable divorce allows return.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r2.anchor: واتفقوا أن الطلاق على ضربين: بائن، ورجعي. فالبائن لا يصح أن يراجعها إلا بعقد جديد، ويصح في الرجعي

JISHUMI:v1p912/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
JISHUMI:v1p912/r3.claim: The apparent position of the author's school is that divorce does not prohibit intercourse.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r3.anchor: فالظاهر من مذهب أصحابنا أنه لا يحرم

JISHUMI:v1p912/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r4.speaker: أبو يوسف والشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p912/r4.claim: Abu Yusuf reports, and al-Shafi‘i holds, that divorce prohibits intercourse.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي يوسف يحرم، وهو قول الشافعي

JISHUMI:v1p912/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
JISHUMI:v1p912/r5.claim: For Abu Hanifa and his companions, revocable divorce is by the explicit divorce formula or phrases such as 'wait out your term' or 'you are one'; it excludes a payment, while euphemisms or payment make divorce irrevocable.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r5.anchor: فقيل: الرجعي أن يقع بلفظ الطلاق، أو يقول: اعتدي واستبرئي رحمك، أو أنت واحدة، ولا يدخل فيه البذل. والبائن ما يقع بالكنايات، أو يدخله بذل، وهذا قول أبي حنيفة وأصحابه

JISHUMI:v1p912/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r6.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p912/r6.claim: Al-Shafi‘i defines irrevocable divorce by whether payment is involved, as in divorce for compensation, regardless of the formula used.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r6.anchor: وقال الشافعي: البائن ما يدخله بذل كالطلاق على مال، ولا اعتبار باللفظ

JISHUMI:v1p912/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p912/r7.claim: For Abu Hanifa, an explicit divorce formula requires no intent; euphemistic wording requires intent or contextual evidence such as anger or discussion of divorce.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r7.anchor: فأما النية ففي الصريح لا يحتاج إلى نية، وفي الكنايات تعتبر نيته، أو دلالة الحال من غضب أو مذاكرة طلاق عن أبي حنيفة

JISHUMI:v1p912/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r8.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p912/r8.claim: Al-Shafi‘i requires intent alone to make divorce take effect through euphemistic wording.

JISHUMI:v1p912/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r9.claim: The only explicit divorce formula is the word ṭalāq.

JISHUMI:v1p912/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p912/r10.claim: They hold that a later revocable divorce attaches to a prior revocable divorce, and an irrevocable divorce attaches to a revocable one, but an irrevocable divorce does not attach to another irrevocable divorce.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r10.anchor: فالرجعي يدخل على الرجعي، والبائن، يدخل على الرجعي، والبائن لا يدخل على البائن؛ فهذا قول أبي حنيفة والشافعي

JISHUMI:v1p912/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r11.speaker: الهادي والزيدية
JISHUMI:v1p912/r11.claim: Al-Hadi and the Zaydis say a further divorce does not attach to a divorced woman until the husband has taken her back, in every case.

JISHUMI:v1p912/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p912/r12.claim: Abu Hanifa says a revocable divorce can attach to a prior irrevocable divorce.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r12.anchor: ثم اختلفوا في الرجعي على البائن فقال أبو حنيفة: يدخل

JISHUMI:v1p912/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r13.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p912/r13.claim: Al-Shafi‘i says a revocable divorce does not attach to a prior irrevocable divorce.

JISHUMI:v1p912/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r14.claim: A waiting period is due for a consummated wife who is divorced or widowed, for an unconsummated wife if her husband dies, for intercourse by mistake or an invalid marriage, and for a freed or widowed umm walad.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r14.anchor: فأما العدة فتجب في المدخول بها إذا طلقها زوجها، أو مات عنها، وعلى غير المدخول بها إذا مات الزوج، وعلى الموطوءة بشبهة أو نكاح فاسد

JISHUMI:v1p912/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r15.claim: For the relevant umm walad and a menstruating divorced woman, the author gives the waiting period as three menstruations; al-Shafi‘i says one for the umm walad.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r15.anchor: وعلى أم الولد إذا أعتقها سيدها أو مات عنها عندنا ثلاث حيض، وعند الشافعي حيضة

JISHUMI:v1p912/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r16.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p912/r16.claim: Abu Hanifa counts qurūʾ as menstruations.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r16.anchor: بالقروء، وهو الحيض عند أبي حنيفة

JISHUMI:v1p912/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r17.speaker: مالك والشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p912/r17.claim: Malik and al-Shafi‘i count qurūʾ as the intervening periods of purity.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r17.anchor: والطهر المتخلل بين الدمين عند مالك والشافعي

JISHUMI:v1p912/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r18.claim: The author prefers menstruation because the waiting period spans three complete cycles and because transfer to months when menstruation is absent shows menstruation is the norm.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r18.anchor: والأول الوجه؛ لأنه يستغرق ثلاثة قروء، ولأنه نقل عند عدم الحيض إلى الشهور، فدل أن الحيض الأصل

JISHUMI:v1p912/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r19.claim: The three-cycle rule applies to a menstruating, nonpregnant woman whose marriage was consummated.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r19.anchor: وهو في المطلقة الحائل المدخول بها إذا كانت تحيض

JISHUMI:v1p912/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r20.claim: A postmenopausal or young girl divorced after consummation waits three months.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r20.anchor: وبالأشهر، وهي عدة الآيسة والصغيرة إذا طلقها زوجها بعد الدخول ثلاثة أشهر

JISHUMI:v1p912/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r21.claim: A widow waits four months and ten days whether or not her husband consummated the marriage.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r21.anchor: وعدة المتوفى عنها زوجها أربعة أشهر وعشر، دخل بها الزوج أو لم يدخل

JISHUMI:v1p912/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p912/r22.claim: An enslaved woman's waiting period is half the free woman's term in months and two menstrual periods when counted by qurūʾ.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r22.anchor: وعدة الأمة على النصف في الأشهر، وفي القرء حيضتان

JISHUMI:v1p912/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r23.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p912/r23.claim: If a husband divorces his wife while fatally ill and dies, and she inherits through his admission, Abu Hanifa requires the longer of the two waiting periods.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r23.anchor: وإذا طلقها في مرضه ومات فورثت بالإقرار على قول أبي حنيفة تعتد بأبعد الأجلين

JISHUMI:v1p912/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p912/r24.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
JISHUMI:v1p912/r24.claim: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the wife in that case waits according to menstruation.
JISHUMI:v1p912/r24.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: تعتد بالحيض

JISHUMI:v1p914/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p914/r1.claim: If menstruation ends after fewer than ten days, Abu Ḥanīfa says the ruling lasts until she prays after tayammum, while Abu Yūsuf and Muḥammad say it ends as soon as she performs tayammum.
JISHUMI:v1p914/r1.anchor: لا تنقطع حتى تصلي، وعند أبي يوسف ومحمد تنقطع بنفس التيمم.

JISHUMI:v1p914/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p914/r2.claim: A woman’s statement is accepted about the end of her waiting period, but Abu Ḥanīfa sets the minimum she can claim at two months.
JISHUMI:v1p914/r2.anchor: ولا خلاف أن القول قولها في انقضاء العدة، ثم اختلفوا فقال أبو حنيفة: أقل ما تصدق فيه شهران،

JISHUMI:v1p914/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r3.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
JISHUMI:v1p914/r3.claim: Abu Yūsuf and Muḥammad set the minimum waiting period she can claim at thirty-nine days.
JISHUMI:v1p914/r3.anchor: قال أبو يوسف ومحمد: تسعة وثلاثون يوما،

JISHUMI:v1p914/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r4.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p914/r4.claim: Al-Shafiʿi sets that minimum at thirty-three days.

JISHUMI:v1p914/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
JISHUMI:v1p914/r5.claim: During a revocable divorce waiting period, the husband may not marry her sister or another four; Abu Ḥanīfa and his companions also forbid this during an irrevocable divorce.
JISHUMI:v1p914/r5.anchor: وما دامت في العدة هل يحل له أن يتزوج بأختها، وأربع سواها قالوا: لا في الرجعة بالاتفاق،

JISHUMI:v1p914/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r6.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p914/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits the husband to marry her sister or another four during an irrevocable divorce waiting period.
JISHUMI:v1p914/r6.anchor: وفي البائن كذلك عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه. وقال الشافعي: يجوز.

JISHUMI:v1p914/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p914/r7.claim: For a freed umm walad, Abu Ḥanīfa bars marrying her sister but permits marrying up to four others.
JISHUMI:v1p914/r7.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة: [نمنع] نكاح الأخت، ولا [نمنع] نكاح الأربع،

JISHUMI:v1p914/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r8.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
JISHUMI:v1p914/r8.claim: Abu Yūsuf and Muḥammad permit both marriages during the freed umm walad’s waiting period.
JISHUMI:v1p914/r8.anchor: وعند أبي يوسف ومحمد لا [نمنع] النكاحين،

JISHUMI:v1p914/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p914/r9.speaker: زفر
JISHUMI:v1p914/r9.claim: Zufar forbids both marriages during the freed umm walad’s waiting period.

JISHUMI:v1p913/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p913/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p913/r1.claim: The passage treats childbirth as the waiting term across divorced and widowed women, women counting qurūʾ, and free and enslaved women; a divorced woman whose marriage was not consummated has no waiting period.
JISHUMI:v1p913/r1.anchor: وضع الحمل ففي الجميع على السواء المطلقة المتوفى عنها زوجها، وذوات الأقراء

JISHUMI:v1p913/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p913/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p913/r2.claim: The waiting period combines God’s right with a human right and is partly devotional: abstaining from marriage, residence, and mourning are devotional, but elapsed time is not.
JISHUMI:v1p913/r2.anchor: والعدة حق الله تعالى مشوب بحق الآدمي، وتعبد للمرأة من وجه

JISHUMI:v1p913/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p913/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p913/r3.claim: If a woman learns of the divorce only after time has passed, the jurists agree that the period starts at divorce; some instead count from when she receives the news.
JISHUMI:v1p913/r3.anchor: فالفقهاء على أنه يعتبر من حين الطلاق، وعن بعضهم من حين الخبر، والأول إجماع الفقهاء

JISHUMI:v1p913/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p913/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p913/r4.claim: Revocation applies to a revocable one- or twofold divorce, not a threefold divorce, a kināya divorce, or a divorce for consideration; al-Shāfiʿī allows it in kināya as well.
JISHUMI:v1p913/r4.anchor: فتثبت في المطلقة الرجعية في الواحدة والثنتين، وتبين في الثلاث، وفي الكنايات لا تثبت الرجعة

JISHUMI:v1p913/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p913/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p913/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa counts intercourse or lustful touching as a return to the marriage; al-Shāfiʿī does not accept return by those acts.
JISHUMI:v1p913/r5.anchor: فعند أبي حنيفة يصير به مراجعا، وعند الشافعي لا تصح الرجعة

JISHUMI:v1p913/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p913/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p913/r6.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says witnesses are not a condition for revocation; al-Shāfiʿī says they are.
JISHUMI:v1p913/r6.anchor: واختلفوا فقال أبو حنيفة: الإشهاد ليس بشرط، وقال الشافعي: شرط

JISHUMI:v1p913/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p913/r7.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
JISHUMI:v1p913/r7.claim: All agree the right of return ends when the waiting period ends; Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad accept a return announced during menstruation if she says the period ended.
JISHUMI:v1p913/r7.anchor: ولا خلاف أنه إذا انقضت العدة تنقطع الرجعة، فأما في الحيض إذا قال: راجعتك

JISHUMI:v1p913/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p913/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v1p913/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa rejects that return when the menstrual period lasted ten days, because the right ends as soon as menstruation stops.
JISHUMI:v1p913/r8.anchor: لا تصح عند أبي حنيفة إذا كان حيضها عشرا، فبنفس الانقطاع تنقطع الرجعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r1.claim: Divorced women are those whose marital ties have been released; talaq means release, like a sheep left without a shepherd.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r1.anchor: يعني المخليات , والطلاق : التخلية كما يقال للنعجة المهملة بغير راع : طالق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r2.claim: Another derivation compares talaq to a horse running a stretch without restraint: the woman is released after previously being forbidden to others.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r2.anchor: وقيل إنه مأخوذ من طلق الفرس , وهو ذهابه شوطا لا يمنع , فسميت المرأة المخلاة طالقا لأنها لا تمنع من نفسها بعد أن كانت ممنوعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r3.claim: A wife is said to be in her husband's bond because she is as if tied to something.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r3.anchor: ولذلك قيل لذات الزوج إنها في حباله لأنها كالمعقولة بشيء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r4.claim: Talaqat al-mar'a can instead mean she gave birth; that sense comes from ṭalaq, the pain of childbirth, not divorce.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r4.anchor: هذا من الطلق وهو وجع الولادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r5.claim: The waiting period is the span of three qurūʾ, whose meaning is disputed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r5.anchor: أي مدة ثلاثة قروء , واختلفوا في الأقراء على قولين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r6.speaker: عمر، علي، ابن مسعود، أبو موسى، مجاهد، قتادة، الضحاك، عكرمة، السدي، مالك، أبو حنيفة، أهل العراق
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r6.claim: The Iraqi position counts qurūʾ as menstrual periods; an anonymous poetic line supports this usage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r6.anchor: أحدهما : هي الحيض , وهو قول عمر , وعلي , وابن مسعود , وأبي موسى , ومجاهد , وقتادة , والضحاك , وعكرمة , والسدي , ومالك , وأبي حنيفة , وأهل العراق ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r7.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r7.claim: The anonymous line uses quruʾ for menstruation, comparing someone's periods to those of a menstruating woman.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r8.speaker: عائشة، ابن عمر، زيد بن ثابت، الزهري، أبان بن عثمان، الشافعي، أهل الحجاز
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r8.claim: The Hijazi position counts qurūʾ as periods of purity, with al-A'sha's line as evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r8.anchor: والثاني : هي الأطهار , وهو قول عائشة , وابن عمر , وزيد بن ثابت , والزهري , وأبان بن عثمان , والشافعي , وأهل الحجاز ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r9.speaker: الأعشى
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r9.claim: Al-A'sha's line refers to what was lost during the wives' qurūʾ, supporting the sense of periods of purity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r9.anchor: لما ضاع فيها من قروء نسائكا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r10.claim: One etymology derives quruʾ from gathering: the Qur'an gathers letters, and Arabic uses the root for food collected in the mouth and water collected in a pool.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p290/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أن القرء الاجتماع , ومنه أخذ اسم القرآن لاجتماع حروفه , وقيل : قد قرأ الطعام في شدقه وقرأ الماء في حوضه إذا جمعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r1.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum's line says the camel had not gathered a fetus, illustrating qara'a as gathering.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r1.anchor: ذراعي عيطل أدماء بكر هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r2.speaker: الأصمعي، الأخفش، الكسائي، الشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r2.claim: On the gathering derivation, qurūʾ denotes menses because blood gathers in the womb, or purity because bodily fluids gather in the body.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r2.anchor: وهذا قول الأصمعي , والأخفش , والكسائي , والشافعي , فمن جعل القروء اسما للحيض سماه بذلك , لاجتماع الدم في الرحم , ومن جعله اسما للطهر فلاجتماعه في البدن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r3.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala gives a second derivation: quruʾ means a due time when a recurring event starts or ends.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r4.claim: Arabic expressions about a need coming due, a star setting or rising, and a wind blowing in its season illustrate quruʾ as a due time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r4.anchor: أقرأت حاجة فلان عندي , أي دنا وقتها وحان قضاؤها . وأقرأ النجم إذا جاء وقت أفوله , وقرأ إذا جاء وقت طلوعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r5.claim: On the time derivation, quruʾ means menses because it is the regular time for blood to flow, or purity because it is the time for blood to be withheld.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r5.anchor: فمن جعل القرء اسما للحيض , فلأنه وقت خروج الدم المعتاد , ومن جعله اسما للطهر , فلأنه وقت احتباس الدم المعتاد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r6.speaker: عكرمة، الزهري، النخعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r6.claim: Ikrima, al-Zuhri, and al-Nakha'i say what women may not conceal is menstruation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r6.anchor: أحدها : أنه الحيض , وهو قول عكرمة , والزهري , والنخعي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r7.speaker: عمر، ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r7.claim: Umar and Ibn Abbas say it is pregnancy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r7.anchor: والثاني : أنه الحمل , قاله عمر وابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r8.speaker: عمر، مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r8.claim: A third view, attributed to Umar and Mujahid, includes both pregnancy and menstruation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r8.anchor: والثالث : أنه الحمل والحيض قاله عمر ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r9.claim: The clause is a threat to women who conceal what is in their wombs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r9.anchor: وعيد من الله لهن , واختلف في سبب الوعيد على قولين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning concerns depriving the husband of his right of return.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r10.anchor: أحدهما : لما يستحقه الزوج من الرجعة , وهو قول ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r11.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r11.claim: Qatada says it warns against assigning a child's lineage to someone else, as in pre-Islamic practice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r11.anchor: والثاني : لإلحاق نسب الوليد بغيره كفعل الجاهلية , وهو قول قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r12.claim: Bu'ul means husbands, a term linked to their elevation over wives through marriage; ba'l means Lord in 37:125 because of divine lordship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r12.anchor: البعل : الزوج , سمي بذلك , لعلوه على الزوجة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r13.claim: Taking the women back means restoring the marriage and applies to revocable divorce, not irrevocable divorce.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r13.anchor: مخصوص في الطلاق الرجعي دون البائن

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r14.claim: Seeking reconciliation means repairing what divorce has damaged between the spouses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r14.anchor: يعني إصلاح ما بينهما من الطلاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r15.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r15.claim: Al-Dahhak says wives are owed good companionship and marital conduct as they owe husbands the obedience God requires.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r15.anchor: أحدها : ولهن من حسن الصحبة والعشرة بالمعروف على أزواجهن , مثل الذي عليهن من الطاعة , فيما أوجبه الله تعالى عليهن لأزواجهن , وهو قول الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says wives have a reciprocal right to adorn and beautify themselves for their husbands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r16.anchor: والثاني : ولهن على أزواجهن من التصنع والتزين , مثل ما لأزواجهن , وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r17.speaker: أبو جعفر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r17.claim: Abu Ja'far says wives have a right not to be harmed by husbands, just as husbands have that right against them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r17.anchor: والثالث : أن الذي لهن على أزواجهن , ترك مضارتهن , كما كان ذلك لأزواجهن , وهو قول أبي جعفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r18.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r18.claim: Mujahid interprets men's degree as their advantage in inheritance and jihad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r18.anchor: أحدها : فضل الميراث والجهاد , وهو قول مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r19.speaker: زيد بن أسلم، عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r19.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and his son Abd al-Rahman interpret it as authority and the wife's obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r19.anchor: والثاني : أنه الإمرة والطاعة , وهو قول زيد بن أسلم , وابنه عبد الرحمن

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r20.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r20.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the degree includes the husband's payment of dower and right to invoke li'an if he accuses her, while she is punished if she accuses him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r20.anchor: والثالث : أنه إعطاء الصداق , وأنه إذا قذفها لاعنها , وإن قذفته حدت , وهو قول الشعبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r21.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada interpret the degree as generosity to her, fulfilling her rights, and overlooking rights he could claim against her.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r21.anchor: والرابع : أفضاله عليها , وأداء حقها إليها , والصفح عما يجب له من الحقوق عليها , وهو قول ابن عباس وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r22.speaker: حميد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r22.claim: Humayd says the degree is that men have beards.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p291/r22.anchor: والخامس : أن جعل له لحية , وهو قول حميد .

MUJAHID:v1p108/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p108/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p108/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets the three qurūʾ as three menstrual periods.
MUJAHID:v1p108/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء ﴾ يعني ثلاث حيض

MUJAHID:v1p108/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p108/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p108/r2.claim: The concealed matter is pregnancy: a woman must not claim she is not pregnant when she is, or pregnant when she is not.
MUJAHID:v1p108/r2.anchor: ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن ﴾ يعني الحمل يقول لا تقول المرأة لست حبلى وهي حبلى ولا تقول إني حبلى وليست حبلى

MUJAHID:v1p108/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p108/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p108/r3.claim: Mujahid takes “during that” to mean during the waiting period.
MUJAHID:v1p108/r3.anchor: وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك ﴾ يعني في العدة

MUQATIL:2:228/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:228/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:228/r1.claim: A divorced woman who menstruates waits for three menstrual periods; Muqatil takes qurūʾ to mean menstruations.
MUQATIL:2:228/r1.anchor: يعنى ثلاث حيض إذا كانت ممن تحيض

MUQATIL:2:228/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:228/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:228/r2.claim: What God created in their wombs means a child; belief in God’s oneness and the resurrection entails not concealing it.
MUQATIL:2:228/r2.anchor: يعنى يصدقن بالله بأنه واحد لا شريك له

MUQATIL:2:228/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:228/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:228/r3.claim: The husband has the stronger right to take his wife back while she is pregnant; the verse concerns Ismaʿil al-Ghifari and his wife, who did not know she was pregnant.
MUQATIL:2:228/r3.anchor: نزلت فى إسماعيل الغفارى وفي امرأته لم تشعر بحبلها

MUQATIL:2:228/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:228/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:228/r4.claim: For reconciliation, Ismaʿil revoked the divorce while his wife was pregnant; she gave birth, then she and the child died.
MUQATIL:2:228/r4.anchor: فعمد إسماعيل فراجعها وهى حبلى، فولدت منه

MUQATIL:2:228/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:228/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:228/r5.claim: Women have rights from their husbands corresponding to the rights their husbands have over them, in fairness.
MUQATIL:2:228/r5.anchor: لهن من الحق على أزواجهن مثل ما لأزواجهن عليهن

MUQATIL:2:228/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:228/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:228/r6.claim: Men have an advantage in rights over women; God is mighty and wise in His merciful ruling concerning pregnancy.
MUQATIL:2:228/r6.anchor: يعنى حكم الرحمة عليها فى الحبل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r1.claim: The divorced women intended are those with whom the marriage was consummated and who menstruate.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r1.anchor: أراد المدخول بهن من ذوات الإقراء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r2.claim: The declarative form means a command; it strengthens the order by presenting compliance as already occurring, like a prayer phrased as a confident report of fulfillment.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r2.anchor: خبر فى معنى الأمر وأصل الكلام ولتتربص المطلقات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r3.claim: The nominal sentence adds emphasis by suggesting permanence, while mention of their own selves stirs women to master desire and wait.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r3.anchor: وفى ذكر الأنفس تهييج لهن على التربص وزيادة بعث لأن أنفس النساء طوامح إلى الرجال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r4.claim: Qurūʾ means menstruations, supported by reports directing women to leave prayer during their periods and setting a slave woman’s waiting period at two menstruations.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r4.anchor: جمع قرء أو قرء وهو الحيض لقوله عليه السلام دعى الصلاة أيام اقرائك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r5.speaker: النبي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says to leave prayer during the days of one’s periods; al-Nasafī cites this as evidence that qurūʾ means menstruation. No grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r5.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام دعى الصلاة أيام اقرائك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r6.speaker: النبي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says a slave woman’s divorce is two and her waiting period is two menstruations; this supports the menstrual sense. No grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r6.anchor: وقوله طلاق الأمة تطليقتان وعدتها حيضتان ولم يقل طهران

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r7.claim: The waiting months for women who no longer menstruate in 65:4 replace menstruations, not intervals of purity, supporting his reading of qurūʾ as menses.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r7.anchor: فأقام الأشهر مقام الحيض دون الإطهار

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r8.claim: The purpose of waiting is to establish that the womb is empty, which menstruation reveals; an enslaved woman’s waiting is likewise measured by a menstruation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r8.anchor: العدة استبراء الرحم والحيض هو الذى يستبرأ به الأرحام دون الطهر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r9.speaker: الشافعي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r9.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī reads qurūʾ as intervals of purity; al-Nasafī argues that this can end the waiting period at two periods and part of the third, so the prescribed three are not completed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r9.anchor: كما قال الشافعى لا نقضت العدة بقرأين وبعض الثالث

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r10.claim: On al-Nasafī’s view, divorce at the end of menstruation does not count toward the waiting period, whereas al-Shāfiʿī counts divorce at the end of purity; three is a fixed number, not fewer.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r10.anchor: فذا غير محسوب من العدة عندنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r11.claim: Thalāthata is either a direct object, ‘wait for three qurūʾ to pass,’ or an adverbial of duration, ‘wait for a period of three qurūʾ.’
NASAFI-FULL:v1p109#2/r11.anchor: وانتصاب ثلاثة على أنه مفعول به أى يتربصن مضى ثلاثة قروء أو على الظرف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r1.claim: The plural of abundance qurūʾ replaces the plural of paucity aqruʾ because the forms overlap in collectivity and qurūʾ was more commonly used.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r1.anchor: ولعل القروء كانت اكثر استعمالا فى جمع قرء من الإقراء فأوثر عليه تنزيلا لقليل الاستعمال منزلة المهمل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r2.claim: What they might conceal is a child, menstrual blood, or both: a woman seeking separation could hide pregnancy to avoid delayed divorce or her husband relenting, or hide menstruation and falsely claim purity to hasten divorce.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r2.anchor: من الولد أو من دم الحيض أو منهما وذلك إذا أرادت المرأة فراق زوجها فكتمت حملها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r3.claim: Invoking belief in God and the Last Day magnifies the warning: one who believes in God and His punishment would not dare such grave acts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r3.anchor: لأن من امن بالله وبعقابه لا يجترئ على مثله من العظائم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r4.claim: Buʿūla is the plural of baʿl, with the feminine tāʾ marking the plural.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r4.anchor: البعول جمع بعل والتاء لاحقة لتأنيث الجمع

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r5.claim: Their husbands are more entitled to take them back; calling them husbands after divorce shows that a revocable divorce does not itself prohibit intercourse.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r5.anchor: أى أزواجهن أولى برجعتهن وفيه دليل على أن الطلاق الرجعى لا يحرم الوطء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r6.claim: ‘Within that’ means during the waiting period.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r7.claim: If the husband seeks reconciliation and the wife refuses, his decision prevails; she has no independent right to refuse the return.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r7.anchor: والمعنى أن الرجل إن أراد الرجعة وأبتها المرأة وجب إيثار قوله على قولها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r8.claim: The husband’s superior right applies when he seeks reconciliation and kindness, not harm to his wife.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r8.anchor: لما بينهم وبينهن وإحسانا إليهن ولم يريدوا مضارتهن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r9.claim: Women have duties corresponding in goodness to their rights, in a manner recognized by religious law and custom; neither spouse may impose what is not owed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r9.anchor: بالوجه الذى لا ينكر فى الشرع وعادات الناس فلا يكلف أحد الزوجين صاحبه ما ليس له

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r10.claim: Equality concerns the comparable goodness of obligations, not identical tasks: if she washes or bakes for him, he need not do the same, but reciprocates suitably as a man.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r10.anchor: والمراد بالمماثلة مماثلة الواجب فى كونه حسنه لا فى جنس الفعل فلا يجب عليه إذا غسلت ثيابه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r11.claim: The men’s degree may be their additional right and merit in managing her affairs, or their maintenance and control of the marriage bond.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r11.anchor: فى اللذة والاستمتاع أو بالانفاق وملك النكاح

NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r12.claim: God is mighty, beyond challenge in His affairs, and wise, commanding only what is right and good.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p110/r12.anchor: لا يامر إلا بما هو صواب وحسن

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله الشيرازي
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r1.claim: In a dream, the Prophet warned that one who knows and follows a path to God but then turns back will suffer a punishment unmatched among the worlds; the report is cited from Lawaqiḥ al-Anwār al-Qudsiyya.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r1.anchor: قال أوحد المشايخ في وقته أبو عبد الله الشيرازي رأيت

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r2.claim: The divorced women intended are free women who menstruate and whose marriages were consummated; nonconsummated women have no waiting period, pregnant or nonmenstruating women count by months or childbirth, and an enslaved woman's period is two cycles or two months.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r2.anchor: المراد بها ذوات الأقراء من الحرائر المدخول بهن

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r3.claim: The root sense of divorce is to remove a bond; the women are those released from their husbands' bonds.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r3.anchor: رفع القيد أي : المخليات من حبال أزواجهن

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r4.claim: The declarative form functions as a command: they are to wait.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r4.anchor: خبر في معنى الأمر أي : ليتربصن وينتظرن

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r5.claim: The باء is causative: they make themselves wait and keep themselves in a waiting state.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r5.anchor: الباء للتعدية أي : يحملن أنفسهن على التربص

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r6.claim: Three cycles is accusative as a duration, meaning the period of three quruʾ, during which they may not marry.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r6.anchor: نصب على الظرفية أي : مدة ثلاثة قروء

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r7.claim: Quruʾ, plural of qarʾ, is an Arabic word with opposite senses, both purity and menstruation, like shafaq for redness and whiteness.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r7.anchor: والقروء جمع قرء وهو من الأضداد في كلام العرب

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions take quruʾ as menstruations: since months replace cycles when menstruation ceases, menstruation must be the original measure.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r8.anchor: ذهب أبو حنيفة وأصحابه إلى أن القروء وهي الحيض

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r9.speaker: الشافعي
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r9.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues quruʾ means periods of purity, reading the timing phrase in 65:1 to rule out menstruation as the time for divorce.

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r10.claim: The author answers al-Shāfiʿī that the command means to divorce women facing their three menstrual periods; divorce comes first and the waiting period begins afterward.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r10.anchor: وجوابه أن معناه فطلقوهن مستقبلات لعدتهن وهي الحيض

BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r11.claim: The disagreement changes the waiting period: al-Shāfiʿī's is shorter, while Abū Ḥanīfa's is longer; for the latter, the remaining purity counts and the period ends only after the relevant menstruation finishes.
BURSEVI:v1p289#3/r11.anchor: وفائدة الخلاف بين الشافعي وأبي حنيفة

BURSEVI:v1p290/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p290/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p290/r1.claim: They must not conceal pregnancy or menstruation, for doing so could deny the husband's child or revocation rights, hasten separation, or lead to abortion; a woman might hide menstruation to secure a divorce during purity.
BURSEVI:v1p290/r1.anchor: من الحبل والحيض بأن تقول المرأة لست بحامل

BURSEVI:v1p290/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p290/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p290/r2.claim: The verse supports accepting women's statements about pregnancy or menstruation, whether affirming or denying them.
BURSEVI:v1p290/r2.anchor: وفيه دليل على قبول قولهن في ذلك نفيا وإثباتا

BURSEVI:v1p290/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p290/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p290/r3.claim: Belief in God and the Last Day, when punishment follows, should prevent concealment; the warning is severe, but the prohibition applies equally to believing and unbelieving women.
BURSEVI:v1p290/r3.anchor: فإن قضية الإيمان بالله واليوم الاخر الذي يقع فيه الجزاء

BURSEVI:v1p290/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p290/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p290/r4.claim: Baʿl originally means lord or owner; a husband is called baʿl because he manages his wife, while baʿūla is a feminine collective plural, with tāʾ marking its collective femininity.
BURSEVI:v1p290/r4.anchor: وأصل البعل السيد والمالك سمي الزوج بعلا

BURSEVI:v1p290/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p290/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p290/r5.claim: Calling a man baʿl after an explicit divorce signals that the marriage bond and permissibility remain; this concerns revocably divorced women, not irrevocably divorced women whose husbands lack return rights.
BURSEVI:v1p290/r5.anchor: ودلت تسمية الزوج بعلا بعد طلاقها الصريح على أن النكاح قائم

BURSEVI:v1p291/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291/r1.claim: A husband's right to return his wife to marriage exists only during the waiting period and ends when it expires.
BURSEVI:v1p291/r1.anchor: فإن حق الرجعة إنما يثبت للزوج ما دامت في العدة

BURSEVI:v1p291/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291/r2.claim: Aḥaqq here means 'rightful' rather than comparative: outsiders have no right to the women, and a wife's refusal does not invalidate her husband's return.
BURSEVI:v1p291/r2.anchor: وأفعل هنا بمعنى الفاعل والمعنى أن أزواجهن حقيقون بردهن

BURSEVI:v1p291/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291/r3.claim: Husbands should return wives to reconcile and treat them well, not to harm them; the intention is exhortation and a warning against abuse, not a condition for a legally valid return.

BURSEVI:v1p291/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291/r4.claim: In pre-Islamic practice, a man might return a wife near the end of her waiting period and divorce her again later to prolong it and harm her.
BURSEVI:v1p291/r4.anchor: كان الرجل يطلق امرأته فإذا قرب انقضاء عدتها راجعها

BURSEVI:v1p291/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291/r5.claim: After establishing that return should benefit a wife, the verse sets out reciprocal rights between spouses.
BURSEVI:v1p291/r5.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى لما بين أن المقصود من الرجعة إصلاح حالها

BURSEVI:v1p291/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291/r6.claim: Each spouse owes the other rights recognized by religious law and custom; equivalence means equal binding force and claim, not identical kinds of rights—for example, a husband owes dowry, maintenance, and housing.
BURSEVI:v1p291/r6.anchor: وجه المماثلة بين الحقين هو الوجوب واستحقاق المطالبة

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r1.claim: Men have an added degree of rights and merit over women, including differences in reason and religion; here the relevant superiority has two aspects.

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r2.claim: First, the husband's rights are greater: he may divorce and revoke during the waiting period, while his wife owes obedience and cannot fast voluntarily or leave home without his permission; her rights include dowry, support, and freedom from harm.
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r2.anchor: لا تصوم تطوعا إلا بإذنه ولا تخرج من بيتها إلا بإذنه

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says both spouses receive the same marital pleasures, while the man's added merit is the care and financial duties he assumes for her.
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r3.anchor: ما أشار إليه الزجاج بقوله معناه أن المرأة تنال من الرجل

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r4.claim: The degree can mean the husband's compassionate responsibilities: dowry, maintenance, housing, protection, care for her interests, and shielding her from harm.
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r4.anchor: فالفضيلة على هذا فضيلة ما التزمه في حقها

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that, were prostration to a person permitted, he would command a wife to prostrate to her husband because God magnified his right over her.
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r6.claim: The verse links to 4:34, where men's guardianship is tied to divine favor and their spending; the added duties make a wife's service in the home more emphatically obligatory.

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r7.claim: God is mighty to punish those who violate His rules, and wise: His laws contain wisdom and benefits.
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r7.anchor: يقدر على الانتقام ممن يخالف أحكامه

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r8.claim: Marriage succeeds when both spouses honor each other's rights and improve their shared life through children, upbringing, kind treatment, home care, and household management.
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r8.anchor: مقاصد الزوجية لا تتم إلا إذا كان كل واحد من الزوجين

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r9.claim: A report calls a woman's good service to her husband her jihad.

BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r10.claim: A report says that a woman who dies while her husband is pleased with her enters Paradise; it is cited in Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn.
BURSEVI:v1p291#2/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث "أيما امرأة ماتت وزوجها راضض عنها دخلت الجنة"

BURSEVI:v1p292/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p292/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v1p292/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he adorns himself for his wife just as she adorns herself for him, treating adornment as a mutual right.
BURSEVI:v1p292/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أني لأتزين لامرأتي

BURSEVI:v1p292/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p292/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p292/r2.claim: A saying compares a woman to a dove that flies once its wings grow, warning that a husband who dresses his wife may find her unwilling to stay home.
BURSEVI:v1p292/r2.anchor: أن المرأة مثل الحمامة إذا نبت لها جناح طارت

BURSEVI:v1p292/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p292/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p292/r3.claim: An anecdote has a man boast that no evil entered his house; a sage asks how his wife entered it.
BURSEVI:v1p292/r3.anchor: وقال رجل ما دخل داري شر قط فقال حكيم

BURSEVI:v1p292/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p292/r4.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p292/r4.claim: Al-Saʿdī's couplet praises a good woman as a source of comfort and asks God for protection from a bad woman.

BURSEVI:v1p292/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p292/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v1p292/r5.claim: An unattributed couplet says a woman's chastity lies in her beauty and that display is forbidden unless lawful.
BURSEVI:v1p292/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : عصمت زن را بمقام جمال

BURSEVI:v1p292/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p292/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p292/r6.claim: A pious Israelite's wife asked to become the most beautiful woman, then left him for rulers; his prayer turned her into a monkey, and his final prayer restored her, wasting all three granted requests.
BURSEVI:v1p292/r6.anchor: حكي أنه كان في بني إسرائيل رجل صالح وكان له امرأة

BURSEVI:v1p292/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p292/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p292/r7.claim: The waiting period of divorced women symbolizes God's patience with servants who sever their bond: He delays turning away, allowing time for heedlessness to lift, love to stir, and repentance and return to arise.
BURSEVI:v1p292/r7.anchor: والإشارة أن المطلقات لما أمرن بالعدة وفاء لحق الصحبة

BURSEVI:v1p292/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p292/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p292/r8.claim: Divine grace calls the repentant seeker to leave the self and come back, and urges anyone seeking success to remain at God's threshold continually.
BURSEVI:v1p292/r8.anchor: فيقال من كمال الفضل والنوال يا قارع الباب دع نفسك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r1.claim: After discussing the oath of abstention and the possibility of divorce, God explains the divorced woman's status.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r1.anchor: لما ذكر الله تعالى الإيلاء وأن الطلاق قد يقع فيه بين تعالى حكم المرأة بعد التطليق.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that a husband once retained the right to take back his wife after divorce, even after three divorces; this was abrogated by 2:229, Divorce is twice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r2.anchor: وفي كتاب أبي داود والنسائي عن ابن عباس قال في قول الله تعالى: { والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء } الآية، وذلك أن الرجل كان إذا طلق امرأته فهو أحق بها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r3.claim: Although general in wording, the verse concerns divorced women whose marriages were consummated; women divorced before consummation are excluded by 33:49, and pregnant women by 65:4.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r3.anchor: والمطلقات لفظ عموم، والمراد به الخصوص في المدخول بهن، وخرجت المطلقة قبيل البناء بآية «الأحزاب»: فما لكم عليهن من عدة تعتدونها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r4.claim: The purpose of the quruʾ period is to establish whether the womb is clear, unlike a widow's waiting period, which is an act of worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r4.anchor: والمقصود من الأقراء الاستبراء بخلاف عدة الوفاة التي هي عبادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r5.claim: The waiting period for a young girl who has not menstruated and an older woman who has despaired of menstruation is counted in months, as explained later.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r5.anchor: وجعل الله عدة الصغيرة التي لم تحض والكبيرة التي قد يئست الشهور على ما يأتي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r6.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r6.claim: Some say the general wording originally included girls and older women and they were later excluded; al-Qurtubi calls this weak and says the verse addresses menstruating women, the usual case.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: إن العموم في المطلقات يتناول هؤلاء ثم نسخن، وهو ضعيف وإنما الآية فيمن تحيض خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r7.claim: Yatarabbaṣna means they wait, as previously explained.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى: { يتربصن } التربص الانتظار على ما قدمناه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r8.speaker: أهل اللسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r8.claim: Linguists take the indicative statement as an imperative, like the command that mothers nurse their children; Ibn al-Shajari cites usage examples and says this is the consensus of speakers of Arabic.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r8.anchor: هذا قول أهل اللسان من غير خلاف بينهم فيما ذكر ابن الشجري.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r9.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects the imperative analysis: the verse reports a legal rule, so a divorced woman who does not wait is outside the law, not proof that God's report is false.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r9.anchor: ابن العربي: وهذا باطل، وإنما هو خبر عن حكم الشرع فإن وجدت مطلقة لا تتربص فليس من الشرع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r10.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r10.claim: Another grammatical explanation supplies an omitted lām, making the phrase mean let them wait.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r11.speaker: جمهور الناس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r11.claim: The majority read quruʾ on the fuʿūl pattern with final hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r11.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «قروء» على وزن فعول، اللام همزة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r12.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r12.claim: A reading reported from Nafi has quru with a doubled, kasra-bearing wāw and no hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r12.anchor: ويروى عن نافع «قرو» بكسر الواو وشدها من غير همز.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r13.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r13.claim: Al-Hasan reads qarʾ with fatḥa on qāf, a silent rāʾ, and tanwīn.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r13.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «قرء» بفتح القاف وسكون الراء والتنوين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r14.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r14.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says quruʾ is the plural of aqruʾ and aqraʾ, with singular qarʾ on ḍamma-bearing qāf.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r14.anchor: وقروء جمع أقرؤ وأقراء، والواحد قرء بضم القاف قاله الأصمعي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r15.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r15.claim: Abu Zayd gives qarʾ with fatḥa and says a woman is muqriʾ when she menstruates; forms also describe her becoming pure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r15.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: «قرء» بفتح القاف وكلاهما قال: أقرأت المرأة إذا حاضت فهي مقرىء. وأقرأت طهرت.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r16.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r16.claim: Al-Akhfash says the verb can describe a woman becoming one who menstruates and gives a form for saying she menstruated once or twice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r16.anchor: وقال الأخفش: أقرأت المرأة إذا صارت صاحبة حيض فإذا حاضت قلت: قرأت، بلا ألف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r17.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r17.claim: Lexical explanations include the cessation of menstruation, the interval between two periods, and a due time approaching, according to al-Jawhari.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r17.anchor: والقرء: انقطاع الحيض. وقال بعضهم: مابين الحيضتين. وأقرأت حاجتك: دنت، عن الجوهري.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r18.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r18.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala says some Arabs use quruʾ for menstruation, some for purity, and some for the combined period of purity with menstruation; al-Nahhas transmits this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r18.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: من العرب من يسمى الحيض قرءا، ومنهم من يسمي الطهر قرءا، ومنهم من يجمعهما جميعا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r19.speaker: أهل الكوفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r19.claim: The Kufan jurists take the three quruʾ as menstrual periods, a view attributed to Umar, Ali, Ibn Masud, Abu Musa, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, Ikrima, and al-Suddi.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r19.anchor: فقال أهل الكوفة: هي الحيض، وهو قول عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وأبي موسى ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وعكرمة والسدي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r20.speaker: أهل الحجاز
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r20.claim: The Hijazi jurists take the three quruʾ as periods of purity, a view attributed to Aisha, Ibn Umar, Zayd ibn Thabit, al-Zuhri, Aban ibn Uthman, and al-Shafiʿi.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r20.anchor: وقال أهل الحجاز هي الأطهار وهو قول عائشة وابن عمر وزيد بن ثابت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r21.claim: Each school explains quruʾ through gathering: blood gathers in the womb during menstruation or in the body during purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r21.anchor: فمن جعل القرء اسما للحيض سماه بذلك لاجتماع الدم في الرحم، ومن جعله اسما للطهر فلاجتماعه في البدن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r22.claim: Al-Qurtubi identifies the underlying sense of qarʾ as a time or appointed interval, as in a wind blowing at its season, and introduces poetry as evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228/r22.anchor: والذي يحقق لك هذا الأصل في القرء الوقت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r1.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r1.claim: A cited poem about the winds blowing at their appointed season illustrates qarʾ as a time.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r1.anchor: كرهت العقر عقر بني شليل إذا هبت لقارئها الرياح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r2.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r2.claim: Al-Aʿsha's poem uses quruʾ for women's periods of purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r2.anchor:
وقال الأعشى في الأطهار:
أفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r3.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r3.claim: Another poet describes a stabbed man with blood like a menstruating woman's, using quruʾ for menstruation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخر في الحيض: يا رب ذي ضغن علي فارض له قروء كقروء الحائض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r4.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r4.claim: Some derive qarʾ from water gathered in a basin and connect Qurʾan with gathering meanings or letters; they also cite a camel that has not gathered a fetus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: هو مأخوذ من قرء الماء في الحوض، وهو جمعه ومنه القرآن لاجتماع المعاني. ويقال لاجتماع حروفه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr rejects deriving qarʾ from gathering water because qarʾ is hamzated whereas the water word is not; al-Qurtubi agrees, following lexicographers who name the water qurā.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو عمر بن عبد البر: قول من قال: إن القرء مأخوذ من قولهم: قريت الماء في الحوض ليس بشيء لأن القرء مهموز

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r6.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r6.claim: Another view defines qarʾ as transition from purity to menstruation or from menstruation to purity; one Shafiʿi position counts only the transition from purity into menstruation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: القرء، الخروج إما من طهر إلى حيض أو من حيض إلى طهر وعلى هذا قال الشافعي في قول: القرء الانتقال من الطهر إلى الحيض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r7.claim: If qarʾ means transition, the word could cover three cycles across both states; al-Qurtubi reasons that the verse does not count transition from menstruation to purity, leaving three transitions beginning with the purity in which divorce occurred.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r7.anchor: فيستقيم معنى الكلام ودلالته على الطهر والحيض جميعا، فيصير الاسم مشتركا. ويقال: إذا ثبت أن القرء الانتقال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r8.claim: Because a Sunnah divorce occurs during purity, the first counted transition begins with that purity; this yields three complete quruʾ without resort to metaphor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#2/r8.anchor: فإذا كان الطلاق في الطهر سنيا فتقدير الكلام: فعدتهن ثلاثة انتقالات فأولها الانتقال من الطهر الذي وقع فيه الطلاق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r1.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r1.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari calls the transition analysis a strong argument for al-Shafiʿi and adds that purity-to-menstruation signals an unpregnant womb, since pregnant women usually do not menstruate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r1.anchor: قال الكيا الطبري: وهذا نظر دقيق في غاية الاتجاه لمذهب الشافعي، ويمكن أن نذكر في ذلك سرا لا يبعد فهمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r2.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r2.claim: Al-Kiya says menstruation-to-purity differs because conception can occur after menstruation and pregnancy may later stop bleeding; Arab praise for pregnancy in purity is illustrated by a poem recited by Aisha.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r2.anchor: والانتقال من حيض إلى طهر بخلافه فإن الحائض يجوز أن تحبل في أعقاب حيضها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r3.claim: Linguists say a woman may have qaraʾ when she menstruates or becomes pure, and also use the verb for pregnancy; they agree qarʾ means a time, leaving the counted unit ambiguous here.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r3.anchor: وقالوا: قرأت المرأة قرءا إذا حاضت أو طهرت. وقرأت أيضا إذا حملت. واتفقوا على أن القرء الوقت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi seeks the counted unit in 65:1: divorce is commanded at a time that counts toward the waiting period, and the following command is to count that period.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r4.anchor: ولا خلاف أنه يؤمر بالطلاق وقت الطهر فيجب أن يكون هو المعتبر في العدة فإنه قال: «فطلقوهن»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r5.claim: The Prophet told Umar to have the divorcer take his wife back and keep her until she is pure, menstruates, and becomes pure again, then said that is the waiting period for which women are to be divorced; al-Qurtubi treats this as explicit evidence that purity counts.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r5.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لعمر: «مره فليراجعها ثم ليمسكها حتى تطهر ثم تحيض ثم تطهر فتلك العدة التي أمر الله أن تطلق لها النساء»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r6.claim: A divorce during menstruation does not count that period, while most jurists count the purity in which divorce occurs; this makes the purity interpretation stronger.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r6.anchor: ولا خلاف أن من طلق في حال الحيض لم تعتد بذلك الحيض، ومن طلق في حال الطهر فإنها تعتد عند الجمهور بذلك الطهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r7.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r7.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman says every jurist they encountered held Aisha's view that quruʾ are periods of purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r7.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن: ما أدركنا أحدا من فقهائنا إلا يقول بقول عائشة في أن الأقراء هي الأطهار.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r8.claim: On the majority purity view, divorce in an unconsummated pure period counts even the remaining moment; after two more periods of purity, the woman leaves the bond when the third menstruation begins.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r8.anchor: اعتدت بما بقي منه ولو ساعة ولو لحظة، ثم استقبلت طهرا ثانيا بعد حيضة، ثم ثالثا بعد حيضة ثانية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r9.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r9.claim: A divorce during a purity in which intercourse occurred is valid but sinful, and the woman counts the remainder of that purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r9.anchor: فإن طلق مطلق في طهر قد مس فيه لزمه الطلاق وقد أساء، واعتدت بما بقي من ذلك الطهر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r10.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r10.claim: Al-Zuhri says that a woman divorced partway through a purity discards what remains and then counts three full periods of purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r10.anchor: وقال الزهري في امرأة طلقت في بعض طهرها: إنها تعتد بثلاثة أطهار سوى بقية ذلك الطهر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r11.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r11.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr knows no other proponent of the purity view besides Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri who discards the remaining purity; on that view release comes only upon entering the fourth menstruation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r11.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لا أعلم أحدا ممن قال: الأقراء الأطهار يقول هذا غير ابن شهاب الزهري

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r12.speaker: ابن القاسم ومالك وجمهور أصحابه والشافعي وعلماء المدينة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r12.claim: Ibn al-Qasim, Malik and most of his associates, al-Shafiʿi, and Medina's scholars say the marriage bond ends at the first spot of blood of the third menstruation; Zayd, Aisha, Ibn Umar, Ahmad, and Dawud also held this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#3/r12.anchor: وقول ابن القاسم ومالك وجمهور أصحابه والشافعي وعلماء المدينة: إن المطلقة إذا رأت أول نقطة من الحيضة الثالثة خرجت من العصمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r1.claim: The Prophet’s permission to divorce during any part of a nonconsummated purity, without specifying its beginning or end, is evidence against al-Zuhri’s timing restriction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r1.anchor: والحجة على الزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أذن في طلاق الطاهر من غير جماع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r2.speaker: أشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r2.claim: Ashhab says the marital bond and inheritance continue until the blood is confirmed as menstruation, so a nonmenstrual discharge is not mistaken for it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r2.anchor: وقال أشهب: لا تنقطع العصمة والميراث حتى يتحقق أنه دم حيض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r3.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r3.claim: The Kufans cite the Prophet’s instruction to Fatima bint Abi Hubaysh: treat the bleeding as a vein, stop praying at menstruation, then purify and pray between periods.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r3.anchor: احتج الكوفيون بقوله عليه السلام لفاطمة بنت أبي حبيش حين شكت إليه الدم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r4.claim: The Kufans infer from 65:4, which names menstruation as what women may despair of and assigns months in its absence, that menstruation is the waiting-period measure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r4.anchor: وقال تعالى: واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسآئكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r5.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r5.claim: Umar said before the Companions that a slave woman’s waiting period is two menstruations, half the free woman’s; he would have made it one and a half if possible.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r5.anchor: وقال عمربحضرة الصحابة: عدة الأمة حيضتان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r6.claim: Because no Companion objected to Umar, al-Qurtubi treats his ruling as consensus, supported by ten Companions including the four caliphs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r6.anchor: فدل على أنه إجماع منهم وهو قول عشرة من الصحابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi reads the three quruʾ as three complete menstrual periods: a purity-based count could include the remainder of the purity in which divorce occurred, then only part of another.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r7.anchor: يريد كوامل، وهذا لا يمكن أن يكون إلا على قولنا بأن الأقراء الحيض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r8.claim: On his view, a woman divorced during an unconsummated purity starts at the next menstruation, counts three periods, and leaves the waiting period after bathing from the third.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r8.anchor: فإذا طلق الرجل المرأة في طهر لم يطأ فيه استقبلت حيضة ثم حيضة ثم حيضة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r9.claim: He invokes the grammatical gender of quruʾ alongside masculine ayyām in 69:7 as a response in the debate over the intended sense of quruʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r9.anchor: لأن اليوم مذكر وكذلك القرء فدل على أنه المراد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa agrees that a woman divorced while menstruating does not count that menstruation or the following purity, but begins with the menstruation after that purity; al-Qurtubi instead counts the purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r10.anchor: ووافقنا أبو حنيفة على أنها إذا طلقت حائضا أنها لا تعتد بالحيضة التي طلقت فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r11.claim: Arabic may use a plural time expression for a partial total: 2:197 calls the pilgrimage months, though the period is two months and part of a third, so three quruʾ can likewise include partial units.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#4/r11.anchor: وقد استجاز أهل اللغة أن يعبروا عن البعض باسم الجميع كما قال تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r1.claim: The phrase in 2:197, “pilgrimage months,” refers to two months and part of a third, illustrating plural wording for a partial amount.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r1.anchor: والمراد به شهران وبعض الثالث فكذلك قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r2.claim: Among scholars who take quruʾ as menstruations, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Tawus, Ibn Shubruma, and al-Awzaʿi say the waiting period ends after bathing from the third period, when revocation also ends.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r2.anchor: قاله سعيد ابن جبير وطاوس وابن شبرمة والأوزاعي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r3.speaker: شريك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r3.claim: Sharik says that even if a woman delays bathing for twenty years, her husband retains the right of revocation until she bathes.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r3.anchor: وقال شريك: إذا فرطت المرأة في الغسل عشرين سنة فلزوجها عليها الرجعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r4.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r4.claim: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh says that entering the third menstruation ends the marriage bond and revocation right, though she may not marry until bathing from it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r4.anchor: وروي عن إسحاق بن راهويه أنه قال: إذا طعنت المرأة في الحيضة الثالثة بانت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r5.claim: A similar position is attributed to Ibn Abbas, but al-Qurtubi calls it weak and counters it with 2:234, where reaching the term precedes freedom to act about oneself.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r5.anchor: وروي نحوه عن ابن عباس وهو قول ضعيف، بدليل قول الله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r6.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi counts the transition from purity into menstruation as a quruʾ, shortening the waiting period: a divorce at the very end of purity is counted at once, and transition into the third ends the bond.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r6.anchor: وأما ما ذكره الشافعي من أن نفس الانتقال من الطهر إلى الحيضة يسمى قرءا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r7.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r7.claim: The majority of scholars hold that a menstruating slave woman waits two menstrual periods after divorce.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r7.anchor: والجمهور من العلماء على أن عدة الأمة التي تحيض من طلاق زوجها حيضتان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r8.speaker: ابن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r8.claim: Ibn Sirin says he would regard a slave woman’s waiting period as the same as a free woman’s unless a Prophetic practice established otherwise, since the practice deserves following.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r8.anchor: وروي عن ابن سيرين أنه قال: ما أرى عدة الأمة إلا كعدة الحرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r9.speaker: الأصم عبد الرحمن بن كيسان وداود بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r9.claim: Al-Asamm Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan, Dawud ibn Ali, and other literalists say the waiting-period verses apply equally to slave and free women.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r9.anchor: وقال الأصم عبد الرحمن بن كيسان وداود بن علي وجماعة أهل الظاهر: إن الآيات في عدة الطلاق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r10.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r10.claim: The majority cite a report from Aisha that the divorce allotment for a slave woman is two and her quruʾ are two menstruations; al-Qurtubi notes that Mazahir ibn Aslam alone transmitted it and is weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r10.anchor: عن القاسم بن محمد عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r11.claim: Ibn Umar is reported to have said that whichever spouse is enslaved reduces the divorce allotment; a group of scholars followed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r11.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر: أيهما رق نقص طلاقه وقالت به فرقة من العلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r12.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r12.claim: Ikrima, al-Zuhri, and al-Nakhaʿi interpret what is in the wombs as menstruation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r12.anchor: أي من الحيض قاله عكرمة والزهري والنخعي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r13.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r13.claim: Umar and Ibn Abbas interpret what is in the wombs as pregnancy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r13.anchor: وقيل: الحمل قاله عمر وابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r14.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r14.claim: Mujahid says the phrase includes both menstruation and pregnancy, on the premise that a pregnant woman can menstruate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الحيض والحمل معا وهذا على أن الحامل تحيض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
