QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r15.claim: Because only women know their menstruation or purity and the waiting period depends on it, their statement about its ending or continuation is accepted and they are entrusted with disclosure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r15.anchor: جعل القول قولها إذا ادعت انقضاء العدة أو عدمها، وجعلهن مؤتمنات على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r16.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r16.claim: Sulayman ibn Yasar says people were not ordered to inspect women’s private parts; the matter was entrusted to women as persons trusted to report it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r16.anchor: وقال سليمان بن يسار: ولم نؤمر أن نفتح النساء فننظر إلى فروجهن، ولكن وكل ذلك إليهن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r17.claim: The ban on concealment protects the husband: falsely claiming menstruation removes his revocation right; falsely denying it can impose extra maintenance or prevent revocation until the term expires; concealing pregnancy can likewise block his right.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#5/r17.anchor: ومعنى النهي عن الكتمان النهي عن الإضرار بالزوج وإذهاب حقه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r1.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r1.claim: Qatada says the verse was revealed because women in pre-Islamic times concealed pregnancy so they could attribute the child to a new husband.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: كانت عادتهن في الجاهلية أن يكتمن الحمل ليلحقن الولد بالزوج الجديد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r2.speaker: رجل من أشجع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r2.claim: A man from Ashjaʿ told the Prophet he feared his divorced pregnant wife might remarry and the child be attributed to another man; the verse was revealed and the Ashjaʿi woman returned to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r2.anchor: وحكي أن رجلا من أشجع أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله، إني طلقت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r3.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r3.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says the scholars known to him reject a claim of three periods and completed waiting period within ten days, unless the woman says she miscarried a fetus with discernible form.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r3.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وقال كل من حفظت عنه من أهل العلم: إذا قالت المرأة في عشرة أيام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r4.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r4.claim: Malik accepts a claim of completed waiting period when the stated duration is one in which it could normally end; if the duration is exceptionally rare, he reports two opinions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r4.anchor: فقال مالك: إذا قالت انقضت عدتي في أمد تنقضي في مثله العدة قبل قولها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r5.claim: In the Mudawwana, Malik accepts a claim of three periods in a month if women confirm it; Shurayh agrees, and Ali praised Shurayh’s judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r5.anchor: قال في المدونة: إذا قالت حضت ثلاث حيض في شهر صدقت إذا صدقها النساء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r6.claim: Ali told Shurayh “qālūn,” meaning he had judged correctly and well, on accepting a woman’s claim when other women corroborated it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r6.anchor: قال له علي بن أبي طالب: قالون! أي أصبت وأحسنت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r7.speaker: محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r7.claim: In Muhammad’s book, the woman is not believed to have completed the three periods in less than a month and a half.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r7.anchor: وقال في كتاب محمد: لا تصدق إلا في شهر ونصف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r8.speaker: أبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r8.claim: Abu Thawr sets the minimum at forty-seven days, reasoning from a minimum purity of fifteen days and a minimum menstruation of one day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r8.anchor: قال أبو ثور: أقل ما يكون ذلك في سبعة وأربعين يوما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r9.speaker: النعمان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r9.claim: Al-Nuʿman and al-Shafiʿi do not believe a claim of completed waiting period in less than sixty days.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r9.anchor: وقال النعمان: لا تصدق في أقل من ستين يوما وقال به الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r10.claim: The conditional is a severe warning that reinforces the ban on concealment and the duty to state truthfully what is in the womb.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r10.anchor: هذا وعيد عظيم شديد لتأكيد تحريم الكتمان، وإيجاب لأداء الأمانة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r11.claim: The conditional does not imply that unbelievers may conceal; like “if you are my brother, do not wrong me,” it means faith should keep a person from such conduct.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r11.anchor: على أنه أبيح لمن لا يؤمن أن يكتم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r12.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, “husband”; he is so called for his elevation over the wife through the marital rights he possesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#6/r12.anchor: البعولة جمع البعل، وهو الزوج سمي بعلا لعلوه على الزوجة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r1.claim: The word baʿl also means lord because of elevation in lordship, as in 37:125, where it refers to a deity addressed as lord.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r2.claim: Baʿl has the plural baʿūla like dhakar/dhukūra and faḥl/fuḥūla; the group feminine ending is emphatic and irregular, so its use is attested rather than extended by analogy, though it may instead be a feminine ending on faʿūl.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r2.anchor: وهذه الهاء زائدة مؤكدة لتأنيث الجماعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r3.claim: Baʿūla can also be a verbal noun; baʿala means to become a husband, while mubāʿala and biʿāl mean intercourse, and a man is his wife’s baʿl while she is his baʿla.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r4.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r4.claim: The Prophet described the days of Tashriq as days of eating, drinking, and intercourse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r4.anchor: قوله عليه السلام لأيام التشريق: «إنها أيام أكل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r5.claim: Baʿl can also mean the owner or master of something.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r5.anchor: وفلان بعل هذا أي مالكه وربه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r6.claim: Here “returning them” means taking them back in revocation; he distinguishes revocation during the waiting period, linked to Ibn Umar, from return after it, linked to Maʿqil.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r6.anchor: أي بمراجعتهن فالمراجعة على ضربين: مراجعة في العدة على حديث ابن عمر. ومراجعة بعد العدة على حديث معقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r7.claim: The general waiting-period clause covers all divorced women, including those divorced three times and those divorced fewer; the right of husbands to revoke is specifically for the latter.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r7.anchor: حكم خاص فيمن كان طلاقها دون الثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r8.claim: There is consensus that a free husband may revoke a consummated wife after one or two divorces during her waiting period even against her will; after it expires, she is independent and can return only through a new proposal and marriage with guardian and witnesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r8.anchor: أنه أحق برجعتها ما لم تنقض عدتها وإن كرهت المرأة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r9.speaker: المهلب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r9.claim: Al-Muhallab says revocation during the waiting period requires no marriage formalities beyond witnesses to the revocation, a consensus he links to 65:2, which mentions witnesses for revocation but not for marriage or divorce.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r9.anchor: قال المهلب: وكل من راجع في العدة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r10.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r10.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says the Qurʾanic evidence cited together with scholarly consensus suffices, without recounting earlier reports on the subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r10.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وفيما ذكرناه من كتاب الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r11.claim: Malik counts intercourse during the waiting period as revocation when he intends to return her, even without witnesses; the wife should prevent intercourse until he witnesses, and Ishaq agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#7/r11.anchor: فقال مالك: إذا وطئها في العدة وهو يريد الرجعة وجهل أن يشهد فهي رجعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r1.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r1.claim: Malik’s intention-based rule cites the Prophetic report that deeds are judged by intentions and each person receives according to what he intended.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r1.anchor: إنما الأعمال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرىء ما نوى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r2.claim: When intercourse occurs without intending revocation, Malik says the husband may revoke during the waiting period but must not have intercourse again until she has completed an interval to establish that his unlawful semen is cleared.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r2.anchor: قال مالك: يراجع في العدة ولا يطأ حتى يستبرئها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r3.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r3.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says that after the waiting period she cannot marry her former husband or another man during the remaining clearance period; a marriage then is annulled, but does not create permanent prohibition because the semen was his.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r3.anchor: قال ابن القاسم: فإن انقضت عدتها لم ينكحها هو ولا غيره في بقية مدة الاستبراء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Sirin, al-Zuhri, Ata, Tawus, and al-Thawri hold that intercourse itself is revocation; witnesses should be used, as held also by the Hanafi school, al-Awzaʿi, and Ibn Abi Layla.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r4.anchor: هكذا قال سعيد بن المسيب والحسن البصري وابن سيرين والزهري

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r5.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r5.claim: Abu Umar reports a view among some Maliki authorities that intercourse revokes in every case, whether intended or not; al-Layth adopted it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمر: وقد قيل: وطؤه مراجعة على كل حال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r6.claim: Scholars agree that a seller with an option to cancel a slave-girl sale can have intercourse during the option period, thereby reclaiming her and undoing the sale; the author says a revocable wife has the same status.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r6.anchor: ولم يختلفوا فيمن باع جاريته بالخيار أن له وطأها في مدة الخيار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r7.claim: A kiss or other intimate touch with intent to revoke counts as revocation; without that intent, kissing or touching is sinful but does not constitute revocation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#8/r7.anchor: من قبل أو باشر ينوي بذلك الرجعة كانت رجعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r1.claim: The Sunnah is to witness revocation before intercourse, kissing, or intimate touching.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r1.anchor: والسنة أن يشهد قبل أن يطأ أو قبل أن يقبل أو يباشر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa, his companions, and al-Thawri count intercourse, lustful touching, or looking at her private parts with desire as revocation; they recommend witnesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: إن وطئها أو لمسها بشهوة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r3.claim: Malik, al-Shafiʿi, Ishaq, Abu Ubayd, and Abu Thawr say these acts do not constitute revocation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r3.anchor: وفي قول مالك والشافعي وإسحاق وأبي عبيد وأبي ثور لا يكون رجعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r4.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Muhammad says revocation is valid by intercourse, a kiss, and all other forms of sexual enjoyment, while speech-based revocation is undisputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r4.anchor: ولا خلاف في صحة الارتجاع بالقول فأما بالفعل نحو الجماع والقبلة فقال القاضي أبو محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r5.speaker: ابن المواز
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r5.claim: Ibn al-Mawwaz includes pleasurable touching and looking at her private parts or nearby beauty when done intending revocation; this differs from al-Shafiʿi’s speech-only rule, also attributed to Abu Thawr, Jabir ibn Zayd, and Abu Qilaba.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r5.anchor: قال ابن المواز: ومثل الجسة للذة، أو أن ينظر إلى فرجها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r6.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi do not allow the husband to travel with a revocable wife until he revokes; Abu Hanifa and his companions allow travel before revocation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r6.anchor: فقال مالك والشافعي: لا يسافر بها حتى يراجعها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r7.speaker: زفر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r7.claim: Reports from Zufar differ: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad transmits permission to travel before revocation, while Amr ibn Khalid transmits that travel must wait until revocation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r7.anchor: إلا زفر فإنه روى عنه الحسن بن زياد أن له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r8.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r8.claim: Malik says he must not be alone with her or enter without permission; she remains covered, he may not see her hair, they may eat together if someone else is present, but not sleep together in one room.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r9.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r9.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says Malik later retracted the permission to enter, maintaining that the husband may not enter or see her hair.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r9.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم: رجع مالك عن ذلك فقال: لا يدخل عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions agree that the revocable wife may adorn herself for her husband with perfume, jewelry, and dress.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r10.anchor: ولم يختلف أبو حنيفة وأصحابه في أنها تتزين له وتتطيب وتلبس الحلي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r11.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab says she should ask permission, may wear clothes and jewelry, and if they share one house they should separate with a curtain; Qatada also recommends announcing entry with a greeting and throat-clearing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r11.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب قال إذا طلق الرجل امرأته تطليقة فإنه يستأذن عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r12.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r12.claim: Al-Shafiʿi treats a revocably divorced wife as forbidden to her former husband like an irrevocably divorced woman until he revokes, and holds that revocation requires spoken words.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#9/r12.anchor: وقال الشافعي: المطلقة طلاقا يملك رجعتها محرمة على مطلقها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r1.claim: By consensus, after the waiting period ends, if a husband says he revoked during it and the wife denies this, her statement with an oath prevails and he cannot take her back on that basis.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r1.anchor: أجمع العلماء على أن المطلق إذا قال بعد انقضاء العدة: إني كنت راجعتك في العدة وأنكرت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r2.speaker: النعمان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r2.claim: Al-Nuʿman does not require an oath in disputes about marriage or revocation; his two companions agree with the rest of scholars that an oath is required.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r2.anchor: غير أن النعمان كان لا يرى يمينا في النكاح ولا في الرجعة وخالفه صاحباه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r3.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r3.claim: If an enslaved wife denies her husband’s claim of revocation after the waiting period, her statement prevails even if her master calls her a liar, according to al-Shafiʿi, Abu Thawr, and al-Nuʿman.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r3.anchor: هذا قول الشافعي وأبي ثور والنعمان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r4.speaker: يعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r4.claim: Yaqub and Muhammad say the master’s claim prevails in a dispute over a slave wife’s revocation and that the master has the stronger claim to her.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r4.anchor: وقال يعقوب ومحمد: القول قول المولى وهو أحق بها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r5.claim: The word “return” implies that the marital bond was removed; al-Qurtubi’s school says intercourse is forbidden to the revocably divorced woman, so return restores permissibility.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r5.anchor: لفظ الرد يقتضي زوال العصمة إلا أن علماءنا قالوا: إن الرجعية محرمة الوطء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r6.speaker: الليث بن سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r6.claim: Al-Layth, Abu Hanifa, and their followers say marital rulings remain intact and divorce only reduces the allotted number; revocation turns the wife back from the path toward separation as the waiting period expires, a figurative return.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r6.anchor: وقال الليث بن سعد وأبو حنيفة ومن قال بقولهما في أن الرجعة محللة الوطء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi distinguishes his school’s literal return: intercourse has actually become forbidden, so revocation restores a real, presently lost permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r7.anchor: والرد الذي حكمنا به رد حقيقي فإن هناك زوال مستنجز وهو تحريم الوطء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r8.claim: “More entitled” is used when two rights compete and one prevails: the husband’s right during the waiting period exceeds her right to herself, which begins only after it ends.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r8.anchor: يطلق عند تعارض حقين، ويترجح أحدهما فالمعنى حق الزوج

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r9.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r9.claim: The author compares the phrasing to the Prophetic statement that a previously married woman is more entitled to herself than her guardian.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r10.claim: Revocation is commendable when intended to repair the relationship and remove estrangement; using it to harm the wife, prolong her waiting, or prevent her release is forbidden under 2:231, though the revocation remains valid and a judge may separate them if the intent is known.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r10.anchor: فأما إذا قصد الإضرار وتطويل العدة والقطع بها عن الخلاص من ربقة النكاح فمحرم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says wives have marital rights corresponding to those husbands have over them; he adorns himself for his wife and does not take every right, so she can claim hers, with adornment kept free of sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إني لأتزين لامرأتي كما تتزين لي، وما أحب أن أستنظف كل حقي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains that wives receive good companionship and kind treatment from husbands just as they owe the obedience Allah has required of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r12.anchor: وعنه أيضا: أي لهن من حسن الصحبة والعشرة بالمعروف على أزواجهن مثل الذي عليهن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r13.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r13.claim: Al-Tabari says a wife’s rights include her husband refraining from harming her, just as she must not harm him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r13.anchor: كما كان ذلك عليهن لأزواجهن. قاله الطبري

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says husbands should fear God concerning their wives just as wives should fear God concerning their husbands; the author says the meanings are close.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#10/r14.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: تتقون الله فيهن كما عليهن أن يتقين الله عز وجل فيكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r1.claim: The verse comprehensively includes all rights within marriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r1.anchor: والآية تعم جميع ذلك من حقوق الزوجية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r2.claim: Scholars explain Ibn Abbas’s self-adornment as matching one’s appearance to age, time, and suitability: a trimmed mustache can suit an older man but look poor on a young man without a full beard.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r2.anchor: زينة تليق بالشباب، وزينة تليق بالشيوخ

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r3.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r3.claim: The Prophet said that God commanded him to let his beard grow and trim his mustache.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r3.anchor: وروي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r4.claim: Men’s adornment also includes suitable clothing and, depending on the individual, kohl; perfume, tooth-cleaning, grooming, purification, and nail-clipping suit everyone, with henna for older men and rings for men of all ages.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r4.anchor: فأما الطيب والسواك والخلال والرمي بالدرن وفضول الشعر والتطهير وقلم الأظفار فهو بين موافق للجميع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r5.claim: A husband should adorn himself in a fitting way to please his wife and help preserve her chastity, and attend to her sexual needs; if unable to fulfill her in bed, he should take medicines that increase potency and desire.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r5.anchor: ليكون عند امرأته في زينة تسرها ويعفها عن غيره من الرجال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r6.claim: Daraja means rank or status; the author also connects its root to a road’s edge, traversing one’s lifetime, stairs, and strength-related words such as rajul and rajīl.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r6.anchor: مدرجة الطريق: قارعته والأصل فيه الطي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r7.claim: The man’s additional degree lies in intellect, strength, financial support, blood money, inheritance, and jihad.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r7.anchor: فزيادة درجة الرجل بعقله وقوته وبالإنفاق وبالدية والميراث والجهاد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r8.speaker: حميد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r8.claim: Humayd is reported to interpret the degree as the beard; al-Qurtubi says this, if correctly attributed, is weak and unsupported by the wording or meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r8.anchor: وقال حميد: الدرجة اللحية وهذا إن صح عنه فهو ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r9.claim: Ibn al-Arabi claims men’s superiority is clear, citing woman’s creation from man and the husband’s authority over her actions, fasting, and pilgrimage.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r9.anchor: قال ابن العربي: فطوبى لعبد أمسك عما لا يعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r10.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r10.claim: Al-Shaʿbi interprets the degree as the bridal payment.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r11.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the degree to mean the permissibility of disciplining a wife.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r12.claim: In sum, the degree indicates preference and that the husband’s right over his wife is more binding than hers over him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#11/r12.anchor: وعلى الجملة فدرجة تقتضي التفضيل، وتشعر بأن حق الزوج عليها أوجب من حقها عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r1.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r1.claim: The Prophet said that if he were to command anyone to prostrate to another besides God, he would command a wife to prostrate to her husband.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r1.anchor: ولو أمرت أحدا بالسجود لغير الله لأمرت المرأة أن تسجد لزوجها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the degree as an exhortation for men to show good companionship and generosity toward women; Ibn Atiyya calls this a fine and excellent interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الدرجة إشارة إلى حض الرجال على حسن العشرة، والتوسع للنساء في المال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r3.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests the degree concerns marital rights: the husband can end the marriage, whereas the wife cannot, and she must answer his call to bed though he is not likewise obliged.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r3.anchor: قال الماوردي، يحتمل أنها في حقوق النكاح له رفع العقد دونها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r4.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r4.claim: The Prophet warned that angels curse a woman who refuses her husband’s call to bed until morning.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r5.claim: Al-Aziz means that God’s sovereignty is invincible and unchallenged; al-Hakim means He knows and acts rightly.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:228#12/r5.anchor: أي منيع السلطان لا معترض عليه

RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r1.claim: A woman divorced before marriage is divorced only in the lexical sense, not by legal convention, and no waiting period is required by consensus.
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r1.anchor: فهي مطلقة بحسب اللغة ، لكنها غير مطلقة بحسب عرف الشرع

RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r2.claim: A married woman divorced before consummation has no waiting period, as stated in 33:49.
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r2.anchor: فإن لم تكن مدخولا بها لم تجب العدة عليها

RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r3.claim: A consummated divorcee who is pregnant waits until delivery, not through menstrual cycles, according to 65:4.
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r3.anchor: فإن كانت حاملا فعدتها بوضع الحمل لا بالإقراء

RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r4.claim: A nonpregnant woman who cannot menstruate because of extreme youth or age counts her waiting period in months, not quruʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r4.anchor: فإن امتنع الحيض في حقها إما للصغر المفرط ، أو للكبر المفرط

RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r5.claim: An enslaved woman counts two quruʾ, not three.
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r5.anchor: فإن كانت رقيقة كانت عدتها بقرأين لا بثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r6.claim: The three-quruʾ rule applies when a woman is married, divorced after consummation, not pregnant, menstruating, and free.
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r6.anchor: فعند اجتماع هذه الصفات كانت عدتها بالإقراء الثلاثة على ما بين الله حكمها في هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r7.claim: An objection says a general term should retain a majority of its cases after specification, like calling a mostly black garment black; this verse appears to exclude five groups and leave one.
RAZI-FULL:v6p73#2/r7.anchor: وهذه الآية ليست كذلك فإنكم أخرجتم من عمومها خمسة أقسام وتركتم قسما واحدا

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r1.claim: A woman divorced before marriage is outside the legal wording because such a woman is not called a divorced woman in this usage.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r1.anchor: أما الأجنبية فخارجة عن اللفظ فإن الأجنبية لا يقال فيها : إنها مطلقة

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r2.claim: The context excludes an unconsummated marriage: the waiting period clears the womb, and that need arises only after prior intercourse.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r2.anchor: وأما غير المدخول بها فالقرينة تخرجها لأن المقصود من العدة براءة الرحم

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r3.claim: Pregnant and menopausal women are outside the quruʾ rule because menstrual cycles do not occur for them.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r3.anchor: وأما الحامل والآيسة فهما خارجتان عن اللفظ لأن إيجاب الاعتداد بالإقراء إنما يكون حيث تحصل الإقراء

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r4.claim: Enslaved women are rare in marriage, so most cases remain within the verse's general wording.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r4.anchor: وأما الرقيقة فتزويجها كالنادر فثبت أن الأعم الأغلب باق تحت هذا العموم

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r5.claim: Although يتربصن is grammatically a report, it means a command; the declarative form avoids implying that the waiting period counts only when begun intentionally.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r5.anchor: قوله : { يتربصن } لا شك أنه خبر

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r6.claim: If a husband dies and his wife does not learn of it until the waiting period expires, the period still counts whether she knew, intended, consented, or was unwilling.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r6.anchor: وعرف أنه مهما انقضت هذه العدة حصل المقصود

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r7.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the declarative form intensifies the command and signals urgency, as though the women had already obeyed; a prayer for mercy uses the same form in confidence of response.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r7.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : التعبير عن الأمر بصيغة الخبر يفيد تأكيد الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r8.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r8.claim: In Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz, ʿAbd al-Qāhir says putting the subject first strengthens the statement; this can single out the actor or establish the actor's characteristic action.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r8.anchor: قال الشيخ عبد القاهر الجرجاني في كتاب ( دلائل الإعجاز ) : إنك إذا قدمت الاسم

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r9.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r9.claim: The fronted subject can specify that actor as uniquely performing the action, or simply establish that the action is the subject's characteristic habit.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r9.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون لتخصيص ذلك الفاعل بذلك الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r10.claim: Rāzī illustrates subject-first exclusivity with 'I write to the ruler on this important matter,' while a statement that someone gives generously confirms a habit without claiming exclusivity.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r10.anchor: كقولك : أنا أكتب في المهم الفلاني إلى السلطان

RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r11.claim: Rāzī cites 16:20 and 5:61 as further examples of clauses with the subject put first to affirm what is said about it.
RAZI-FULL:v6p74/r11.anchor: ومثله قوله تعالى : { والذين يدعون من دون الله لا يخلقون شيئا وهم }

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r1.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r1.claim: The anonymous poet's line front-loads the subject in a statement praising the two men, serving as an example of the construction under discussion.

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r2.claim: Naming the subject first creates anticipation for the predicate; when it arrives, it is received more forcefully, confirming the statement and removing doubt.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r2.anchor: فيحصل في العقل شوق إلى معرفة ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r3.claim: Mentioning their selves incites women to wait by urging them to restrain their longing for men and overcome their own desires.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r3.anchor: في ذكر الأنفس تهييج لهن على التربص وزيادة بعث

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r4.claim: Rāzī contrasts the wording here with 2:226, which commands a four-month waiting period without mentioning the selves.

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r5.claim: Although anfus is a plural of paucity and quruʾ a plural of abundance, Arabic freely exchanges the two plural patterns, or quruʾ may simply be the more usual plural of qarʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r5.anchor: يتسعون في ذلك فيستعملون كل واحد من الجمعين مكان الآخر

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r6.claim: The number uses the masculine form thalāthata because quruʾ is grammatically masculine.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r6.anchor: لأنه أتبع تذكير اللفظ ولفظ القروء مذكر

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r7.claim: There is no dispute that qarʾ can name both menstruation and the period of purity between menstruations.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r7.anchor: ولا خلاف أن اسم القرء يقع على الحيض والطهر

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda calls al-aqrāʾ a word of opposite meanings; the better-known analysis treats it as genuinely applying to both, like shafaq for redness and whiteness.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الإقراء من الأضداد في كلام / العرب

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r9.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r9.claim: Some make menstruation the literal meaning and purity figurative; others reverse the relation.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون إنه حقيقة في الحيض ، مجاز في الطهر

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r10.speaker: قائلون
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r10.claim: Another group says the word has one underlying shared sense applicable to both menstruation and purity.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r10.anchor: وقال قائلون : إنه موضوع بحيثية معنى واحد مشترك

RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r11.speaker: الأصمعي والأخفش والفراء والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r11.claim: The first shared-sense explanation is gathering: blood gathers in the womb during menstruation and in the body during purity.
RAZI-FULL:v6p75/r11.anchor: وهو قول الأصمعي والأخفش والفراء والكسائي

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayd takes qurʾ as a transition from one state to another.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r1.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو قول أبي عبيد : أنه عبارة عن الانتقال من حالة إلى حالة

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ says qurʾ means a time or appointed period, such as the time when stars rise or set or winds blow; Hudhalī poetry witnesses this usage.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r2.anchor: والقول الثالث : وهو قول أبي عمرو بن العلاء : أن القرء هو الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r3.claim: If qurʾ means an appointed time, it can include either menstruation or purity, since each has its own defined time.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r3.anchor: وإذا ثبت أن القرء هو الوقت دخل فيه الحيض والطهر ، لأن لكل واحد منهما وقتا معينا

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r4.claim: Although the verse's surface could suggest any three units called qurūʾ, scholars agree a woman must count three of the same kind; they disagree whether these are purity periods or menstruations.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r4.anchor: والظاهر يقتضي أنها إذا اعتدت بثلاثة أشياء تسمى ثلاثة أقراء أن تخرج عن عهدة التكليف ، إلا أن العلماء أجمعوا على أنه لا يكفي ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī counts the three qurūʾ as periods of purity; Rāzī reports this also from Ibn ʿUmar, Zayd, ʿĀʾisha, the seven jurists, Mālik, Rabīʿa, and Aḥmad in one narration.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r5.anchor: فمذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنها الأطهار ، روى ذلك عن ابن عمر ، وزيد ، وعائشة

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r6.speaker: علي وعمر وابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r6.claim: ʿAlī, ʿUmar, and Ibn Masʿūd count the qurūʾ as menstruations; Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Thawrī, al-Awzāʿī, Ibn Abī Laylā, Ibn Shubruma, and Isḥāq share this position.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r6.anchor: وقال علي وعمر وابن مسعود هي الحيض ، وهو قول أبي حنيفة ، والثوري

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r7.claim: Counting purity makes the waiting period shorter: the remainder of purity after divorce counts and it ends when the third menstruation begins. In the Ḥanafī account, it ends only after the third menstruation if divorce was during purity, or the fourth if during menstruation; after maximum menstruation it ends before bathing, but after minimum menstruation only with bathing, dry ablution if water is absent, or the passing of a prayer time.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r7.anchor: فائدة الخلاف أن مدة العدة عند الشافعي أقصر ، وعندهم أطول

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r8.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r8.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues from 65:1 that divorce is for the time when the waiting period begins; since divorce during menstruation is forbidden, the waiting period begins in purity.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى : { النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن } ( الطلاق : 1 ) ومعناه في وقت عدتهن

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r9.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r9.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf explains 65:1 as meaning divorce them with their waiting period still in the future, as in saying there are three days left in a month.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r9.anchor: أجاب صاحب ( الكشاف ) عنه فقال بمعنى مستقبلات لعدتهن

RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r10.claim: Rāzī says the al-Kashshāf gloss strengthens al-Shāfiʿī: divorce can occur throughout purity, so the purity period beginning after divorce must count toward the waiting period.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76/r10.anchor: وأقول هذا الكلام يقوى استدلال الشافعي رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says that the qurūʾ are periods of purity.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r1.anchor: ما روي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت : هل تدرون الأقراء ؟ الأقراء الأطهار

RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī adds that women know this matter best because they experience it.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r2.anchor: ثم قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : والنساء بهذا أعلم ، لأن هذا إنما يبتلي به النساء

RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r3.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r3.claim: The gathering sense of qurʾ is supported by usage: a camel that has not gathered offspring, the womb gathering menstrual blood, a basin gathering water, stars gathering before setting, and the Qurʾān gathering letters, words, and sciences; ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's verse is also cited.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r3.anchor: يقال : ما قرأت الناقة نسلا قط ، أي ما جمعت في رحمها ولدا قط ومنه قول عمرو بن كلثوم

RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r4.claim: As a further argument for purity, Rāzī says menstrual blood does not collect in the womb but flows drop by drop; during purity it gathers in the body and accumulates toward its fullest state at the end, making the end of purity the complete qurʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r4.anchor: قلنا : الدماء لا تجتمع في الرحم ألبتة بل تنفصل قطرة قطرة أما وقت الطهر فالكل مجتمع في البدن

RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that no one should have power to detain another person's freedom without proof; therefore the shorter count of three purity periods is required, not the extra time added by counting menstruations.
RAZI-FULL:v6p76#2/r5.anchor: أن الأصل أن لا يكون لأحد على أحد من العقلاء المكلفين حق الحبس والمنع من التصرفات

RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that either purity or menstruation can be called qurʾ, but purity is the shorter count; a woman may not be required to wait through the excess time, so menstruation is not obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r1.anchor: وكل واحد من الطهر ومن الحيض يسمى بهذا الاسم ، فوجب أن تخرج المرأة عن العهدة بأيهما كان

RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r2.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues that although qurūʾ can lexically mean purity or menstruation, legal usage favors menstruation, citing the Prophet's instruction to stop praying during one's qurūʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r2.anchor: لما روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( دعي الصلاة أيام أقرائك )

RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r3.claim: The Ḥanafī argument says menstruation better fits three complete qurūʾ: counting purity can end the waiting period after only two full purities and part of a third.
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r3.anchor: أن القول بأن الأقراء حيض يمكن معه استيفاء ثلاثة أقراء بكمالها

RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī answers by analogy with the hajj months in 2:197, a plural counted as three although the hajj period includes only part of the third month.
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r4.anchor: أجاب الشافعي رضي الله عنه عن ذلك أن الله قال : { الحج أشهر معلومات } ( الحج : 197 )

RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r5.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilī al-Jubbāʾī rejects the analogy: the apparent count in 2:197 was left for evidence, while no such evidence permits leaving the apparent three here; unlike hajj months, the waiting period is continuous and must be completed.
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r5.anchor: أجاب الجبائي من شيوخ المعتزلة عن هذا الجواب من وجهين الأول : أنا تركنا الظاهر في تلك الآية لدليل

RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r6.speaker: المتأخرون من أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r6.claim: Rāzī's later colleagues answer that counting menstruations also creates a partial unit when divorce occurs during purity, but that excess is necessary because divorce during menstruation is forbidden; under the purity reading, the purity in which divorce occurs counts.
RAZI-FULL:v6p77/r6.anchor: وإجاب المتأخرون من أصحابنا عن هذه الحجة من وجهين الأول : كما أن حمل الأقراء على الأطهار يوجب النقصان

RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r1.claim: Rāzī replies that if qurʾ means gathering, the full gathering is reached at the end of purity, so counting purity does not make any qurʾ incomplete.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r1.anchor: بينا أن القرء اسم للاجتماع وكمال الاجتماع إنما يحصل في آخر الطهر قرءا تاما

RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r2.claim: The Ḥanafī side argues from 65:4: months replace menstruations for women without menses, and a substitute is counted in complete units; therefore the replaced qurūʾ must also be complete menstruations, not two purities and part of a third.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r2.anchor: فقال : { واللائى يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر } ( الطلاق : 4 )

RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says an enslaved woman's divorce is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstruations; since her waiting period is half that of a free woman, the argument infers that a free woman's qurūʾ are menstruations.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r3.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( طلاق الأمة تطليقتان ، وعدتها حيضتان )

RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r4.claim: The Ḥanafī argument cites consensus that a purchased enslaved woman is cleared for intercourse by one menstruation, then equates the purpose of that waiting with divorce iddah.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r4.anchor: أجمعنا على أن الاستبراء في شراء الجواري يكون بالحيضة ، فكذا العدة تكون بالحيضة

RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r5.claim: The Ḥanafī argument says the main purpose of iddah is to establish that the womb is clear, which menstruation establishes and purity does not.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r5.anchor: أن الغرض الأصلي في العدة استبراء الرحم ، والحيض هو الذي تستبرأ به الأرحام دون الطهر

RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r6.claim: The Ḥanafī position is presented as precaution: at the point when a new marriage would be permitted under the purity view, the menstruation view still forbids it; the argument gives priority to prohibition, the presumption that sexual relations are forbidden, and avoiding doubt.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r6.anchor: أن القول بأل القروء هي الحيض احتياط وتغليب لجانب الحرمة

RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r7.claim: The argument cites the Prophet's maxim that when lawful and forbidden considerations meet, the forbidden prevails, and his instruction to leave what causes doubt for what does not.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78/r7.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ما اجتمع الحرام والحلال إلا وغلب الحرام الحلال )

RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r1.claim: Rāzī concludes that the competing proofs weaken preference; for each person, God's ruling is what their own ijtihād leads them to.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r1.anchor: عند تعارض هذه الوجوه تضعف الترجيحات ، ويكون حكم الله في حق الكل ما أدى اجتهاده إليه

RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r2.claim: Because the end of iddah depends on menstruation or childbirth, facts men cannot directly know, the woman is trusted to report her status and her claim of ending iddah is accepted when the elapsed time permits it.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r2.anchor: جعلت المرأة أمينة في العدة ، وجعل القول قولها إذا ادعت انقضاء قرئها في مدة يمكن ذلك فيها

RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r3.claim: On al-Shāfiʿī's calculation, the shortest possible iddah is thirty-two days and one hour: a purity at divorce, a minimum one-day-and-night menses, fifteen days of purity, another minimum menses, fifteen days of purity, then renewed bleeding.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r3.anchor: وهو على مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه اثنان وثلاثون يوما وساعة

RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r4.claim: A pregnant woman who claims that she miscarried is likewise believed because she is treated as trustworthy in this matter.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r4.anchor: وكذلك إذا كانت حاملا فادعت أنها أسقطت كان القول قولها

RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r5.claim: One interpretation includes both pregnancy and menstruation: a woman might conceal pregnancy to shorten iddah, avoid the first husband's return, marry another, or have a child attributed to the later husband.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r5.anchor: الأول : أنه الحبل والحيض معا ، وذلك لأن المرأة لها أغراض كثيرة في كتمانهما

RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r6.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r6.claim: Under the same interpretation, a woman might conceal menstruation to lengthen iddah so her first husband returns, or shorten it to defeat his right of return, by hiding an early, third, or ongoing menses.
RAZI-FULL:v6p78#2/r6.anchor: وأما كتمان الحيض فغرضها فيه أن المرأة إذا طلقها الزوج وهي من ذوات الأقراء فقد تحب تطويل عدتها

RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r1.claim: A second interpretation restricts the concealed matter to pregnancy: it cites 3:6, says menstruation is outside rather than created in the womb, and considers a child nobler than menstrual blood; Rāzī rejects these reasons and includes all such hidden states because they change marriage's lawful status.
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r1.anchor: القول الثاني : أن المراد هو النهي عن كتمان الحمل فقط ، واحتجوا عليه بوجوه

RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r2.claim: Rāzī rejects restricting the phrase to pregnancy: its purpose is to forbid hiding private conditions that others cannot know and that alter whether marriage is lawful, so it covers them all.
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r2.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الوجوه ضعيفة ، لأنه لما كان المقصود منعها عن إخفاء هذه الأحوال

RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r3.claim: A third interpretation restricts the warning to menstruation because it follows mention of qurūʾ and pregnancy had not yet been mentioned; Rāzī rejects the restriction, reading the clause as independent and inclusive of all that is created in the womb.
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r3.anchor: القول الثالث : المراد هو النهي عن كتمان الحيض ، لأن هذه الآية وردت عقيب ذكر الإقراء

RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r4.claim: Rāzī says the clause is a self-contained statement rather than a continuation limited by the preceding mention of qurūʾ, and so it covers everything created in the womb.
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r4.anchor: لأن قوله : { ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله فى أرحامهن } كلام مستأنف مستقل بنفسه

RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r5.claim: The faith phrase is not a condition making the prohibition apply only to believers; like telling an oppressor that a believer should not oppress, it is a severe threat to women.
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r5.anchor: فليس المراد أن ذلك النهي مشروط بكونها مؤمنة ، بل هذا كما تقول للرجل الذي يظلم

RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r6.claim: Rāzī links the threat to 2:283: concealing testimony makes the heart sinful, and a person entrusted with something must return the trust and fear God; betraying entrusted responsibility is grave.
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r6.anchor: وهو كما قال في الشهادة { ومن يكتمها فإنه ءاثم قلبه } ( البقرة : 283 )

RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r7.claim: One analysis takes buʿūla as a plural of baʿl, like other collective plurals; the feminine ending reinforces the group's feminine form and is permitted only in established Arabic usage, not with every noun.
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r7.anchor: أنه جمع بعل ، كالفحولة والذكورة والجدودة والعمومة ، وهذه الهاء زائدة مؤكدة لتأنيث الجماعة

RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r8.claim: Baʿl can name either spouse: a woman may be called baʿla or zawja, while zawj is the more eloquent term; baʿl originally means master or owner, and was also the name of an idol taken as lord.
RAZI-FULL:v6p79/r8.anchor: واعلم أن اسم البعل مما يشترك فيه الزوجان فيقال للمرأة بعلة

RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r1.claim: A second analysis takes buʿūla as a verbal noun for becoming a husband; bāʿala can mean intercourse, and usage in reports about the days of tashrīq and good treatment of husbands supports reading the phrase as their husbands.
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r1.anchor: أن العبولة مصدر ، يقال : بعل الرجل يبعل بعولة ، إذا صار بعلا

RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r2.claim: Rāzī explains aḥaqq as the first husband's greater right during iddah: concealment could make a later marriage appear possible, or a woman's claim that iddah ended could give another man an apparent right.
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r2.anchor: فإذا فعلن ذلك كان الزوج الأول أحق بردهن ، وذلك لأنه ثبت للزوج الثاني حق في الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r3.claim: A second explanation is that the waiting woman has a right to end the marriage by letting iddah pass, while the husband's revocation can cancel that right, so he is called more entitled to take her back.
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r3.anchor: إذا كانت معتدة فلها في مضي العدة حق انقطاع النكاح فلما كان لهن هذا الحق

RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r4.claim: Radd means to return or restore; Rāzī cites the wording in 18:36 and a parallel expression using rajʿa.
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r4.anchor: يقال : رددته أي رجعته قال تعالى في موضع { ولئن رددت إلى ربى } ( الكهف : 36 )

RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r5.claim: Although a revocably divorced woman remains a wife during iddah, revocation is called a return because it ends the waiting and monitoring; on al-Shāfiʿī's view it also changes her from forbidden intimacy back to permissibility.
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r5.anchor: أن الرد والرجعة يتضمن إبطال التربص والتحري في العدة فهي ما دامت في العدة كأنه كانت جارية

RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r6.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that intimacy with a revocably divorced wife is forbidden until the husband formally revokes the divorce.
RAZI-FULL:v6p80/r6.anchor: ومذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه يحرم الاستمتاع بها إلا بعد الرجعة

RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r1.claim: Rāzī explains rajula through strength and power, with examples of a strong man, a horse able to walk, forceful speech without deliberation, and daylight growing bright; daraja means a rank or step on a road, from the image of life and travel unfolding stage by stage.
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r1.anchor: يقال : رجل بين الرجلة ، أي القوة ، وهو أرجل الرجلين أي أقواهما ، وفرس رجيل قوي على المشي

RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r2.claim: One reading of men's degree lists advantages in intellect, blood money, inheritance, leadership and legal roles, polygyny and concubinage, unilateral divorce and revocation, and a larger share of booty; Rāzī says these leave women vulnerable and make men more bound to fulfill their rights, since greater blessings make abuse more culpable.
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r2.anchor: أن الرجل أزيد في الفضيلة من النساء في أمور أحدها : العقل والثاني : في الدية والثالث : في المواريث

RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r3.claim: Rāzī cites the Prophet's instruction to treat women well, describing them as captives in men's care.
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r3.anchor: ولهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( استوصوا بالنساء خيرا فإنهن عندكم عوان )

RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r4.claim: Rāzī cites another report urging care for two vulnerable groups, the orphan and the woman.
RAZI-FULL:v6p81#2/r4.anchor: وفي خبر آخر : اتقوا الله في الضعيفين : اليتيم والمرأة

RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r1.claim: A second reading sees marital benefits as shared: marriage brings tranquility, affection, love, kinship, helpers and friends, and pleasure; Rāzī even allows that the woman's share may be greater.
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r1.anchor: أن يكون المراد حصول المنافع واللذة مشترك بين الجانبين ، لأن المقصود من الزوجية السكن والألفة والمودة

RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r2.claim: On this reading, the husband bears additional duties of dowry, maintenance, defense, meeting her needs, and protecting her from harm; the wife's duty of service is therefore stronger in recognition of his added obligations, as 4:34 says.
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r2.anchor: ثم إن الزوج اختص بأنواع من حقوق الزوجة ، وهي التزام المهر والنفقة ، والذب عنها

RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r3.claim: Rāzī cites the Prophet saying that, if he were to command prostration to anyone besides God, he would command a wife to prostrate to her husband.
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r3.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لو أمرت أحدا بالسجود لغير الله لأمرت المرأة بالسجود لزوجها )

RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r4.claim: God is invincible and cannot be prevented; His rulings and acts are sound and cannot involve purposelessness, folly, error, or falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v6p82/r4.anchor: أي غالب لا يمنع ، مصيب أحكامه وأفعاله ، لا يتطرق إليهما احتمال العبث والسفه والغلط والباطل
